en:
In 1719 miners draining a long-flooded shaft at Falun brought up the body of Mats Israelsson, missing for forty-two years and kept soft and whole by the vitriol water. His old fiancée Margaret Olsdotter recognised him, and only afterwards did the corpse harden to stone.

Falun grew up around the Great Copper Mountain, Stora Kopparberg, where farmers were digging copper around the year 1000. In 1347 King Magnus Eriksson granted the miners their privileges: shares were held according to the smelters a man owned and could be bought and sold, a joint-stock arrangement centuries older than the first shareholding banks, from which the Stora company descends. The mountain was worked by fire-setting. Great piles of timber were burned against the ore face through the night, and in the morning the cooled and shattered rock was prised loose with wedges and sledges, about a metre of advance in a month. Sulphur smoke from the open roasting hung over Falun for seven hundred years. In the seventeenth century this was Sweden's largest workplace, with about a thousand hands, and at its peak around 1650 it yielded over three thousand tonnes of copper in a year, at times two thirds of the world's supply. The Privy Council called it the kingdom's treasury and stronghold, and its metal paid for the armies of Sweden's age of greatness. The red sludge of the tailings, boiled with rye flour and linseed oil, became Falu red, the paint that made wooden cottages look like brick houses.

Half a millennium of workings had hollowed out the mountain, and at Midsummer 1687 the great pit fell in, leaving the Stora stoten, 95 metres deep and 1.6 kilometres around. It was a holiday and no one was underground. Linnaeus, visiting in 1734, called the mine one of Sweden's great wonders but as horrible as hell itself.
zh:
1719年，人们抽干法伦一条淹了多年的竖井，抬出矿工马茨·伊斯拉埃尔松的遗体：他失踪已四十二年，含硫酸盐的水把尸体保存得柔软完好。他当年的未婚妻玛格丽特·奥尔斯多特认出了他，之后尸体才慢慢硬得像石头。

法伦大铜矿旧称大铜山（Stora Kopparberg），法伦城是围绕它发展起来的。约公元1000年，农民已在山上采铜。1347年，马格努斯·埃里克松国王颁给矿工特许状：股份按各人拥有的冶炼炉分配，可以买卖，比最早的股份制银行早了好几个世纪，日后的斯道拉公司就是从这家矿场起家。矿上用火烧法取矿：整夜在矿脉前燃起大堆木材，早晨岩石冷却碎裂，再用楔子和大锤撬下，一个月大约掘进一米。矿石在露天焙烧，含硫的烟气在法伦上空飘了七百年。17世纪，这里是瑞典最大的工场，约有一千名矿工；1650年前后极盛，一年产铜逾三千吨，一度占到世界铜产量的三分之二。瑞典枢密院称它为王国的钱库和堡垒，瑞典称霸时代的连年征战，多靠这里的铜买单。矿渣堆里渗出的红色矿泥拌上黑麦粉和亚麻油熬煮，就成了「法伦红」颜料，瑞典的木屋纷纷刷上这种漆，好让自己看上去像砖墙宅邸。

五百年的巷道把整座山挖空。1687年仲夏节，大矿坑整体塌陷，形成深95米、周1.6公里的「大塌陷坑」；那天是节日，井下没有人。1734年林奈到访，说这座矿是瑞典的大奇观之一，却「和地狱本身一样可怕」。

en:
Kronborg stands on a sandspit at the narrowest neck of the Sound, where four kilometres of water separate Zealand from Scania and every Baltic ship had to pass. Eric of Pomerania's Krogen of the 1420s covered the line of the Sound Dues together with Kärnan on the Scanian shore. The toll was levied on the captain's own valuation of his cargo, and the king kept the right to buy the goods at that price, so a merchant who undervalued could lose his whole lading.

After the Northern Seven Years' War Frederick II rebuilt Krogen into the showpiece of his reign. Flemings directed the work, and the walls were faced with sandstone from Scania and roofed in copper. In 1577 the fortress took the name Kronborg. The Great Hall, one of the largest rooms in northern Europe, was hung with forty-three tapestries of the Danish kings made by Dutch weavers, fifteen of which survive. In 1590 James VI of Scotland, newly married to Anne of Denmark, lodged here and tipped the household two thousand gold dalers. On the night of 24 September 1629 two workmen's carelessness burned most of the castle; only the vaulted chapel escaped, and the interiors came back baroque and never as lavish. When Carl Gustaf Wrangel's Swedes took the castle in 1658 they carried off the courtyard fountain, the king's canopy woven with gold and silver thread, and the ceiling paintings of the hall.

Danish legend says that Holger Danske, the paladin of Charlemagne, sleeps in the casemates deep under the bastions until the day the country needs him again. Above him Kronborg was now a fortress first and a palace second. A crownwork was added, chained convicts laboured on the ramparts, and Queen Caroline Matilda, sister of George III, was held here for three months in 1772 after Struensee's fall.
zh:
克隆堡建在厄勒海峡最窄处的沙嘴上，西兰与斯科讷之间四公里宽的水面，是波罗的海每艘船的必经之门。波美拉尼亚的埃里克15世纪20年代修起的克罗根本垒，它和斯科讷岸上的克尔南塔一前一后，看住海峡税的税线。关税按船长自报的货物估值计征，国王保留照报价买下整船货的权利，所以低报货价的商人，可能赔上全部货物。

北方七年战争后，腓特烈二世把克罗根改建成他统治年代最得意的工程。主持工程的是佛兰德人。墙身贴上从斯科讷运来的砂岩，屋顶覆以铜皮，1577年要塞改名克隆堡，意为「王冠堡」。舞厅是北欧最大的厅堂之一，挂着荷兰织工织成的四十三幅历代丹麦国王挂毯，存世的只有十五幅。1590年，刚与丹麦的安妮成婚的苏格兰国王詹姆斯六世驻跸堡中，临走给堡内仆从打赏了两千达勒金币。1629年9月24日夜，两名工匠一时不慎，城堡大半焚于大火，只有拱顶坚固的礼拜堂幸免；内部重修成巴洛克样式，再没恢复旧日的奢华。1658年，卡尔·古斯塔夫·弗兰格尔的瑞典军攻陷城堡，掠走庭院喷泉、那顶以金线银线织成的国王华盖，还有舞厅的天顶画。

丹麦传说说，查理曼的圣骑士霍尔格（Holger Danske）就在棱堡深处的地窖里沉睡，直到国家再需要他的那一天。在他头顶上，克隆堡此后先是要塞，其次才是宫殿：增建了「王冠工事」，戴镣铐的苦役在棱堡上服刑，英王乔治三世的妹妹、王后卡罗琳·玛蒂尔达1772年施特林泽倒台后在此被关押三个月。

en:
The merchants of Visby walled their town in limestone: a ring 3.4 kilometres long, six metres high on the landward side, with a covered archer's walk and slits for arrows, and in the end twenty-nine large towers and twenty-two small ones. The oldest stone is the squat Kruttornet at the harbour mouth, raised in the 1100s and the oldest surviving secular building in the Nordic countries; a sea wall ran from it to a second tower around 1250. The land wall followed in the 1270s and 1280s, and it answered a quarrel between the merchants and the Gotland country assembly that blew into civil war in 1288. In medieval Sweden only Visby, Stockholm and Kalmar had city walls. The wall was raised another three or four metres in the 1350s and given its saddle towers.

At the seaward Maiden Tower they told of a goldsmith's daughter walled up alive for opening the town to the Danes, though the tower itself is a century newer than the story. Within the ring the Hanse Germans built for the centuries: their church of St Mary, the Franciscans' St Karin's, stone warehouses and stepped gable houses along the quayside street Strandgatan. When Valdemar Atterdag entered in 1361 he had a stretch of wall pulled down as a token of submission, and it was sealed again two years later. Lübeck's troops stormed the wall in 1525 and the churches burned or were closed. In 1533-34 the governor Henrik Nielsen Rosenkrantz demolished St John's and St Peter's to clear a field of fire for Visborg castle, leaving St Mary's the only roof among a circle of church ruins. Caponiers for muskets were added in the 1600s, and afterwards the wall earned its keep as a toll barrier; when the inland tolls were abolished in 1810 it was already an antiquity no one cared to pull down.
zh:
维斯比城的商人用石灰岩把全城围了起来：城墙周长三千四百米，临陆一侧高六米，墙内有遮蔽的弓箭手通道，墙上开着箭缝，全盛时共有29座大塔、22座小塔。最古老的石头在港口：矮壮的火药塔建于12世纪，是北欧现存最古老的世俗建筑；约1250年，一道海墙从它延伸到另一座塔楼。陆地城墙筑于13世纪70至80年代，筑城是为了对付商人与哥得兰乡庭的冲突，双方在1288年大打内战。整个中世纪的瑞典，只有维斯比、斯德哥尔摩和卡尔马三座城市拥有城墙。14世纪50年代，城墙又加高三四米，并增设骑墙的小塔。

朝海的少女塔流传着一个故事：金匠的女儿给丹麦人开城，被活活砌进墙里，不过这座塔本身比故事晚了一百年。石环之内，汉萨的德意志人为百年之计而营建：他们自己的圣马利亚教堂，方济各会修士的圣卡琳教堂，以及沿滨海街挤成一排的石砌货栈和山墙带台阶的房屋。1361年瓦尔德马四世入城时，下令拆去一段城墙作为降服的象征，两年后这段墙又被补好。1525年吕贝克军队攻破城墙，各教堂或焚毁或关闭；1533至1534年，总督亨里克·尼尔森·罗森克兰茨又拆掉圣约翰和圣彼得两座教堂，为维斯堡扫清射界，一圈教堂废墟中只剩圣马利亚还有屋顶。17世纪，墙下添了供火枪侧射的暗堡；此后城墙靠当关卡收税维持，1810年国内关税废除时，它已是没人舍得拆的古迹。

en:
In 1745 thirty cats were fetched from Kazan to hunt mice in the half-finished Winter Palace, the first cats kept there. The palace on the Neva embankment is the fifth winter residence of that name. Peter the Great started with a small wooden winter house and the stone Wedding Chambers, Governor Menshikov's gift for his marriage to Catherine; Georg Mattarnovi then built a larger palace beside the Winter Canal, where Peter died. Empress Anna Ioannovna found it cramped and set Bartolomeo Rastrelli to rebuild it from 1732, giving herself some seventy state halls, more than a hundred bedrooms, a theatre and a chapel. Elizabeth was no fonder of it: on 1 January 1752 she ordered a new one. Rastrelli's baroque block is 215 metres long and thirty high, with about 1,500 rooms, 1,945 windows and 117 staircases. Elizabeth died before it was finished, Peter III took delivery in April 1762 and was overthrown that summer, and Catherine II completed the building and dismissed Rastrelli.

Catherine filled the palace with pictures. In 1764 a Berlin merchant's debt to a Russian prince was settled with some three hundred paintings, mostly Dutch and Flemish, which were hung in the empress's private apartments. She called the rooms her Hermitage, her place of solitude, and a separate Little Hermitage was built beside the palace a few years later. She gave the chambers directly below her own to Grigory Orlov, reached by a private gallery. Around two thousand people lived in the palace in those years, and anyone respectably dressed could walk in and look around, even through the Diamond Room in the imperial apartments. Foreign envoys followed a fixed route on audience days, up the Jordan Staircase and through the enfilade of state halls overlooking the Neva, and Giacomo Quarenghi's new Great Throne Hall opened in 1795.
zh:
1745年，为捕捉半成品冬宫里的老鼠，人们从喀山弄来三十只猫，这是宫里养的第一批猫。涅瓦河畔的这座宫殿是同名的第五座冬季宅邸。彼得大帝先住小小的木制冬屋和石造婚礼宫，后者是总督缅什科夫送给他和叶卡捷琳娜的成婚礼物；后来格奥尔格·马塔尔诺维在冬宫运河边建起更大的宫殿，彼得就在这里去世。安娜·伊凡诺夫娜女皇嫌它狭小，1732年起命巴托洛梅奥·拉斯特雷利重建，给自己安排了约七十座典礼大厅、一百多间卧室，还有剧院和礼拜堂。伊丽莎白同样看不上它：1752年1月1日她下令另建新宫。拉斯特雷利设计的巴洛克大厦立面长215米、高30米，里面约有1500个房间、近两千扇窗和117座楼梯。伊丽莎白没能等到竣工；彼得三世1762年4月接过宫殿，当年夏天就被推翻，最后由叶卡捷琳娜二世把工程收尾，并辞退了拉斯特雷利。

叶卡捷琳娜把宫殿变成了藏画之所。1764年，一位柏林商人欠俄国亲王的债以约三百幅画抵偿，大半是荷兰和佛兰德斯画派，这些画挂进女皇的私室。她把这几个房间称作自己的艾尔米塔什，即退隐独居之处，几年后宫殿旁又建起一座独立的小艾尔米塔什。她把自己楼下的房间拨给格里戈里·奥尔洛夫，以一道私廊相通。那些年宫里常住约两千人，凡衣着体面者都可入内参观，连皇家寝宫的钻石厅也照开不误。外国使节觐见时有固定路线：先登约旦阶梯，再穿过一溜面朝涅瓦河的典礼大厅；贾科莫·夸伦吉修建的新大宝座厅1795年启用。

en:
Above twelve Doric columns of the Brandenburg Gate a goddess of victory drives four horses of beaten copper toward the city. The gate replaced a baroque customs gate on the old road from Berlin west to Brandenburg an der Havel, pulled down in 1788 for something grander. Frederick William II wanted his capital to rival Vienna and Paris, and his architect Carl Gotthard Langhans took the Propylaea of the Athenian Acropolis for his model, working from measured engravings because he had never seen Greece. Raised in Elbe sandstone, with five passages between the columns, it was Prussia's first great building in the Greek style. Johann Gottfried Schadow directed the sculpture: the metopes repeat the Parthenon's fight of centaurs and Lapiths, and reliefs in the passages show the labours of Hercules, read as the deeds of Frederick the Great. The gate opened to traffic in 1791 as the Peace Gate, for Prussia's intervention in Holland.

The quadriga was Schadow's too, hammered out by the city's coppersmiths, and the king refused to have it gilded. After Jena and Auerstedt Napoleon rode in through the gate on 27 October 1806 and had the group taken down that December. Packed in twelve crates, it went by water through Hamburg to Paris, where it was restored in the Louvre but never mounted on the Porte Saint-Denis as Napoleon had intended. For seven years Berliners saw only the bare iron mounting spike above the columns, and felt it as a deeper insult than the empty roof. In 1814 Blücher's men found the crates in Paris and sent them home. On 7 August Frederick William III rode through the gate at the head of his troops as the wrappings fell from the restored chariot, and the city nicknamed the returned goddess the Retourkutsche, 'return carriage', Berlin slang for a sharp reply. Karl Friedrich Schinkel then gave Victoria a new oak wreath around the Iron Cross, with the crowned Prussian eagle above it.
zh:
勃兰登堡门的十二根多立克柱上方，一位胜利女神驾着四匹锻铜的骏马朝向城内。大门取代了柏林城西、通往哈弗尔河畔勃兰登堡的大道上一座巴洛克式税关城门，旧门1788年拆除，让位给更宏大的建筑。腓特烈·威廉二世要让柏林与维也纳、巴黎比肩，王室建筑师卡尔·戈特哈德·朗汉斯以雅典卫城的山门为范本，他本人没有去过希腊，依据的是测绘版画。大门用易北砂岩建成，柱间五条通道，是普鲁士第一座希腊风格的宏大建筑。约翰·戈特弗里德·沙多主持全部雕塑：檐壁上的排档间饰模仿帕特农神庙上半人马与拉庇泰人的战斗，通道里的浮雕表现赫拉克勒斯的功绩，被读作腓特烈大王功业的隐喻。1791年大门开放通行，定名「和平门」，纪念普鲁士出兵荷兰。

门顶的四马战车同样出自沙多之手，由城里的铜匠锻成，国王没有采纳鎏金的建议。耶拿和奥尔施泰特战败后，拿破仑1806年10月27日穿过勃兰登堡门进入柏林，同年12月下令拆下战车。战车分装十二箱，经汉堡走水路运往巴黎，在卢浮宫修复，最终没有按拿破仑的打算安到圣但尼门上。此后七年，柏林人只能看见柱顶竖着一根光秃秃的安装铁桩，比起门顶空空，这根「尖刺」更让他们觉得屈辱。1814年，布吕歇尔的部下在巴黎找到那些箱子，运回柏林。8月7日，腓特烈·威廉三世率军穿过大门，修复的战车同时揭幕，柏林人把归来的女神戏称为「回敬马车」（Retourkutsche），在柏林土话里这个词也指顶嘴还击。申克尔随后为维多利亚重制了标志：新的橡叶环环抱着铁十字，上方立着戴王冠的普鲁士雄鹰。

en:
Ambras Castle began as a present for a wife whom the archduke had married in secret. Ferdinand II, second son of Emperor Ferdinand I, had married Philippine Welser, an Augsburg merchant's daughter, in secret, and when he received the Tyrol in 1564 he set two Italian architects to turn the old fortress on the hill above Innsbruck into a Renaissance residence for her. The tenth-century castle of the Counts of Andechs had been destroyed in 1133 and nothing of it survives. Philippine was a commoner, and the valley loved her: even nobles addressed their petitions to her as 'Merciful Miss', and the Tyrolese mourned her when she died in 1580.

Ferdinand was one of the great collectors of his age, and he built the Lower Castle to hold his collections. The Chamber of Art and Curiosities is the only Renaissance Kunstkammer that has never left its original rooms, and coral growths, clocks, medals, automata and oddities of nature still stand together in it. In 1589 he added a hall for his 'heroes', the armour and portraits of famous commanders, the first systematic display of its kind in the history of museums. Under the family apartments lies the Spanish Hall, with an inlaid wooden ceiling and twenty-seven full-length portraits of the rulers of Tyrol. The Upper Castle is hung with Habsburg portraits, among them many of the dynasty's children.

After Ferdinand's death his son Charles, Margrave of Burgau, let castle and collections decay, and in 1606 he sold them to Emperor Rudolf II, a tireless collector himself, who left his uncle's treasures where they were. Later emperors cared less, and Leopold I moved the rarest books and manuscripts to Vienna. In 1805, with Austria beaten by France, Napoleon looked through the inventories, recognised the collection as Habsburg private property and had it carried to safety in Vienna.
zh:
阿姆布拉斯宫起初是献给一位秘密妻子的礼物。斐迪南二世大公是皇帝斐迪南一世的次子，他秘密娶了奥格斯堡商人的女儿菲利皮内·韦尔泽；1564年领有蒂罗尔之后，他命两名意大利建筑师把因斯布鲁克上方山头的旧堡垒改建成文艺复兴式府邸，给她居住。10世纪安德克斯伯爵的老城堡早在1133年就已被毁，一点痕迹也没留下。菲利皮内是平民出身，谷地里的人却爱戴她：连贵族递请愿书也称她「仁慈的小姐」，1580年她去世时蒂罗尔人为她服丧。

斐迪南是那个时代首屈一指的收藏家，他专门修了下堡来存放藏品。艺术与奇珍室是唯一没有离开过原室的文艺复兴奇珍柜，珊瑚、钟表、徽章、自动机械和各种自然异物仍并陈一室。1589年他又加建一座陈列「英雄」的厅馆，收着历代名将的甲胄和肖像，是博物馆史上第一次这样系统的陈列。宅邸下方是西班牙厅，木嵌天顶之下排着27幅蒂罗尔统治者的等身肖像；上堡挂满哈布斯堡家族的肖像，其中有不少是王朝子孙年幼时的模样。

斐迪南死后，儿子布尔高藩侯卡尔任由宫殿和藏品败落，1606年把它们卖给皇帝鲁道夫二世。鲁道夫自己就是孜孜不倦的收藏家，仍把叔父的珍藏留在原处。后来的皇帝不太上心，利奥波德一世把最珍稀的书籍和手稿迁到维也纳。1805年奥地利败给法国，拿破仑翻看清单，认定这批藏品是哈布斯堡的私产，下令把它全部安全运抵维也纳。

en:
For four hundred years a wooden crane stood on the stump of Cologne Cathedral's south tower, and the city joked that the world would end on the day the Dom was finished. The church was conceived as a giant stone reliquary. The bones of the Three Kings made Cologne one of the great pilgrimage goals of the Middle Ages, so the chapter planned a French High Gothic minster on the scale of Amiens, to rise above every Romanesque church in the city. Archbishop Konrad von Hochstaden laid the first stone on 15 August 1248, with trachyte from the Drachenfels for the walls. Master Gerhard, who planned the chevet of seven chapels, is said to have died after a mysterious fall from his scaffolding. His successors raised the choir and consecrated it in 1322. Its 104 stalls, the largest set in Germany, kept one seat for the emperor and one for the pope, and forty-eight painted kings look down from the upper windows. When the Reformation dried up the pilgrim and indulgence money, the masons' lodge closed around 1560.

For nearly three centuries the Dom remained a torso: a finished choir walled off from a half-height nave under an emergency roof, with the crane, more than twenty-five metres high, the best-known mark on the skyline. French troops entered in October 1794 and used the church as a stable and storehouse, while the chapter smuggled the shrine of the Three Kings away to Westphalia. Then the Romantics made completion their cause. Joseph Görres called the building a national shrine in 1814, and Sulpiz Boisserée, a Cologne art dealer who had been surveying the fabric, found the lost facade plan of about 1370 in Darmstadt and Paris in the following years. In 1821 the pope restored the Dom as a cathedral, the Prussian state took on its building costs, and Boisserée published the first engravings of a finished church. The crane stayed on the stump.
zh:
科隆大教堂南塔的残顶上，一架木起重机站了四百年，科隆人开玩笑说，大教堂完工之日就是世界终结之时。这座教堂从设计之初就是一具巨大的石造圣物匣。三王圣骸使科隆成为中世纪最主要的朝圣地之一，教士团于是决定以亚眠的尺度修建一座法国盛哥特式教堂，高过城里所有罗马式教堂。1248年8月15日，大主教康拉德·冯·霍赫施塔登放下第一块基石，墙体用德拉亨费尔斯山的粗面岩砌成。设计了七座小堂环绕的东端圣坛的格哈德师傅，据说是从脚手架上神秘坠落身亡的。继任者们砌起唱诗班席，1322年祝圣启用。席位一百零四个，是德国最大的一组，其中一个留给皇帝，一个留给教宗；高窗上绘着四十八位国王。宗教改革使朝圣和赎罪券的进项枯竭，约1560年，石匠作坊关闭。

此后近三百年，大教堂一直是副未完成的躯干：完工的唱诗班席被一道墙与只砌到一半高、盖着应急屋顶的中殿隔开，高逾二十五米的起重机是科隆天际线最出名的标记。1794年10月法军进入科隆，教堂一度被当作马厩和仓库，教士团则把三王金盒秘密送往威斯特伐利亚。后来浪漫派把续建当成事业：戈雷斯1814年称它为民族圣地，科隆艺术品商人苏尔皮茨·布瓦塞雷（Sulpiz Boisserée）一直在测绘建筑，随后几年在达姆施塔特和巴黎找回了约1370年的立面设计图。1821年，教宗下诏恢复它的主教座堂地位，普鲁士国家承担起建筑费用，布瓦塞雷出版了设想中教堂完工样貌的第一批铜版画。南塔上的起重机没有撤下。

en:
The Amsterdam bourse opened for just one hour a day, from eleven to twelve, so that every goods broker had to be on the floor at the same time; for years it was the only place in the city where business might legally be done. Before the Koopmansbeurs, the Merchants' Exchange, opened in 1611, merchants struck their bargains in the open air on the Nieuwe Brug by the IJ and in bad weather crowded into the Jerusalem Chapel or a church. In April 1607 the town council voted a bourse 'for the convenience of the merchants', and Hendrick de Keyser, the city's master sculptor, sailed to London with the master mason Cornelis Danckertsz de Rij to study the Royal Exchange. The building went up across the Rokin just south of the Dam, resting partly on the vaults of a sluice and partly on piles fifty to sixty feet long.

Most deals were in commodities, but the floor also traded shares in the East India Company and, from 1621, the West India Company, plus forward contracts, insurance and shipping deals, along with news from distant markets. A later bylaw even barred brokers from lingering near the building or the Dam after hours. In 1688 Joseph de la Vega, a Portuguese Jewish merchant of the city, published Confusion de Confusiones, the first full-length book about a stock exchange and the people who traded on one.

A legend attached itself to the early bourse. In 1622 Balthasar Paul, a stonemason's journeyman from Namur, plotted to burn Amsterdam down, the bourse included, and died on the scaffold on the Dam; in the telling, an orphan boy found a ship loaded with gunpowder under the bridge and beat his drum, after which the orphan boys were allowed to drum through the town at fair time. In 1668 the city architect Daniël Stalpaert extended the courtyard from twelve arches to seventeen and set a Mercury over the new Rokin front.
name_zh: 阿姆斯特丹证券交易所
zh:
阿姆斯特丹证券交易所每天只开一小时，从十一点到十二点，好让所有货物经纪人同一时间都在场内；有很长一段时间，全城只准在这里做生意。1611年商人交易所落成以前，商人们在艾湾畔的新桥露天议价，遇上坏天气就挤进耶路撒冷礼拜堂或借教堂落脚。1607年4月，市议会决定「为商人之便」修建交易所，当年春天，城市雕刻师傅亨德里克·德·凯泽（Hendrick de Keyser）随泥瓦师傅科内利斯·丹克茨·德赖赴伦敦考察皇家交易所。大楼建在水坝广场南侧，横跨罗金（Rokin），一半架在水闸的拱顶之上，一半立在五六十英尺长的木桩上。

场内成交以货物为主，但也买卖东印度公司股票，1621年起又加上西印度公司股票，另有远期合同、保险和货运合约，远方市场的消息也在此汇集。后来的法令甚至禁止经纪人事后在交易所和水坝广场附近逗留。1688年，城里的葡萄牙犹太商人约瑟夫·德拉维加（Joseph de la Vega）出版《Confusion de Confusiones》（意为「混乱中的混乱」），这是第一部完整讲述证券交易所和场内交易者的书。

交易所早年还附着一桩传说：1622年，那慕尔来的石匠帮工巴尔塔扎·保罗密谋纵火烧掉阿姆斯特丹，交易所也在目标之列，事败后在水坝广场被处死；故事后来讲成一个孤儿院男孩发现桥下停着满载火药的船，击鼓报警，此后孤儿院的男孩获准在集市期间穿城击鼓。1668年，城市建筑师丹尼尔·斯塔尔帕特（Daniël Stalpaert）主持扩建，庭院拱廊从十二拱加长到十七拱，罗金一侧的新门面上立起墨丘利神像。

en:
Legend says that after the St Elizabeth's flood a cradle was found floating with a baby asleep inside, kept dry and level by a cat leaping back and forth along its edge; the dike where it came ashore, the story runs, gave Kinderdijk its name. The flood itself was real. On the night of 18-19 November 1421 a storm burst the dikes of the Grote Waard, villages vanished and between 2,000 and 10,000 people drowned.

The polders are land taken from the water and kept dry by dikes, sluices and mills. From the eleventh century monks and settlers banked off the silted marshes of Holland, and as the peat soil sank beneath the sea the dikes grew with it. The first official water boards, Rijnland, Schieland and Delfland, were set up in the thirteenth century, and by 1444 Holland was a country of dike rings and wind pumps, its water boards older than most of its towns.

Draining inland lakes began with experiments. The Achtermeer, a 35-hectare lake south of Alkmaar, was pumped dry in 1533 under a county patent, the first droogmakerij, a polder made from a lake bed. Investors then took on the Beemster, a wide lake open to the Zuiderzee, from 1608. When a sea dike broke the water poured back, so the ring dike was raised a full metre above the surrounding country, and by 1612 the lake bed stood dry, cut into a strict grid of parallel canals and roads and divided among the shareholders. Its farms grew provisions for the ships of the East India Company. More lakes followed, the Purmer, the Wormer, the Watergraafsmeer on Amsterdam's doorstep and the Schermer, until in 1635 the last of them fell dry and the great lakes of North Holland had become farmland, every field lying below the water that the mills kept pumping out.
zh:
相传圣伊丽莎白洪水之后，有人看见一只摇篮漂在水上，一个婴儿在里面安睡，一只猫在摇篮边沿来回跳跃，使它保持平稳、不致进水；摇篮靠岸的那段堤，据说便得名小孩堤防（Kinderdijk）。洪水本身确有其事：1421年11月18日至19日夜间，风暴冲决大堤瓦尔德的堤坝，整座整座的村庄消失，溺死者两千至一万人。

荷兰圩田是从水里夺来、靠堤坝、水闸和风车保住的土地。从十一世纪起，修士和移民把荷兰淤积的沼泽围堤开垦，泥炭土在海平面之下不断沉陷，堤坝也就一层层加高。最早的官办水利机构赖恩兰、斯希兰和代尔夫特水利委员会都设立于十三世纪；到1444年，荷兰已是堤围与排水风车之地，水利委员会比大多数城镇还要古老。

排干内陆湖泊从试验开始：1533年，凭伯爵颁给的特许，阿尔克马尔以南三十五公顷的阿赫特梅尔湖被抽干，成为第一块湖底圩田（droogmakerij）。投资者随后从1608年起向贝姆斯特这片与须得海相通的大湖动手。海堤溃决时湖水倒灌，人们便把环形围堤加高到比周围地面整整高出一米，1612年湖底终于干涸，土地按严格的网格划分，水道与道路平行延伸，分给入股的投资人。圩田上的农场为东印度公司的船只供应给养。皮尔默湖、沃尔默湖、阿姆斯特丹近郊的瓦特赫拉夫斯米尔湖和斯海尔默湖相继排干，到1635年最后一座湖干涸，北荷兰的大湖已变成农田，每一块田都低于水面，全靠风车不停抽水。

en:
Above the roof of the Duomo rises a marble forest of 135 spires and pinnacles, with saints standing on every ledge and crest. It occupies the forum of Roman Mediolanum, where two older cathedrals had stood, and was begun in 1386 by Archbishop Antonio da Saluzzo. His cousin Gian Galeazzo Visconti soon took the works in hand, meaning to give his new duchy a church in the latest Gothic, and gave the Fabbrica del Duomo, the permanent building office, exclusive rights to the marble of Candoglia; every block was marked for the works and passed toll-free.

Foreign masters were called in to judge the rising piers. The Parisian Jean Mignot pronounced the work 'in peril of ruin', built 'without science'; the walls stood, but the insult drove the masons to improve their tools. In 1488 Leonardo and Bramante both entered models for the cupola, and Leonardo withdrew. Archbishop Carlo Borromeo cleared the lay tombs from the nave and consecrated the church in 1577. Marco d'Agrate's Saint Bartholomew Flayed shows the saint carrying his own skin over one shoulder. High in the apse a red lamp marks a nail said to come from the True Cross, lowered once a year on a cloud-shaped lift, the Nivola. In 1762 the Madonnina spire reached 108.5 metres, carrying Giuseppe Perego's gilded Madonna; in Milan's fog, a day when she could be seen from the city counted as clear weather.

The facade was the great unfinished argument, and Renaissance, Gothic and Baroque schemes stayed on paper for centuries. Crowned King of Italy at the Duomo with the Iron Crown in 1805, Napoleon ordered it finished at French expense; the money was never paid, but Carlo Amati completed the facade by 1813, and a statue of Napoleon was set on one of the spires. Behind it opens one of the largest church interiors in Christendom, five naves on 40 pillars under vaults about 45 metres high, the highest Gothic vaults of a completed church.
zh:
米兰主教座堂的屋顶上方，135座尖塔和小尖顶组成一片大理石的森林，每一层台沿和冠饰上都立着圣徒像。它占着古罗马梅迪奥拉努姆广场的位置，那里原本立着两座老主教座堂，1386年由大主教安东尼奥·达·萨卢佐动工。他的表弟吉安·加莱亚佐·维斯孔蒂很快接管工程，要给自己的新公国造一座追上最新样式的哥特教堂，并把坎多利亚大理石矿的独占权拨给常设的大教堂工程局，每块供料都烙上工程专用的印记、免缴一切通行税。

工地请来外地匠师评判正在升高的巨墩。巴黎人让·米尼奥断言工程「有坍塌之险」、做法「不合科学」；墙没有塌，这番羞辱却逼着工匠改良工具和技法。1488年，列奥纳多·达·芬奇和伯拉孟特各自为中央穹顶制作模型参选，列奥纳多退出。大主教卡洛·博罗梅奥把俗人陵墓清出中殿，1577年为整座教堂祝圣。堂内立着马尔科·德·阿格拉泰所作《剥皮的圣巴多禄茂》，圣人把自己的皮搭在肩上；后殿高处一盏红灯标记着相传取自十字架的圣钉，每年一次，圣钉乘一架叫「尼沃拉」的云形升降具降到信众面前。1762年，马东尼纳尖塔升到108.5米高，顶着朱塞佩·佩雷戈塑的镀金圣母；米兰多雾，城里能望见她的日子就算晴天。

立面是争论最久的难题，文艺复兴式、哥特式和巴洛克式的方案一代代停在纸上。1805年，拿破仑在米兰主教座堂戴上铁王冠加冕为意大利国王，下令由法国国库出资完成立面；钱从未拨付，卡洛·阿马蒂却在1813年把立面建成，一座尖顶上还安放了拿破仑的雕像。立面之后是基督教世界最大的教堂室内之一：五廊、40根巨柱、约45米高的拱顶，那是已建成教堂里最高的哥特拱顶。

en:
Along the frieze of the Great Council hall the doges pass in portrait, all except Marino Faliero, who attempted a coup in 1355 and is represented by a black cloth. The Doge's Palace was the doge's house and the republican government in one building: apartments, council halls, law courts and prisons all looked onto the same courtyards. The palace of 1444 was the Gothic structure raised from about 1340 on the lagoon side, two storeys of arcading patterned in pale Istrian stone and pink Verona marble. Its ceremonial entrance, the Porta della Carta, is crowned by Justice with sword and scales and a doge kneeling to the lion of Saint Mark. After a fire in 1483 Antonio Rizzo rebuilt the doge's wing in the new Renaissance manner and laid out the Giants' Staircase, where new doges were afterwards crowned beneath Sansovino's colossal Mars and Neptune.

The patricians of the Great Council, who governed the republic, met in the hall above. In December 1577 fire destroyed the council chamber itself, with paintings by Bellini, Titian and Carpaccio. The senate rebuilt the shell in the old Gothic despite a classical scheme from Palladio, and Tintoretto and his workshop covered the new wall with Paradise, a canvas said to be the widest in the world.

Justice had its darker quarters in the same building. The damp, windowless ground-floor cells were called the Wells, and more cells under the lead roof were called the Leads. Giacomo Casanova later told how he broke out of the Leads through the roof, crossed the palace and left by the Porta della Carta. Soon after 1600 a covered bridge joined the law courts to the New Prisons across the canal; prisoners crossing it caught a last open glimpse of the lagoon and San Giorgio, and later travellers named it the Bridge of Sighs. When the republic fell in 1797 the French smashed the medieval group over the Porta della Carta, Doge Foscari kneeling before the lion of Saint Mark.
zh:
大议会厅的檐壁上，历代总督的肖像依次排开，唯独1355年谋反的马里诺·法列罗那里只挂一幅黑布。总督宫是总督宅邸，也是共和国政府的驻地：住所、议事厅、法庭和监狱都开向同一组庭院。1444年眼前这座是约1340年起在潟湖一侧建起的哥特式宫殿，两层拱廊用白色伊斯特拉石和粉色维罗纳大理石相间砌成。礼仪大门「纸门」门顶立着手持剑与天平的正义女神，还有向圣马可之狮跪拜的总督。1483年的大火之后，安东尼奥·里佐按新兴的文艺复兴样式重建了总督住所一翼，并修造巨人阶梯；后来的新总督都在梯上加冕，梯顶立着圣索维诺雕的巨大战神与海神。

大议会的贵族执掌共和国，在楼上大厅议政。1577年12月，一场大火吞噬了大议会厅本身，贝利尼、提香和卡尔帕乔的画作同归于尽。元老院拒绝帕拉第奥的古典式方案，按旧哥特样式重建外壳，丁托列托和作坊在新墙上画出《天堂》，据说那是世界上最宽的画布。

司法在这座建筑里还有更阴暗的角落。底层潮湿无窗的牢房叫「井狱」，铅皮屋顶下的牢房称「铅狱」。贾科莫·卡萨诺瓦后来讲述自己如何钻出屋顶逃出铅狱，穿过总督宫，从纸门离去。1600年后不久，一座封闭廊桥跨运河把法庭和新监狱连起来；过桥的囚徒最后一次望见潟湖和圣乔治马焦雷，后来的旅行者便为它取名叹息桥。1797年共和国灭亡，法军砸毁纸门上的中世纪群雕：福斯卡里总督跪在圣马可之狮前的那一座。

en:
Dante used the Venetian word arzanà in the Inferno: the pitch boiling in the fifth pit of hell is compared to the pitch the Venetians boiled in winter to caulk their damaged ships. The word came from the Arabic dar al-sina'a, house of craft. The state dockyard in the Castello district, traditionally founded in 1104, grew into the largest industrial site in pre-industrial Europe, about 45 hectares behind a two-mile rampart, fifteen per cent of the city. Its basins let the state build and repair its whole navy and largest merchantmen; shipwrights built hulls frame-first, and a canal moved each hull past the workshops, with up to a hundred galleys on the stocks at different stages. Oak came from the state forest at Montello, and the rope-walks spun hemp from the Don and the Sea of Azov. The yard made guns as well, from bombards to light field artillery on mobile carriages.

Before its land gate, modelled on a Roman arch at Venetian-ruled Pula, four ancient stone lions were set in 1687, Greek spoils. The largest, the Piraeus Lion, carries runic graffiti on its flanks, probably cut by Scandinavian mercenaries in the eleventh century. In 1593 Galileo became the yard's consultant on ballistics, oars and timber; the shipwrights' problems fed his later book on the strength of materials. The doge's ceremonial barge, the bucentaur, was built and berthed here too; every Ascension Day it carried the doge out to drop a ring in the Adriatic, wedding Venice to the sea. The last and largest, launched in 1729, ran to 35 metres and needed 168 oarsmen.

Even in decline the yard kept its reputation: when Peter of Russia built galleys for the Sea of Azov he called in Venetian shipwrights. When the republic collapsed in 1797 the French broke up unfinished hulls and sent more than 5,000 captured artillery pieces to Toulon. The bucentaur was taken to pieces and burned in 1798 to strip the gold from its carving.
zh:
但丁在《神曲·地狱篇》里用了威尼斯方言词arzanà（军械库）：地狱第五恶囊里沸腾的沥青，被他比作威尼斯人冬天熬来修补漏水船只的沥青。这个词来自阿拉伯语「工匠之家」。城堡区的国家船坞传统上认为建于1104年，最终成为工业革命以前欧洲最大的工业区，占地约45公顷，环着3公里长的围墙，约占全城面积的15%。国家的整支舰队和最大的商船都在它的船坞里建造和维修；船匠采用先立骨架的造法，一条渠道把船身依次送过各作场，同时常有多达一百艘桨帆船处在不同的建造阶段。橡木取自国家在蒙泰洛的专属森林，绳索工场纺制的麻来自顿河口和亚速海。军械库也铸炮，从射石炮到装在轻便炮架上的野战火炮都有。

威尼斯军械库的陆地正门仿照威尼斯治下普拉的一座古罗马凯旋门，1687年门前安放了四尊古代石狮，都是从希腊带回的战利品。最大的「比雷埃夫斯之狮」侧身刻着如尼文，多半是11世纪斯堪的纳维亚雇佣兵的手笔。1593年，伽利略受聘为军械库顾问，解决弹道、船桨和木料问题，船匠们的难题后来写进他关于材料强度的著作。总督的礼舟也在这里建造和停泊：每年耶稣升天节，礼舟载着总督出海，把一枚戒指投入亚得里亚海，表示威尼斯与大海成婚。最后也最豪华的一艘1729年下水，长35米，需168名桨手。

即便在衰落年代，船坞仍有声名：俄国的彼得营建亚速海舰队时，就请来威尼斯船匠。1797年共和国灭亡，法国人拆毁在建船身，把缴获的五千多门火炮运往土伦。那艘礼舟1798年被拆散焚烧，为的是刮下雕花上的金箔。

en:
Santa Maria del Fiore stood without its dome for decades. Begun in 1296 to replace the old church of Santa Reparata, its nave was finished first, faced in bands of white Carrara, green Prato and red Sienese marble, but the east end waited on a problem no one could solve. The model by Neri di Fioravanti called for an octagonal dome wider and higher than any ever built, without the Gothic buttresses Florentines despised; it would start 52 metres above the floor and span 44, and Tuscany held nowhere near enough timber for the usual wooden centring.

In 1418 the wool guild opened a competition, and the goldsmith Filippo Brunelleschi won it against Lorenzo Ghiberti. He raised two brick shells, a thick inner one and a thin outer one, and laid the courses in a herringbone bond so that each fresh ring locked itself into the vertical ribs while the mortar set, with no scaffold from below. He designed the hoists that raised 37,000 tons of material and more than four million bricks. On 25 March 1436, New Year's Day in the Florentine calendar, Pope Eugene IV consecrated the finished cathedral while Guillaume Dufay's motet Nuper rosarum flores was sung. Brunelleschi died in 1446, a few months after the lantern was begun, and was buried in his own cathedral in a plain tomb in the old crypt of Santa Reparata. In 1469 Verrocchio crowned the lantern with a gilded copper ball, the young Leonardo watching from his workshop; lightning shattered it later and a larger one replaced it.

Inside, Paolo Uccello made the one-handed liturgical clock over the main door, its dial running the 24 hours to sunset, and Domenico di Michelino painted Dante among the three realms of his Comedy. Paolo Toscanelli pierced the dome with an observation hole for a short meridian line near the altar. Grand Duke Cosimo I had the inside of the dome painted: Giorgio Vasari began the Last Judgment, and Federico Zuccari finished its 3,600 square metres of figures in 1579.
zh:
圣母百花大教堂有几十年没有穹顶。它1296年动工，取代旧的圣雷帕拉塔堂，殿身先行完工，外墙以白色卡拉拉、绿色普拉托和红色锡耶纳大理石相间镶成，但东端卡在一个无人能解的难题上。内里·迪·菲奥拉万蒂的模型要求一座八角穹顶：起脚点离地52米、跨度44米，比以往任何穹顶都更高更宽，还不许用佛罗伦萨人鄙夷的哥特飞扶壁；而托斯卡纳全境的木材都不够搭传统的满堂脚手架。

1418年羊毛行会悬赏征集方案，金匠菲利波·布鲁内莱斯基赢了洛伦佐·吉贝尔蒂。他造了内外两层砖壳，内壳厚实、外壳轻薄，砖层按鱼骨纹排列，灰浆未干时每一圈新砖都自行锁进竖向肋条，穹顶从下而上不用任何支撑。他又设计专用吊车，吊起3.7万吨材料和四百多万块砖。1436年3月25日，佛罗伦萨历的元旦，教皇恩仁四世为完工的大教堂祝圣，纪尧姆·迪费的经文歌《玫瑰新开》（Nuper rosarum flores）在典礼上演唱。采光亭动工几个月后，布鲁内莱斯基于1446年去世，葬在他自己建起的大教堂里，墓在旧圣雷帕拉塔堂地下，形制简朴。1469年韦罗基奥在锥顶安上镀金铜球，年轻的列奥纳多·达·芬奇正在作坊里看着；后来雷电击碎铜球，一只更大的取而代之。

堂内，保罗·乌切洛制作了主门上方的单针礼仪大钟，钟面按24小时倒数到日落；多梅尼科·迪·米凯利诺画出但丁置身《神曲》三界的图景。保罗·托斯卡内利在穹顶上开出观测孔，在祭坛附近铺出一段短短的子午线。大公科西莫一世下令绘制穹顶内壁，乔治·瓦萨里动笔绘制《最后的审判》，费德里科·祖卡里1579年完成了这3600平方米的画面。

en:
In 1586 Domenico Fontana moved the granite obelisk of Nero's circus into the square before St Peter's. As the lifting ropes began to smoke from the strain, a sailor from Sanremo shouted for water and saved the stone, and his town earned the duty of supplying the palms for Palm Sunday.

The church it stood before began as Constantine's basilica on Vatican Hill, built over Peter's grave outside the city walls; on Christmas Day 800 Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne emperor at its altar. By the 1400s the old church was ruinous, and Alberti measured one long wall leaning more than six feet out of true. Julius II had it pulled down, which shocked many Romans, since it carried the papacy's continuity back to Peter. Bramante won the competition with a Greek-cross plan under a dome like the Pantheon's, and the first stone was laid in 1506. Indulgences sold in Germany to pay for it gave the preacher Johann Tetzel his scandal and helped push Luther into revolt. Raphael lengthened the plan into a nave, and the sack of Rome in 1527 scattered the works for years.

In 1547 Michelangelo, already in his seventies, took charge, saying he served 'for the love of God and in honour of the Apostle'. He bulked up the cracked piers and designed the dome, a double brick shell with 16 stone ribs; it was closed in 1590, after his death. Carlo Maderno stretched the church into a Latin cross, and Urban VIII consecrated it on 18 November 1626. Under him Bernini raised a 29-metre bronze baldachin over Peter's altar, its twisted columns copied from the old church. Michelangelo's Pietà stood in a side chapel; among the laity buried there were Queen Christina of Sweden, who abdicated to become a Catholic, and the exiled Stuart pretenders.
zh:
1586年，多梅尼科·丰塔纳把尼禄马戏场的花岗岩方尖碑移到圣伯多禄大殿（圣彼得大教堂）前的广场。吊索被磨得冒烟时，圣雷莫的一名水手高喊浇水，救下了石碑，他的家乡因而得到为圣枝主日供应棕榈枝的特权。

广场后的大殿起初是君士坦丁大帝建在梵蒂冈山丘上的老殿，坐落在罗马城墙外的伯多禄墓上；800年圣诞节，教皇良三世在祭坛前为查理曼加冕为帝。到15世纪，老殿已四处倾颓，莱昂·巴蒂斯塔·阿尔贝蒂量得一道长墙倾斜超过六英尺。儒略二世下令拆毁老殿，许多罗马人深感震惊，因为老殿连着从伯多禄开始的教皇世系。伯拉孟特以希腊十字平面和万神殿式穹顶中标，1506年奠基。为筹款在德意志售卖赎罪券，让多明我会修士约翰·台彻尔成了丑闻的中心，也把马丁·路德推向公开反抗。拉斐尔把方案改成长厅，1527年罗马之劫又让工程搁置多年。

1547年，已年过七旬的米开朗基罗接掌工程，自称「为了天主的爱和宗徒的荣耀」而做。他加固开裂的墩柱，设计了这座双层砖壳、外带16道石肋的穹顶；穹顶在他身后于1590年封顶。卡洛·马代尔诺把教堂拉成长拉丁十字，1626年11月18日教皇乌尔巴诺八世为大殿祝圣。乌尔巴诺八世任内，贝尔尼尼在伯多禄祭坛上方竖起29米高的青铜华盖，扭柱形制取自老殿。侧堂里供着米开朗基罗的《圣殇》，葬在此间的在俗信徒有放弃王位皈依天主教的瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜，也有流亡的斯图亚特家族王位觊觎者。

en:
At the top of the park of Caserta an artificial cascade falls 78 metres, fed by water that travelled 38 kilometres from the Fizzo springs on Monte Taburno through the Carolino Aqueduct, mostly underground. Where it crosses the Valle di Maddaloni the channel runs over a three-tier tufa bridge 529 metres long and 56 metres high, copied from the aqueducts of ancient Rome.

The palace itself stands in the plain 35 kilometres north of Naples, a five-storey rectangle of 247 by 190 metres with about 1,200 rooms. Charles VII of Naples, later Charles III of Spain, laid the first stone on 20 January 1752, his thirty-sixth birthday. He wanted court, government and guard barracks under one roof on the model of Versailles, on ground beyond the reach of Vesuvius and sea raids and away from crowded, revolt-prone Naples. Luigi Vanvitelli made the design, and over two thousand workmen and slaves raised it from local tuff, travertine and lime. Charles never slept a night in it: in 1759 he left for the crown of Spain, and his young son Ferdinand IV inherited an unfinished house. Vanvitelli died before it was done and his son Carlo carried the work on; the court first lived there in 1789, when the palace had cost seven million ducats.

Queen Maria Carolina had the English gardener John Graefer lay out an English garden with plants brought directly from Japan, China and Australia, while a silk mill at San Leucio worked on the same aqueduct's water. The Parthenopaean Republic seized the palace in 1799 and carried off its furniture, later recovered. Under French rule Joachim Murat installed his court here and left an Empire apartment hung with San Leucio silk; Ferdinand IV came back in 1815.
zh:
卡塞塔的园林尽头，有一道78米高的人工瀑布，水来自塔布尔诺山的菲佐泉，由38公里长的卡罗利诺水道送来，水道大半埋在地下。跨越马达洛尼谷地的一段是三层凝灰拱券桥，长529米、高56米，仿古罗马水道而建。

卡塞塔王宫本身立在那波利以北35公里的平原上，是一座247米长、190米宽的五层矩形建筑，约有1200个房间。1752年1月20日，那波利国王卡洛七世（后来的西班牙国王卡洛斯三世）在他36岁生日那天埋下奠基石。他想把宫廷、衙署和卫兵营房集中在一座建筑里，以凡尔赛为样板，选在维苏威火山波及不到、海上袭击够不着的地方，离开拥挤又容易闹事的那波利。路易吉·万维泰利主持设计，两千多名工匠和奴隶用当地的凝灰岩、洞石和石灰把它砌起来。卡洛没有在王宫里住过一夜：1759年他动身去西班牙继位，未完工的宫殿留给幼子费迪南多四世。万维泰利没能看到竣工，由其子卡洛接手；宫廷1789年才首次入住，此时工程已花去700万杜卡特。

王后玛丽亚·卡罗利娜请来英国园艺师约翰·格雷费尔营造英式园林，栽种直接从日本、中国和澳大利亚运来的植物，圣卢乔的丝织厂也借同一条水渠的水力开工。1799年帕特诺珀共和国没收王宫、搬走家具（后来追回）。法国统治时期，若阿基姆·缪拉把宫廷设在宫中，留下挂满圣卢乔丝绸的帝政风格套房；费迪南多四世1815年回宫。

en:
The Malta forts ring the Grand Harbour, one of the safest anchorages between Sicily and the African coast. Its core was Fort St Angelo on the Birgu headland, a medieval castle the Aragonese called the Castrum Maris; after 1530 the Hospitallers cut a dry ditch through its rock and made it the grand master's seat. Across the water, on the tip of the Sciberras peninsula, an Aragonese watchtower was rebuilt as the star fort St Elmo, and it took the first blow in 1565. About 150 knights and 600 soldiers held out for 28 days under fire from Mount Sciberras, until the fort fell on 23 June and none of its knights survived. An Ottoman cannon misfired and threw up stone splinters that mortally wounded the admiral Dragut, and the month spent on St Elmo gave Birgu and Senglea time to arm. St Angelo drove off the sea attack on Senglea in August and never fell, and weeks later the relief army from Sicily landed.

Afterwards the knights girdled their new capital Valletta with bastions drawn by the papal engineer Francesco Laparelli, and kept building for two centuries. The Cottonera Lines were meant to shelter 40,000 islanders in a siege; Fort Ricasoli guarded the harbour mouth and became the largest fort on the islands; Fort Manoel on its islet, paid for by Grand Master Vilhena, was finished in 1733 with its own Baroque chapel. Fort Chambray on Gozo was meant to take in that island's whole population, but the town planned inside its walls was never built.

In 1775 thirteen rebel priests seized St Elmo for a few days; three were executed and their heads displayed on a Valletta cavalier. The guns did not save the order: when Napoleon landed in June 1798 Grand Master Hompesch surrendered the fortified harbour within days, without a siege. The French garrison held the forts through the two-year Maltese blockade and gave them up to the British in 1800.
zh:
马耳他堡垒群环绕着大港，那是西西里与非洲海岸之间最稳妥的锚地之一。核心是比尔古角上的圣安杰洛堡，中世纪时本是阿拉贡人所称的「海边城堡」；1530年后，医院骑士团凿开岩石修成干壕，把这里作为大教长驻地。对岸希伯拉斯半岛尖端，阿拉贡人的瞭望塔被改建成星形的圣埃尔莫堡，1565年它首当其冲：约150名骑士和600名士兵在希伯拉斯山的炮火下坚守28天，6月23日城陷，堡中骑士无一生还。一门奥斯曼大炮炸膛，飞起的碎石给海军将领德拉古特造成致命伤；攻打圣埃尔莫耗掉的一个月，为比尔古和森格莱阿争取了备战时间。8月，圣安杰洛堡击退对森格莱阿的海上进攻，始终未破，几周后西西里援军登岛。

此后骑士团按教皇派来的工程师弗朗切斯科·拉帕雷利的设计，给新都瓦莱塔围上棱堡，两百年里仍在增筑。科托内拉防线打算在围城时容纳4万名岛民；里卡索利堡扼守港口咽喉，后来成为群岛最大的堡垒；马尔萨穆谢特港小岛上的马诺埃尔堡由大教长维列纳出资，1733年完工，堡内还有一座巴洛克小教堂。戈佐岛上的尚布雷堡为战时收容全岛居民而建，但墙内规划的新城始终没有盖起来。

1775年，十三名起事的神父一度占领圣埃尔莫堡，三人被处死，首级挂在瓦莱塔的一座碉楼上示众。这些大炮终究没能保住骑士团：1798年6月拿破仑登陆，大教长霍姆佩施几天内就献出设防港口，未经一场围城战。法国守军靠着堡垒撑过马耳他人两年的封锁，于1800年把它们交给英国人。

en:
The story goes that Emperor Matthias, hunting here, found an artesian well and cried 'Welch' schöner Brunn!', what a fine spring, and so gave Schönbrunn its name. The estate lies on the Wien river outside Vienna, below a wooded hill. In 1569 Maximilian II bought it as the Katterburg, fenced it and made it the court's hunting ground, with a pen of its own for turkeys and peafowl. Eleonora Gonzaga, widow of Ferdinand II, added the first palace and an early orangery in the following decades. The Ottoman siege of 1683 wrecked them, and Leopold I charged Johann Bernhard Fischer von Erlach with a new palace for his heir. His first draft would have outdone Versailles but was beyond the treasury; the smaller baroque palace built over the ruins became the core of the house.

In 1740 Charles VI gave the neglected estate to his daughter Maria Theresa. Her architect Nikolaus von Pacassi added a storey and fitted the rococo rooms that made it the imperial summer seat, to which the court moved from the Hofburg each year. On 13 October 1762 the six-year-old Mozart played here for the empress, and his family later told how he slipped on a polished floor and promised to marry the archduchess who helped him up, the future Marie Antoinette. Behind the palace the Gloriette went up in 1775 as a monument to Kolin, where Frederick the Great's march on Vienna was stopped in 1757.

Napoleon made the palace his headquarters in 1805 and again in 1809, sleeping in the room that took his name. There on 14 October 1809 Austria signed the Peace of Schönbrunn, losing the Illyrian provinces and Galicia, and the marriage of Archduchess Marie Louise to Napoleon the next year sealed the forced alliance.
zh:
相传皇帝马蒂亚斯出猎到这里，发现一眼自流井，脱口赞道「好一眼美泉」，「美泉」之名就这样得来。庄园位于维也纳城外维也纳河的滩地上，背靠一座林木覆盖的山丘。1569年，马克西米利安二世买下这片名为卡特堡的庄园，圈起来做宫廷猎场，另给火鸡和孔雀单辟一圈围栏。斐迪南二世的遗孀埃莱奥诺拉·贡扎加随后添建了第一座宫殿和一座早期橘园。1683年奥斯曼围城时，这些建筑被毁，利奥波德一世委托约翰·伯恩哈德·费舍尔·冯·埃拉赫为继承人重建新宫；建筑师的初稿本要压过凡尔赛，却超出国库承受之力；在废墟上建成的较小的巴洛克宫殿，成了美泉宫的核心。

1740年，卡尔六世把这座渐受冷落的庄园赐给女儿玛丽亚·特蕾西亚。她的建筑师尼古劳斯·冯·帕卡西把宫殿加高一层，装出一整套洛可可厅堂，这里就此成为皇室的夏宫，宫廷每年都从霍夫堡搬来。1762年10月13日，六岁的莫扎特在此为女皇演奏，据他家人后来讲述，他在光滑的地板上滑倒，被小公主扶起后便宣布将来要娶她，那就是后来的玛丽·安托瓦内特。宫后小丘上，1775年建起凯旋门（Gloriette），纪念1757年挡住腓特烈大王进军维也纳的科林战役。

拿破仑1805年和1809年两次以美泉宫为司令部，睡的那间房后来就叫拿破仑室。1809年10月14日，奥地利在宫中签署《美泉宫和约》，割去伊利里亚诸省和加利西亚；次年玛丽·路易丝女大公与拿破仑成婚，为这场强加的同盟作了担保。

en:
Pericles told the Athenians that the forty talents of gold on the statue of Athena inside the Parthenon were all removable, to be coined in an emergency and replaced afterwards. The temple went up from 447 BC, when Athens held the tribute of the Delian League. Ictinus and Callicrates built it in Pentelic marble, and nearly every line is a subtle curve: the platform rises at its centre, the columns swell and lean inward, and the corner columns stand a little thicker than the rest. Phidias' Athena Parthenos, about thirteen metres of cypress wood sheathed in ivory and gold, was carried to Constantinople and lost. The temple became the church of the Theotokos and then the Latin cathedral of the Florentine dukes, until in 1436 Cyriacus of Ancona named it the temple of Athena and a work of Phidias, the first such description since antiquity.

After the Acropolis surrendered the church became a mosque: the Frankish bell tower was raised into a minaret, the apse became a mihrab and the saints were whitewashed, but the marble fabric stayed whole. The Ottoman traveller Evliya Celebi called it a fortress not made by human hands and prayed it might stand forever, and Jacques Carrey drew its pediments and metopes for a French embassy, now often the only record of lost figures. On 26 September 1687, during Morosini's siege, a mortar from the Hill of Philopappos dropped into the Parthenon, where the Ottoman garrison had piled gunpowder and sheltered the Turkish families of the town. Three cella walls came down, with three-fifths of the frieze, and about three hundred people died. Morosini then tried to prise Athena's chariot horses and the figure of Poseidon off the west pediment as loot; his men dropped them and they shattered on the rock. From 1801 agents of Lord Elgin removed roughly half the surviving sculptures with permission from the Ottoman authorities; the British Museum bought the marbles, and Lord Byron denounced the whole affair as plunder.
zh:
伯里克利曾向雅典人说明，帕特农神庙里雅典娜像上的四十塔兰同黄金全部可以拆下，危急时铸成钱币，事后再补。神庙始建于公元前447年，当时雅典掌管着提洛同盟的贡金。建筑师伊克蒂诺斯和卡利克拉特以潘泰列克大理石建造，几乎没有一条直线：台基中央微微上拱，柱身鼓胀并稍向内倾，角柱比其余柱子略粗。菲狄亚斯所作的雅典娜·帕特农巨像以柏木为胎、外包象牙和金箔，高约十三米，后来被运到君士坦丁堡并就此失踪。神殿先后成为天主之母教堂和佛罗伦萨公爵治下的拉丁礼主教座堂；1436年，安科纳的齐里亚科是古代以后第一个重新把它称作雅典娜神庙、菲狄亚斯作品的人。

卫城投降后，教堂改成清真寺：法兰克人的钟楼被加高为宣礼塔，后殿改为米哈拉布，墙上圣像被白灰覆盖，但大理石的主体仍然完整。奥斯曼旅行家埃夫利亚·切莱比称它如非人力所造的堡垒，祈愿它永世长存；雅克·卡雷则为法国使团画下它的三角墙和陇间壁，这些画后来常是失落雕像仅存的记录。1687年9月26日晚，莫罗西尼率威尼斯军队攻城，一发迫击炮弹从菲洛帕波斯山射落帕特农；奥斯曼守军把火药堆在庙里，城中的土耳其妇孺也躲在里面。内殿四壁倒了三面，五分之三的浮雕带坠落，约三百人丧命。莫罗西尼又想把西三角墙上雅典娜战车的群马和波塞冬像撬下带走，兵士失手，雕像摔碎在岩石上。1801年起，埃尔金伯爵的代理人经奥斯曼当局许可拆走约一半幸存雕刻；大英博物馆买下这批石雕，拜伦勋爵则斥之为劫掠。

en:
Writers who saw the interior of Hagia Sophia said the dome seemed to hang in the air: forty windows circled its base and the light filled the drum. Justinian I began the church in 532 after the Nika riot destroyed its predecessor, and Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus directed some ten thousand workers for five years. At the consecration on 27 December 537, walls of polychrome marble and porphyry surrounded a nave about 76 metres long, under a dome roughly 31 metres across that rested on pendentives. By 1444 it was nearly nine centuries old and still the patriarchal cathedral, though visitors found parts dilapidated, with doors fallen from their hinges. In December 1452 Isidore of Kiev proclaimed the Union of Florence there, and many anti-union Orthodox kept away from the liturgy.

In the last days of the May 1453 siege, Nestor Iskander's tale recorded a light around the dome that frightened viewers interpreted as the Holy Spirit abandoning the city. As the walls were breached, refugees barred themselves inside the cathedral; Ottoman troops battered down the doors and divided the people they found there. When Mehmed II entered, he stopped a soldier from prying up a Proconnesian marble paving slab and had a scholar climb the ambo to recite the shahada. The first Friday prayer followed on 1 June. Mehmed repaired the building and endowed it with houses, shops and markets, making it Istanbul's first imperial mosque.

Later sultans rebuilt it in their own rite. Bayezid II added a minaret at the northeast corner, and Suleiman I placed two huge Hungarian campaign candlesticks by the mihrab. Under Selim II, Mimar Sinan strengthened the tired Byzantine walls and added the two western minarets; Selim and several later sultans were buried in tombs beside the mosque. Figural mosaics were plastered over gradually, not all at once, and seventeenth-century travellers could still report Christian images in the old cathedral.
zh:
见过圣索菲亚大教堂内部的作者都说，穹顶像悬在半空：穹座绕着40扇窗，光线灌满整个穹筒。532年尼卡暴动烧毁前代教堂后，查士丁尼一世下令兴建这座教堂，特拉勒斯的安提莫斯和米利都的伊西多尔主持工程，约一万名工人修了五年多。537年12月27日献堂时，彩色大理石和斑岩镶满墙面，约76米长的中厅上方，直径约31米的穹顶落在三角帆拱上。到1444年，这座建筑已近九百年，仍是牧首座堂，但西方访客已看见它局部破败，有些门扇从铰链上脱落。1452年12月，基辅的伊西多尔在此宣布佛罗伦萨合一，许多反对合一的东正教徒便不再来参加礼仪。

1453年5月围城末期，内斯托尔·伊斯坎德尔的《夺取沙皇城记》记下穹顶周围出现异光，惊慌的观者把它解释成圣灵弃城。城墙被突破后，难民把自己关在这座大堂里，奥斯曼军队撞开门，将里面的人分作战利品。穆罕默德二世入内后，制止一名士兵撬起普罗孔尼索斯大理石地砖，又命一位宗教学者登上读经台念诵清真言。6月1日，第一次主麻礼拜在此举行。穆罕默德下令修缮建筑，并把房屋、店铺和市场拨作瓦合甫产业，圣索菲亚大教堂成了伊斯坦布尔第一座帝国清真寺。

此后的苏丹按伊斯兰礼仪改建它。巴耶济德二世在东北角增建宣礼塔，苏莱曼一世把从匈牙利战事中带回的两座巨型烛台放在米哈拉布两侧。塞利姆二世时期，米马尔·锡南加固了老化的拜占庭墙体，又增建西边两座宣礼塔；塞利姆和后来几位苏丹都葬在寺旁的陵墓里。人物马赛克是逐渐被灰泥覆盖的，并非一次封死；17世纪的旅行者仍记载自己在旧大堂里看见基督教图像。

en:
Some Ottoman jurists forbade Muslims to pray in the Sultan Ahmed Mosque. The ulema held that an imperial mosque ought to be paid for with spoils from a victorious campaign, and Ahmed I had won no such victory; he was drawing on a strained treasury, after a peace in 1606 that the jurists read as a blow to dynastic prestige. In 1609 he chose the southeast side of the old Hippodrome, facing Hagia Sophia across the imperial centre. The ground held the Hippodrome's bleachers and imperial box, then the palaces of viziers including Sokollu Mehmed Pasha, so the state had to carry out a costly expropriation.

Sedefkar Mehmed Agha built the mosque. Its prayer hall, 64 by 72 metres, is covered by a central dome 43 metres high and 23.5 metres across, carried on four semi-domes and fronted by a broad courtyard. Six minarets rise at the corners. The interior uses more than twenty thousand Iznik tiles in blue, green and white, with floral patterns, more than two hundred coloured-glass windows and calligraphy by Diyarbakırlı Seyyid Kasım Gubari; the blue tones later gave European visitors the name Blue Mosque. Around it rose madrasas, a hospital, a soup kitchen, a bath, shops, fountains and Ahmed's tomb. The mosque opened in 1617, the year the sultan died, and the last construction accounts were signed by his successor, Mustafa I.
zh:
苏丹艾哈迈德清真寺落成前后，一些奥斯曼法学家甚至禁止穆斯林到这里礼拜。教法学者认为，帝国清真寺应当用胜仗得来的战利品支付，而艾哈迈德一世没有取得这样的大胜，还在财政吃紧时动用国库；1606年的和约又被教法界视为王朝声望受挫。1609年，他选定旧赛马场东南侧，在帝国中心隔地面向圣索菲亚大教堂。这里原有赛马场看台和皇家包厢，后来又有索科卢·穆罕默德帕夏等维齐尔的宅邸，国家必须高价征购土地。

塞德夫卡尔·穆罕默德阿迦主持修建。礼拜殿长72米、宽64米，中央穹顶高43米、直径23.5米，由四座半穹顶承接，殿前是宽阔庭院。六座宣礼塔立在角落。殿内使用两万多块蓝、绿、白色调的伊兹尼克瓷砖，饰以花卉纹样，还有二百多扇彩色玻璃窗和迪亚巴克尔人赛义德·卡西姆·古巴里书写的经文；偏蓝的色调让欧洲访客后来称它为蓝色清真寺。寺周建有经学院、医院、施粥场、浴场、店铺、喷泉，以及艾哈迈德的陵墓。清真寺1617年举行开幕礼，艾哈迈德一世也在同年去世；最后一批工程账目由继任者穆斯塔法一世签署。

en:
The books of Matthias Corvinus wore dark leather bindings, often stamped with the royal arms and the Corvinus raven, and a workshop in Buda made them. In 1444 none of this existed: the Bibliotheca Corviniana was still only a possibility inside Buda's old Gothic palace. Matthias became king in 1458 and collected through agents, scribes and booksellers in Italy and the eastern Mediterranean. After he married Beatrice of Naples in 1476, Italian humanists, painters and craftsmen came to Buda, and the palace received early Renaissance rooms, a loggia and two gilded ceilings. One gilded room held the library; the passage beside it was painted with the twelve signs of the zodiac.

The shelves held Greek and Latin classics beside theology, law, history, geography, medicine, architecture and natural science. Hungarian estimates put about 2,500 codices in the collection when Matthias died in 1490, some finished in Florence and never delivered. A Florentine humanist, Bartolomeo della Fonte, wrote that Lorenzo de' Medici's own Greek and Latin library was encouraged by the Hungarian king's example. That patronage ended with Matthias. After the defeat at Mohács in 1526, codices from Buda were carried to Istanbul, while others were dispersed or lost. Later catalogues identify about 216 Corvinae, and a few lost volumes are known to have held the only surviving texts of ancient works.
zh:
马加什·科尔温的藏书用深色皮面装帧，封面常压印王徽和科尔温家族的渡鸦，装订由布达本地的作坊完成。1444年这一切还不存在，科尔文纳图书馆只是布达旧哥特王宫里的一处空位。马加什1458年即位，通过代理人、抄书人和书商，在意大利和东地中海搜集书籍。1476年他迎娶那不勒斯的贝亚特丽切后，意大利人文主义者、画家和工匠来到布达，王宫增建了早期文艺复兴风格的厅堂和敞廊，还有两间鎏金天花板的房间：一间安放图书馆，相邻的走廊绘有黄道十二宫。

书架上，希腊语和拉丁语古典著作与神学、法律、历史、地理、医学、建筑、自然科学书籍并列。据匈牙利学者估算，马加什1490年去世时馆藏约有2500部抄本，其中有些已在佛罗伦萨完成，却没有运到布达。佛罗伦萨人文主义者巴尔托洛梅奥·德拉·丰特写道，洛伦佐·德·美第奇建立自己的希腊语、拉丁语图书馆，就受到这位匈牙利国王的启发。马加什一死，这种扶持也随之中断。1526年匈牙利在摩哈赤战败后，布达的抄本被运往伊斯坦布尔，另一些流散或遗失。后世目录可考的科尔文纳抄本约216部；已知有几部散佚抄本，曾保存着某些古代著作的唯一文本。

en:
The Kremnica ducat became hard currency in Central Europe because its gold never varied in purity. The Golden City was a fortified mining economy rather than a single monument: gold veins, shafts, the mint, double town walls and the castle above Kremnica's square. On 17 November 1328 Charles Robert raised Cremnychbana to a free royal mining and minting town, and the new mint struck gold florins from 1335. The Chamber Count had his seat there, supervising mines and mints across twelve counties of the Hungarian crown. Minters and settlers came from Italy, Bavaria, Austria, Silesia and Bohemia, including coiners from Kutná Hora. The castle hill had begun with a Romanesque church and ossuary, then gained a double ring of walls, the Chamber Count's palace and a secure storehouse for extracted gold and newly struck coins. In 1444 the walls above Hont guarded one of the Hungarian crown's most reliable pay chests.

Firearms and deeper ore shaped the town in the following centuries. The castle fortifications were rebuilt with firing positions, and the Miner's Bastion began as a small chapel of the Nativity of the Virgin; when the Ottoman danger grew in the sixteenth century its nave was pulled down and its presbytery became an open artillery position. St Catherine's tower burned in 1560 and was rebuilt in Renaissance form, and in 1588 Peter Gräf cast the great bell Urban for the Clock Tower. Kremnica also became a centre of medal work, above all for the religious medals cut by Joachim Deschler. As shafts followed the gold deeper, groundwater raised costs and narrowed profits, although the mint kept striking coin. Between 1765 and 1772 the town put up one of the last great plague columns in the Habsburg lands.
zh:
克雷姆尼察杜卡特之所以成为中欧的硬通货，是因为它的金子成色从不波动。黄金城是一整套围绕金矿运转的设防体系，而不是单独的一座建筑：矿脉、竖井、造币厂、双重城墙，以及高踞城镇广场上方的城堡。1328年11月17日，查理·罗贝尔把克雷姆尼察班亚升格为自由王家矿业和造币城镇，新设的造币厂从1335年起铸造金弗罗林。金库总管驻在此地，代表匈牙利国王监管十二个州的矿山和造币厂。造币匠和定居者来自意大利、巴伐利亚、奥地利、西里西亚和波希米亚，其中也有库特纳霍拉的铸币工匠。城堡丘最初有罗马式教堂和藏骨堂，后来围起双重城墙，建起金库总管宫和安全库房，存放开采出的黄金与新铸钱币。1444年，洪特山间这些高墙守护的，是匈牙利王冠最可靠的钱库之一。

此后几百年，火器和越来越深的矿层改变了这座城。城堡防御工事按火枪和火炮作战改造；矿工棱堡最初是圣母降生小堂，16世纪奥斯曼威胁加重后，礼拜堂中殿被拆，圣所改成开放炮兵阵地。圣凯瑟琳教堂塔楼1560年遭火灾，后按文艺复兴样式重建；1588年，彼得·格雷夫为钟楼铸造了文艺复兴大钟「乌尔班」。克雷姆尼察也成为奖章制作中心，尤其是约阿希姆·德施勒雕刻的宗教奖章。矿工追逐金脉不断深入，地下水推高成本、压低利润，造币厂仍继续铸币。1765年至1772年，城中立起哈布斯堡领地内最晚的大型瘟疫柱之一。

en:
Notre-Dame rises on the Ile de la Cite, the old royal island in the Seine. Bishop Maurice de Sully had the earlier churches there cleared and the cornerstone laid in 1163 before Louis VII and Pope Alexander III, and the work ran on for nearly two centuries. The choir is propped by fifteen-metre flying buttresses, an early use of the device on such a scale, and the two transept roses are among the largest in Europe. In 1239 Saint Louis brought the Crown of Thorns from Constantinople and laid it up in the cathedral while the Sainte-Chapelle was built to receive it. By 1444 the great church had been complete for a century.

When Reims was out of reach, Notre-Dame served as France's coronation church in Paris: in December 1431 the ten-year-old Henry VI of England was crowned king of France before its altar. In 1572 Marguerite de Valois married the Protestant Henry of Navarre on a platform raised against the west front; the bridegroom stood in the open porch for the nuptial mass, and the St Bartholomew's killings in the city began six days later. In the eighteenth century the canons, wanting more light, stripped out the medieval glass except for the roses. Revolutionaries made the cathedral a Temple of Reason: the twenty-eight kings of Judah over the portals were beheaded as kings of France, the bells were taken down and melted with only the great bourdon Emmanuel spared, and the nave stored grain. Catholic worship returned at Easter 1802.
zh:
巴黎圣母院立在塞纳河中的老城岛西岱岛上。1163年，主教莫里斯·德·叙利命人平掉岛上的旧教堂，在路易七世和教宗亚历山大三世面前放下第一块基石，工程持续了近两百年。唱诗班席外撑着15米长的飞扶壁，是这种构件最早的大规模运用之一；耳堂两面玫瑰窗属于欧洲最大的一批。1239年，圣王路易把从君士坦丁堡购得的荆冠暂存圣母院，待圣礼拜堂建成后再行安放。到1444年，这座大教堂已经整体落成一百年了。

兰斯用不上时，这里就是法兰西在巴黎的加冕教堂：1431年12月，十岁的英格兰国王亨利六世在祭坛前加冕为法兰西国王。1572年，玛格丽特·德·瓦卢瓦在西立门外搭起的高台上嫁给新教徒纳瓦拉的亨利，新郎只能站在露天门廊下听完婚礼弥撒，六天后巴黎便开始了圣巴托洛缪之夜的屠杀。18世纪，司铎们嫌堂内太暗，把除玫瑰窗外的中世纪彩窗尽数拆去。大革命中教堂被改成理性庙：门楣上方二十八尊犹太列王像被误认为法兰西国王，悉数砍头；众钟被拆下熔毁，只有大低音钟埃马纽埃尔幸免，中殿则用来堆存粮食。1802年复活节，天主教礼拜重新举行。

en:
In 1444 Versailles was a name for a stretch of wooded marsh west of Paris, good mainly for boar hunting. Louis XIII put up a hunting lodge there in 1623 and rebuilt it as a small brick-and-stone chateau; courtiers laughed at the 'puny chateau' in the mud, and the king would not even let his queen sleep there. The son who inherited it thought very differently. In August 1661 Louis XIV was guest of his finance minister Nicolas Fouquet at Vaux-le-Vicomte, a house and gardens so dazzling that he had Fouquet arrested within weeks and carried off the men who made them: the architect Louis Le Vau, the gardener Andre Le Notre and the painter Charles Le Brun. They enlarged the old chateau stage by stage, Louis XIV going over every plan himself. Jules Hardouin-Mansart added the wings and, from 1678, the 73-metre Hall of Mirrors, its 357 mirrors supplied by the royal glassworks founded to break Venice's hold on the trade. Le Notre drained the marsh into terraces, fountains and the Grand Canal.

The king then kept the whole court under that roof, its days cut to the ceremonies of his lever and coucher, the great nobles vying for leave to stand nearest his chair; embassies arrived from Genoa, Ayutthaya and Safavid Iran. Louis XIV died at Versailles on 1 September 1715 after seventy-two years on the throne, and the regent at once carried the child Louis XV back to Paris. On 5 October 1789 thousands of Paris market women marched to the gates and led the royal family back to Paris the next day. The furnishings were auctioned in seventeen thousand lots, and workmen chiselled the fleurs-de-lys off the walls. Napoleon thought of moving back and flinched at the cost; the gilded halls of the great chateau stayed empty.
zh:
1444年，凡尔赛宫所在的地方还只是巴黎西边一片林木丛生的沼泽，最大的用处是打野猪。路易十三1623年在这里盖了一座猎舍，后来改建成小小的砖石小宫；廷臣们讥笑它是泥地里的「破城堡」，国王甚至连王后都不许在此过夜。继位的儿子对它却看得极重。1661年8月，路易十四赴财政大臣尼古拉·富凯的沃勒维孔特宫之宴，那座宫殿和花园华美得让他几周后就把富凯下狱，又把营造的人尽数带走：建筑师路易·勒沃、园艺师安德烈·勒诺特尔和画家夏尔·勒布伦。他们把旧宫一期期扩建，每份图样都经路易十四亲自过目。于勒·阿杜安-芒萨尔加建两翼，并在1678年起修出73米长的镜厅，357面镜子由为与威尼斯争胜而设立的王家制镜厂供货。勒诺特尔排干沼泽，开出层层台地、喷泉和大运河。

此后国王把整个宫廷收在这片屋顶下，日子由晨起礼（lever）和就寝礼（coucher）切成一段一段，大贵族们争的是获准站在离国王御座最近的位置；热那亚、阿瑜陀耶和萨法维伊朗的使节先后来到。1715年9月1日，路易十四在凡尔赛去世，在位七十二年，摄政立刻把年幼的路易十五带回巴黎。1789年10月5日，数千名巴黎市场妇女走到宫门前，第二天把王室一家带回巴黎。宫中陈设分一万七千批拍卖，工匠把墙面上的百合花徽逐一凿掉。称帝后的拿破仑盘算过搬回凡尔赛，又嫌修缮费太高；大宫殿那些镀金的大厅一直空着。

en:
The Palais des Papes crowns the Rocher des Doms above the Rhone: eleven thousand square metres of Gothic stone walled about with high towers, one of the largest palaces built in medieval Europe. Benedict XII, a Cistercian who wanted a fortress rather than a court, had the old bishop's palace pulled down and from 1335 raised the Palais Vieux around a cloister. Clement VI, the most lavish of the Avignon popes, added the Palais Neuf, its great halls painted by Sienese masters: Simone Martini and Matteo Giovanetti covered walls and vaults with saints, prophets and hunting scenes. The papal library held some two thousand volumes, the largest collection in Christendom, and Clement heard Machaut's Messe de Nostre Dame in the Grand Chapel. For thirty years the work swallowed much of the papacy's income.

The popes went back to Rome in 1377, and the palace kept only their substitutes. During the Schism the Avignon claimant Benedict XIII was besieged there by Geoffrey Boucicaut's troops in 1398 and lived as a prisoner in his own palace for five years before he escaped. Cardinal-legates took over, and in 1444 the great halls stood half-empty around a much-shrunken court. In October 1791 the Glaciere killings happened inside one of its towers, where the bodies were thrown into an old ice-pit. Under Napoleon the state made the palace a barracks and prison: soldiers stripped out the wooden ceilings, stabled horses in the chapels and whitewashed the painted walls.
zh:
教宗宫踞在罗讷河畔的多姆岩上，是一万一千平方米、高墙高塔环护的哥特石构，中世纪欧洲没有几座宫殿比它更大。本笃十二世是西多会修士，想要要塞而非宫苑，他命人拆毁旧主教宫，1335年起围绕回廊筑起旧宫。阿维尼翁诸教宗中最讲排场的克雷芒六世加建新宫，大厅由锡耶纳画派名家执笔：西蒙内·马蒂尼和马泰奥·焦万内蒂在墙壁和拱顶上画满圣徒、先知和围猎图。教宗藏书室收有约两千卷书，是基督教世界最大的一批藏书；克雷芒在大礼拜堂听过马肖的《圣母弥撒》。工程持续三十年，吞掉了教廷岁入的大头。

1377年教宗迁回罗马，宫里只剩下代理人。教会大分裂期间，阿维尼翁的对立教宗本笃十三世1398年在宫中被若弗鲁瓦·布西科的军队围困，在自己的宫殿里被囚五年才逃脱。后来宫殿由枢机使节接管，1444年时大厅大半空着，宫廷已大大缩水。1791年10月的格拉西耶尔屠杀就发生在它的一座塔里，尸体被扔进塔中的旧冰窖。拿破仑时期，国家把宫殿改成兵营和监狱：士兵拆走木顶棚，在礼拜堂里拴马，又把画满壁画的墙壁用白灰盖死。

en:
The Aljaferia was raised on the flat parade ground outside the Roman walls of Saraqusta, the Muslim Zaragoza. From 1065 Abu Ya'far Ahmad al-Muqtadir, second king of the Banu Hud, built it there as a palace of leisure: in his own verses he named it Qasr al-Surur, the Palace of Joy, and called his audience chamber the Golden Hall. The name the building kept comes from Abu Ya'far himself. A rectangle of walls ringed by sixteen semicircular towers enclosed courtyards of mixtilinear arches and carved stucco, baths and a small private mosque, whose mihrab keeps a polylobed horseshoe arch. It is the only large Hispano-Muslim palace of the taifa era that survives.

Alfonso I made it a royal palace after taking Zaragoza in 1118. In the fourteenth century Peter IV the Ceremonious rebuilt much of it in Gothic and Mudejar style, and palace records list rooms kept for his lions and other wild beasts. In 1444 it was still the palace of the kings of Aragon in their chief peninsular city, even though Alfonso V held his court in Naples. In 1486 the old keep became a prison of the Inquisition, and prisoners later covered its upper walls with graffiti. Ferdinand the Catholic then had the main floor rebuilt for the Catholic Monarchs by Mudejar master builders, who left it its carved wooden ceilings. In 1593 the palace was converted into a Renaissance fortress with a new moat and then into regimental barracks, and French bombardments during the two sieges of the Peninsular War left its Islamic halls open to the sky.
zh:
阿尔哈费里亚宫建在穆斯林的萨拉戈萨（阿拉伯语称萨拉库斯塔）罗马城墙外的平坦阅兵场上。1065年起，巴努·胡德王朝第二任君主阿布·雅法尔·艾哈迈德·穆克塔迪尔在此修建游乐宫殿：他在自己的诗里称它为「喜悦之宫」，把接见使节的御座殿叫做「金厅」，阿尔哈费里亚这个名字也来自他的名号阿布·雅法尔。十六座半圆形塔楼环着长方形围墙，墙内是多重混合线脚拱券庭院、灰泥浮雕、浴室和一间私人小礼拜寺，米哈拉布上保留着多瓣马蹄拱。它是泰法时代仅存的大型伊斯兰宫殿。

1118年阿方索一世攻下萨拉戈萨后，这里成为阿拉贡国王的王宫。14世纪，礼仪者佩德罗四世以哥特式和穆德哈尔风格大规模改建，宫中档案还列有饲养狮子和其他猛兽的兽房。1444年，阿方索五世的宫廷虽远在那波利，这里仍是阿拉贡国王在其半岛首要城市的宫殿。1486年，旧主堡成为宗教裁判所的监狱，囚犯后来在上层墙壁上写满涂鸦；随后天主教徒费尔南多二世请穆德哈尔工匠把主层改建为双王宫殿，精雕木顶棚就是那时留下的。1593年它被改造成带新壕沟的文艺复兴式要塞，随后充作军团兵营；半岛战争的两次围城中，法军的炮击把伊斯兰时期的殿堂轰成了露天废墟。

en:
Tradition reads the plan of El Escorial as a gridiron. Philip II ordered the house after his army defeated the French at Saint-Quentin on 10 August 1557, the feast of Saint Lawrence, and the foundation charter dedicated it to that saint, martyred in Rome on a grill; the rectangular plan, with the royal block projecting like a handle,. It lies at the foot of Mount Abantos in the Sierra de Guadarrama, forty-five kilometres northwest of Madrid, a grey grid of granite and slate on a bare hillside. Philip also meant it as a family pantheon under Charles V's will, burying his new dynasty apart from the old Trastamara sites, and as a house of learning for the Counter-Reformation. The first stone was laid in 1563. Juan Bautista de Toledo, who had worked on Saint Peter's in Rome, designed it until his death, and his pupil Juan de Herrera took over; the works were finished in 1584. 'The work of El Escorial' became a Spanish byword for a job that never ends.

Monastery, palace, basilica, school and library shared a single facade. Hieronymite monks kept the offices while Philip's ambassadors bought manuscripts across his empire and beyond; some four hundred books banned by the Inquisition were kept locked there for experts alone, and about 7,500 relics were housed in 570 cases. Philip governed from the Escorial in his last years and died there in 1598, and most kings of Spain from Charles V onward were buried in its Royal Pantheon. A fire in 1671 destroyed 5,280 codices, though the hall of printed books was saved. During the Peninsular War French troops sacked the monastery and expelled the monks.
zh:
相传埃斯科里亚尔修道院的平面是一只烤架。1557年8月10日圣洛伦索瞻礼日，腓力二世的军队在圣康坦击败法军，他为此下令修建这座修道院；建院特许状把它奉献给在罗马被放在烤架上炙烤殉道的圣洛伦索，矩形平面加上突出如柄的王宫部分，被认为是这位圣徒的烤架。修道院坐落在瓜达拉马山的阿万托斯山麓、马德里西北约45公里处，光秃的山坡上立着一片花岗岩与板岩砌成的灰色方整建筑。腓力还要按卡洛斯五世的遗愿把它建成家族陵寝，让新王朝脱离特拉斯塔马拉家族的旧墓地另葬一处，并使它成为反宗教改革的学术之所。1563年奠基，曾参与罗马圣彼得大教堂工程的胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·托莱多主持设计，他去世后由弟子胡安·德·埃雷拉接手；1584年完工。西班牙语后来有句俗话：「埃斯科里亚尔的工程」，指一件做不完的事。

修道院、王宫、大殿、学校和图书馆共用一道外墙：赫罗尼莫会修士主持宗教事务，腓力派驻各地的使节为图书馆在帝国境内外搜购抄本；约400册被宗教裁判所查禁的书锁在馆中，只许专家翻阅，全院还藏有约7500件圣物，分装在570具圣物箱里。腓力二世晚年在此理政，1598年死在这里，自卡洛斯五世起的西班牙国王大多葬于院中王家陵寝。1671年大火烧毁5280册抄本，印刷本大厅幸而保住。半岛战争期间法军洗劫修道院、驱逐修士。

en:
The Alhambra takes its name from al-Hamra, the red one, after the reddish rammed earth of its walls on the Sabika hill above Granada. In 1444 it was a palace-city on its own: at least six royal palaces, a Friday mosque, baths, workshops and a tannery, watered by an acequia that came down from the Generalife slopes, partly through tunnels cut in the bedrock, and ran in open channels through the courts. The sultan received embassies in the Hall of Ambassadors, a chamber 18 metres high inside the Comares Tower, beneath a wooden ceiling of 8,017 interlocking pieces laid out as the seven heavens.

In the Court of the Lions twelve marble lions ring a fountain whose basin carries a poem by the vizier-poet Ibn Zamrak, and one of the halls beside it has a darker story. Tradition says that the father of Boabdil invited the chiefs of the Abencerrajes to a banquet there and had them massacred. The Nasrid motto is carved across the walls again and again: 'No victor but God.'

After the surrender of 1492 Ferdinand and Isabella lived in the Alhambra until May, and on 31 March they signed the edict expelling the Jews who would not convert, known as the Alhambra Decree. In 1590 a gunpowder magazine exploded beside the Palace of the Lions and shattered one of its muqarnas ceilings, replaced with a Baroque vault before a visit by Philip V in 1714. The Tendilla family had governed the palace for generations; Philip V dismissed its marquis in 1718, royal money dried up after that, and the rooms passed to self-serving governors, prisoners and squatters.
zh:
阿尔罕布拉宫的名字来自阿拉伯语「哈姆拉」，意思是红色，因为萨比卡丘上的围墙用发红的夯土筑成，高踞格拉纳达之上。1444年，这里是一座自成一体的宫城：至少六座王宫、一座聚礼清真寺、浴室、作坊和鞣皮作坊；一条引水渠从赫内拉利费一带把水引来，部分水道凿在基岩隧洞里，再顺着庭院中的明渠流淌。苏丹在使节厅接见来使，这座18米高的方厅位于科马斯塔中，顶上8017块木件相扣，拼成象征七重天的藻井。

狮子庭院里，十二尊大理石狮子环着喷泉，泉沿刻着维齐尔诗人伊本·扎姆拉克的诗句；旁边一厅还带着血腥的传说。相传博阿布迪尔的父亲邀阿本塞拉赫斯家族的首领赴宴，在席间将他们尽数诛杀。墙上反复刻着纳斯里德王朝的格言：「除真主外，绝无战胜者」。

1492年受降后，斐迪南和伊莎贝拉在宫中住到5月；3月31日，他们签署敕令，驱逐不肯改宗的犹太人，后世称《阿尔罕布拉宫敕令》。1590年，狮子宫旁一座火药库爆炸，震碎了一厅的钟乳石顶棚，1714年费利佩五世来访前才换成巴洛克拱顶。滕迪利亚家族世代掌管宫务，1718年费利佩五世撤了其侯爵的官职；此后王室拨款枯竭，宫室落入中饱私囊的地方长官、囚犯和占住者手中。

en:
Tucked under a western turret of the Belem Tower is a gargoyle in the shape of a rhinoceros, carved from the beast an Indian ruler sent Manuel I in 1515, the same animal Durer made famous in his Nuremberg woodcut. The tower stands at the point where the Tagus narrows into Lisbon's harbour. John II had wanted a fort there to close the river bar, and Manuel I took the plan up: work began in 1514 under the military architect Francisco de Arruda. Raised of pale lioz limestone on a basalt islet lapped by the river, it pairs a low gunned bastion with a thirty-metre keep, and nearly every stone carries the age's signature: twisted ropes and knots, armillary spheres, the crosses of the Order of Christ, and domed corner turrets borrowed from Moorish building. A fleet home from India met this tower first at the river mouth, and it served as Lisbon's ceremonial sea gate.

Its own guns decided very little. When the Duke of Alba invaded in 1580, the small garrison surrendered after a few hours; under Spanish rule the bastion's powder rooms became dungeons, and political prisoners were held there for generations. From 1655 the tower doubled as a customs post, and every ship entering the Tagus had to pay duty beneath its walls. French detachments were quartered in it through the Peninsular War. After they withdrew, Lord Beresford judged the bastion walls too low for the new range of artillery and asked for stronger batteries beside them.
zh:
贝伦塔西角楼下藏着一尊犀牛形滴水嘴，原型是1515年一位印度君主送给曼努埃尔一世的犀牛，正是丢勒在纽伦堡制成木刻、传遍欧洲的那一头。塔立在塔霍河收窄、进入里斯本港的位置。若昂二世早想在此修一座堡垒封住河口沙洲，曼努埃尔一世接手了这个计划：1514年由军事建筑师弗朗西斯科·德·阿鲁达动工。塔身用浅色利奥兹石灰岩砌在一座被河水环绕的玄武岩小岛上，下部是低矮的炮垒，上部是30米高的主楼，几乎每块石头都带着那个年代的印记：绞绳纹和绳结、浑天仪、基督骑士团的十字，角楼上带穹顶的小哨塔则借自摩尔式建筑。从印度返航的船队到河口最先遇见的就是这座塔，它也充当里斯本的礼仪海门。

它自己的火炮没决定过多少事。1580年阿尔瓦公爵率军来犯，小小的守军几小时后便投降；西班牙人统治时期，炮垒的火药库改成地牢，政治犯一关就是几代人。1655年起，贝伦塔又兼作海关，每艘进塔霍河的船都要在墙下缴税。半岛战争期间，法国部队驻扎塔中。法军撤走后，贝雷斯福德勋爵认为炮垒的墙太矮，挡不住新射程的火炮，要求在旁边加固炮台。

en:
On the chalk of Salisbury Plain stands a ring of about thirty upright sarsens, each some four metres high and twenty-five tons heavy, once capped by lintels pegged in place with mortise-and-tenon joints. Inside, five free-standing trilithons make a horseshoe opening towards the midsummer sunrise, and among them stand smaller bluestones quarried in the Preseli Hills of Wales, more than two hundred kilometres away. The monument was raised in stages between roughly 3100 and 1600 BC. Medieval England had a better story. Geoffrey of Monmouth gave it: the stones were the Giants' Dance, which giants had brought from a mountain in Ireland for their healing virtue, and Merlin moved them across the sea and set them up as a memorial to the British nobles treacherously slain by Hengist. By 1444 it was a half-ruined riddle on the grazing down.

No one answered the riddle much better in the centuries that followed. In 1620 the Duke of Buckingham had a pit dug in the centre to see what lay beneath, and James I set Inigo Jones to make the first measured survey; Jones judged it a Roman temple. John Aubrey found the ring of fifty-six pits in 1666 and guessed the Druids had built it. From 1719 William Stukeley surveyed the stones each summer, worked out the solstice alignment and made the Druid story long-lived. Sheep grazed among the leaning pillars, and in 1797 one of the great trilithons toppled; labourers in the fields half a mile off felt the ground shake.
zh:
索尔兹伯里平原的白垩地上立着一圈约三十根萨尔森巨石，每根高约4米、重约25吨，顶上原横架石楣，以榫头卯眼相接。圈内有五座独立的三石牌坊，排成马蹄形，开口正对夏至日出；其间立着较小的青石，产自二百多公里外威尔士的普雷塞利山。巨石阵从约公元前3100年起分几个阶段修成，至约公元前1600年停工。中世纪的英格兰有更动听的说法，出自蒙茅斯的杰弗里：这些石头本是「巨人之舞」，巨人因它有疗病之效把它从爱尔兰一座山中搬来，梅林又将石头跨海运到此地，立为被亨吉斯特谋害的不列颠王公的纪念碑。到1444年，它是牧场上一座半塌的谜。

此后几百年里，没有人把这个谜解得更明白。1620年，白金汉公爵在石阵中央挖了个坑，想看底下埋着什么；詹姆士一世随即命伊尼戈·琼斯做第一次精确测绘，琼斯断定它是罗马人的神庙。1666年，约翰·奥布里发现了那圈五十六个坑穴，猜测巨石阵出自德鲁伊之手。1719年起，威廉·斯蒂克利每年夏天都来测绘，测出主轴线对准夏至日出，也让德鲁伊之说流传了很久。羊群在倾斜的石柱间吃草；1797年，一座大三石牌坊倒塌，半英里外田里干活的雇工都感到了地面震动。

en:
In 1252 the king of Norway sent Henry III a polar bear, and it spent its days at the Tower of London fishing in the Thames on the end of a long chain; Louis IX of France later sent an elephant. The Tower began as the White Tower, begun in 1078 for William the Conqueror under Gundulf, bishop of Rochester, the first stone keep in England, raised against the Roman city wall beside the river. Later kings wrapped it in two concentric rings of walls and a flooded moat and added St Thomas's Tower with the water gate later called Traitors' Gate. By the fifteenth century it was armoury, treasury, mint, record office, royal residence and zoo at once, and from the early fourteenth century kings lodged in it for several nights before their coronation and rode in procession to Westminster.

It was a prison too. In 1483 the twelve-year-old Edward V and his younger brother were lodged here and never seen again. Anne Boleyn, Margaret Pole, Catherine Howard and the sixteen-year-old Lady Jane Grey died on Tower Green, a privilege that spared them the crowd on Tower Hill, where 112 people were beheaded over four centuries. The future Elizabeth I spent two months under arrest here in 1554. Walter Raleigh kept rooms in the Bloody Tower and wrote his History of the World there; released for a last voyage to Guiana, he went back to the block in 1618. The boldest attempt on the Crown Jewels came in 1671, when an Irish adventurer named Thomas Blood, disguised as a parson, bound the keeper, flattened the crown with a mallet and nearly carried it out. Charles II pardoned him and granted him Irish lands worth 500 pounds a year. The last beheading on Tower Hill was that of Simon Fraser, Lord Lovat, in 1747, after the Jacobite rising.
zh:
1252年，挪威国王送给亨利三世一头北极熊，它在伦敦塔里拴着长链，每天在泰晤士河里捉鱼；后来法兰西的路易九世又送来一头大象。伦敦塔的起点是白塔，1078年征服者威廉下令动工，由罗切斯特主教贡杜夫监造，是英格兰第一座石砌主楼，借泰晤士河畔的罗马城墙而起。后来的国王又在白塔外围加上两圈同心城墙和一道灌满水的护城河，并建起圣托马斯塔，即后来所称的「叛徒门」水门。到15世纪，伦敦塔同时是军械库、国库、造币厂、档案馆、王宫和兽苑；从14世纪初起，历代国王加冕前都在塔里住上几夜，再列队前往威斯敏斯特。

它也是监狱。1483年，十二岁的爱德华五世和弟弟被安置进塔，之后再没有人见过他们。安妮·博林、玛格丽特·波尔、凯瑟琳·霍华德和十六岁的简·格雷郡主死在塔内绿地上，这是一种恩典，免得被塔山的围观民众看见；四百年间另有112人在塔山被斩首。1554年，后来的伊丽莎白一世曾在此被关押两个月。沃尔特·雷利在血塔中有自己的房间，他的《世界史》就写于狱中；他为最后一次圭亚那远航获释，回来后仍在1618年被处决。1671年，爱尔兰冒险家托马斯·布拉德扮成牧师前来，捆住看守，用锤子把王冠砸扁，差点带走；查理二世赦免了他，还赐给他每年值五百英镑的爱尔兰土地。塔山最后一次斩首是在詹姆斯党起事之后：1747年，洛瓦特勋爵西蒙·弗雷瑟人头落地。

en:
Edinburgh Castle sits on the plug of an extinct volcano, a dolerite crag 130 metres high with cliffs on three sides and one easy slope up from the east. The garrison's standing worry was water, for basalt sheds rain; a well was driven thirty-four metres down and still ran dry during a long siege. A royal castle has stood on the rock since the eleventh century, and David I's St Margaret's Chapel is the oldest building in the city. In the fifteenth century it was Scotland's chief arsenal as well as a royal residence, and the bronze guns Robert Borthwick cast here included a set called the Seven Sisters, whose finish English officers praised after capturing them.

Mary, Queen of Scots, gave birth to James VI in the palace on 19 June 1566. Five years later the rock faced its hardest test, the Lang Siege of 1571 to 1573, when Sir William Kirkcaldy of Grange held it for the exiled queen with forty cannon and seven gunners and bombarded the town below. In May 1573 a thousand English troops with twenty-seven guns brought from Berwick battered the walls, and the garrison surrendered as its water gave out. Most of the medieval castle perished in that bombardment, and the Half Moon Battery rose over the ruins of David's Tower.

The Honours of Scotland, the crown, sceptre and sword, were kept in the palace vault. In 1651, as Cromwell advanced, they went to Dunnottar in wool sacks; Christian Fletcher, the Kinneff minister's wife, smuggled them out and buried them under her kirk until the king returned. Cromwell's men took the rock after a three-month siege. After the Union the Honours were sealed in a chest in the Crown Room, and in 1818 Walter Scott broke the seals and found all three inside; they went back on show at a shilling a head.
zh:
爱丁堡城堡坐落在一座死火山的岩颈上：130米高的辉绿岩崖三面绝壁，只有东坡一条缓路可上。守军常年的难题是水：玄武岩留不住雨水，一口井深达34米，围城日久仍会见底。11世纪起岩上就有王室城堡，大卫一世所建的圣玛格丽特礼拜堂是全城最古老的建筑。15世纪这里既是王宫，也是苏格兰最重要的军械库，铸炮师罗伯特·博思韦克在此铸造的青铜炮中有一组名为「七姊妹」，英军缴获后，连英国军官都称赞它们做工精良。

1566年6月19日，苏格兰女王玛丽在宫中生下詹姆士六世。五年后，岩堡迎来最严酷的考验，即1571至1573年的「长围」：威廉·柯卡尔迪·格兰奇爵士为流亡的女王据守，四十门炮只有七个炮手，还向山下城区开炮。1573年5月，一千名英军带着从贝里克调来的二十七门大炮猛轰城墙，守军饮水耗尽，终于出降。中世纪城堡大半毁于这场炮战，半月炮台建在大卫塔的残基之上。

苏格兰王权仪仗（王冠、权杖和宝剑）收藏在王宫拱顶库房。1651年克伦威尔推进时，仪仗藏在羊毛袋里送往邓诺塔，金内夫牧师的妻子克里斯蒂安·弗莱彻又把它偷运出来，埋在自己教堂的地板下，直到国王回国。克伦威尔的军队则用三个月围城拿下了岩堡。联合之后，仪仗被封存在王冠室的柜子里，1818年沃尔特·司各特打开封印，在柜中找到全部三件；重新展出时，门票一先令。

en:
The Kraków Cloth Hall began as two facing rows of cloth stalls in the middle of the Main Market, with a covered street between them that could be locked at both ends after dark. Bolesław V promised stone stalls in the 1257 town charter, and the passage received its roof around 1300. Before 1358 Casimir III replaced it with a Gothic hall 108 metres long and ten metres wide. Two rows of stalls, each 7.5 metres deep, ran along the central hall, and eighteen vaulted booths opened onto it through pointed or round-arched doorways. In 1444 eastern merchants brought spices, silk, leather and wax into this passage, while Kraków dealers sent out cloth, lead and salt from Wieliczka.

Fire destroyed the Gothic hall in 1555, and the city rebuilt it within four years. Master Pankracy gave the long interior a barrel vault, Santi Gucci designed the Renaissance attic, arcaded and crowned with a row of carved mascarons, and Jan Maria Padovano added columned loggias. In 1601 workmen cut a transverse passage through the building, turning the old straight market lane into a cross-shaped thoroughfare inside the hall. When Józef Poniatowski's forces briefly took Kraków in 1809, a ball was held in the Cloth Hall for the prince and his officers.
zh:
克拉科夫纺织会馆最初只是主市场中央两排相对的布摊，中间夹着一条有顶的商业街，入夜后两端可以上锁。1257年博莱斯瓦夫五世颁发设城特许状，承诺修建石质布摊；约1300年，通道加上了屋顶。1358年以前，卡齐米日三世把它改建成一座长108米、宽10米的哥特大殿。中央大厅两侧各有深7.5米的摊位带，18个带拱顶的铺位经尖拱或半圆拱门洞朝向大厅。1444年，东方商人把香料、丝绸、皮革和蜂蜡带进这条通道，克拉科夫商人则向外运出呢绒、铅和维利奇卡盐。

1555年大火烧毁哥特会馆，城市四年内重建。匠师潘克拉齐为长厅加上筒形拱顶，圣蒂·古奇设计了文艺复兴式阿提卡墙，墙上有拱券分格，顶端排着一列怪面雕饰，扬·马里亚·帕多瓦诺则增建柱廊。1601年，工匠又横向凿穿会馆，把原来笔直的市场巷道变成建筑内部的十字通道。1809年约泽夫·波尼亚托夫斯基的军队短暂夺取克拉科夫后，人们就在纺织会馆为这位亲王和他的军官举行舞会。

en:
Prague Castle runs for some 570 metres along the hilltop above the Vltava, and its centre is St Vitus Cathedral, where the kings of Bohemia were crowned and buried. When Prague became an archbishopric in 1344, King John laid the foundation stone of a new Gothic minster. Matthias of Arras, summoned from Avignon, planned a French cathedral after Amiens and died with only the east end of the choir built. Peter Parler, twenty-three years old, took over the lodge and worked the stone like sculpture: the busts on the triforium show the royal family, the bishops and the two master builders, Parler among them. His St Wenceslas Chapel is sheathed below in more than 1,300 semi-precious stones around paintings of the Passion, and a door with seven locks leads to the crown jewels. After the Hussite wars stopped the work and a fire gutted the castle in 1541, the minster ended for nearly three centuries in a provisional wall under a timber roof, where the nave should have been.

Below the castle, the Charles Bridge carries the old coronation road across the river. Legend says that Charles IV, a believer in numerology, laid the first stone himself at 5.31 on the morning of 9 July 1357: written out as digits, 135797531 reads the same in both directions, and the emperor held that such a number would make the bridge strong. It was finished in 1402, runs 516 metres on sixteen arches between three bridge towers, and for more than four centuries was the only fixed crossing of the Vltava at Prague. In 1621, after the White Mountain, the severed heads of the executed rebel leaders were fixed to the Old Town bridge tower as a warning. In 1648 Swedish troops who held the Lesser Town bank fought their way onto the bridge and were stopped there. Around 1700 thirty baroque statues of saints went up along the parapet.
zh:
布拉格历史中心以城堡为冠。布拉格城堡沿伏尔塔瓦河畔的山脊绵延约五百七十米，核心是圣维特大教堂，波希米亚国王在这里加冕，也葬在这里。1344年布拉格升为大主教区，国王约翰为新建的哥特式大教堂奠基。从阿维尼翁召来的阿拉斯的马提亚斯（Matthias of Arras）以亚眠大教堂为蓝本设计法式教堂，去世时只建起唱诗班席的东端。二十三岁的彼得·帕尔莱日（Peter Parler）接掌石匠作坊，把石料当雕塑来做：楼廊上的半身像刻着王室成员、主教和两位总建筑师，帕尔莱日本人也在其中。他建的圣瓦茨拉夫礼拜堂，下半部墙面镶嵌一千三百多块半宝石，环绕着耶稣受难组画，一扇配七把锁的小门通往王冠珍宝。胡斯战争使工程中断，1541年大火又烧毁城堡大片建筑，此后近三百年，大教堂西端只以临时墙封堵，本该建中殿的地方盖着木屋顶。

城堡脚下，查理大桥载着旧日的加冕大道跨过伏尔塔瓦河。相传笃信数字术的查理四世亲手放下第一块基石，时间是1357年7月9日清晨5时31分：把数字连起来是135797531，正读反读都一样，皇帝认为这样的数字能让大桥坚固。桥1402年完工，长五百一十六米，十六个桥拱，三座桥头塔拱卫，此后四个多世纪里是布拉格唯一的固定过河通道。1621年白山战败后，被处死的叛乱首领的头颅悬挂在老城桥塔上示众。1648年，占据小城河岸的瑞典军队冲上大桥，被阻击在桥上。约1700年，三十尊巴洛克圣徒像沿栏杆立起。

en:
Trakai Castle stands on an island in Lake Galvė, west of Vilnius, built of red Gothic brick with stone kept for the foundations and the upper walls. Kęstutis began the stone fortress in the second half of the fourteenth century, and Teutonic troops badly damaged it in 1377. After Vytautas recovered Trakai in 1392, the second building campaign lasted to about 1409, and during a truce the Order's own stonemason Radike supervised the work. A six-storey keep 35 metres high guarded the southern side with movable gates, chapel and lodgings. Beyond it lay the Ducal Palace around a courtyard, its 10-by-21-metre great hall second only to the hall in Vilnius Upper Castle. The walls were 2.5 metres thick, with corner towers, a gatehouse and a narrow boat moat between palace and bailey.

After Grunwald removed the Teutonic threat, the island became less a frontier fort than a decorated residence, with frescoes in the palace and foreign envoys received in its hall. A visitor who saw it in 1414, Guillebert de Lannoy, described a castle 'completely new, built from bricks following French pattern'. Vytautas died there in October 1430, while the papers for his Lithuanian coronation were held at the Polish border. In 1444 it was the brick ducal seat of the young Casimir IV, and the archive of the grand duchy, the Lithuanian Metrica, was kept on the island for decades. Later rulers used parts of it as a prison, and Sigismund Augustus had the interiors remodelled in Renaissance style for short summer stays. The Muscovite war of the 1650s left the castle damaged and without repair; by the later seventeenth century the brick towers were ruins above the lake.
zh:
特拉凯城堡立在维尔纽斯以西加尔瓦湖的一座岛上，用红色哥特砖砌成，只在地基和墙体上部使用石块。14世纪后半叶，科斯图提斯在岛上动工修建石砌要塞，1377年条顿骑士团的进攻使它严重受损。1392年维陶塔斯收复特拉凯后，第二轮工程持续到约1409年，休战期间监工的竟是骑士团自己的石匠拉德克。南侧立起一座35米高的六层主楼，设有可升降闸门、小堂和住所。主楼连接围着内院的公爵宫，宫中10米宽、21米长的公爵厅，规模仅次于维尔纽斯上城堡的大厅。城墙厚达2.5米，配有角楼、门楼，宫殿与外堡之间还有一道只容小船通过的窄壕。

格伦瓦尔德战役解除条顿威胁后，这座湖心岛更多成了装饰一新的王公住所，宫中绘有湿壁画，外国使节在大厅受接见。1414年，吉勒贝尔·德·拉努瓦见到一座「全新的砖筑城堡，依照法式样式建造」。1430年10月，维陶塔斯在堡中去世，为他运送立陶宛国王加冕文书的队伍仍被阻在波兰边境。1444年，这里是年轻的卡齐米日四世的砖石公爵驻地，立陶宛大公国的档案也在岛上存放了几十年。后来的统治者把部分建筑用作监狱，齐格蒙特·奥古斯特还曾按文艺复兴风格重装内部，短期来此度夏。17世纪50年代的莫斯科战争使城堡受损，之后没有再修；到17世纪后期，湖面上只剩残破的砖塔。

en:
