The Kiev Pechersk Lavra began as a hole in a hillside. In 1051 Anthony, a monk back from Mount Athos, dug himself a cell in the Berestov bank above the Dnieper. Disciples gathered, and when twelve men lived in the cave they cut a church into the earth; Anthony then moved to a neighbouring hill and opened a second set of caves. Theodosius of Kursk brought in the Studite rule, kept a hospice for the blind and the lame on a tenth of the house's income and sent a cart of bread to the prisoners every Saturday. The stone Dormition Cathedral was consecrated in 1089, its frescoes and mosaics by painters summoned from Constantinople. Dead monks were laid in niches along the cave corridors, and Lithuanian and Ruthenian princes, among them Konstanty Ostrogski, victor of Orsha, asked to be buried in the same ground. Pilgrims stooped through the low passages to venerate the relics of the monastery's saints.

Raiders sacked the lavra again and again, the Mongols in 1240 among them, and Tatars burned it in the fifteenth century. Under Polish rule the revived monastery held out against the Union of Brest with the backing of the Ostrogski princes. The preacher Joannicius Galiatovsky recorded a legend: during a Polish siege of the hill in 1630, the Mother of God turned a rain of fire on the besiegers and the monks were saved. Hetman Ivan Mazepa paid for new fortifications and baroque rebuilding around 1700. Above the whole ensemble rises the Great Bell Tower, four tiers 96.5 metres high, built in 1731-1745 for Johann Gottfried Schadel, the tallest free-standing bell tower then built; its first great bell was cast by Ivan Motorin, who went on to cast the Tsar Bell in Moscow. Orthodox travellers held that a pilgrimage to Kiev outweighed the journey to Jerusalem, and the lavra boiled the chrism used in churches all across the Russian Empire.
zh:
基辅洞窟大修道院起初只是山坡上的一个洞。1051年，安东尼从阿索斯山修行归来，在第聂伯河高岸的别列斯托夫山岸凿出一间修室。门徒渐聚，住到十二人时，众人在洞里凿出一座教堂；安东尼后来另择邻近山冈开出新洞。库尔斯克的费奥多西引入斯图狄乌斯会规，以修道院十分之一的收入收容盲人和跛者，每周六还给囚犯送一车面包。石造安息大教堂1089年祝圣，壁画和马赛克出自君士坦丁堡请来的匠人。去世的修士葬在洞道两侧的壁龛里，立陶宛和鲁塞尼亚的王公也求葬于此，其中包括奥尔沙之战的胜者康斯坦丁·奥斯特罗格斯基。朝圣者躬身穿过低矮的通道，敬拜修道院圣徒的圣骸。

修道院一次次遭劫，1240年的蒙古人只是其中之一，15世纪鞑靼人又纵火焚院。波兰统治时期，复兴的修道院靠奥斯特罗格斯基王公家族支持，顶住了布列斯特联合带来的压力。传教士约阿尼基·加利亚托夫斯基记下一则传说：1630年波兰军队围攻山冈，圣母降下火雨打向围攻者，修士得救。盖特曼伊万·马泽帕出资修筑新的防御工事，约1700年按巴洛克风格改建。大钟楼凌驾于整个修道院之上，约翰·戈特弗里德·谢德尔设计，1731至1745年建成，四层、高96.5米，是当时世界上最高的独立钟楼；第一口大钟由伊凡·莫托林铸成，他后来又为莫斯科铸了沙皇钟。东正教信众认为，赴基辅朝圣比远赴耶路撒冷更值得；修道院还为全俄各地的教堂熬制圣油。

en:
In the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries the Kremlin walls were whitewashed, so that the citadel of that age looked white rather than brick-red. It stands on Borovitsky Hill, where the Neglinnaya stream ran into the Moskva, and its walls enclose 27.5 hectares, five palaces and four cathedrals. In 1444 the hill still held the white-stone fortress of the grand princes; within forty years Ivan III had rebuilt it. Pietro Antonio Solari of Milan designed the brick walls and towers, and the Spassky Gate keeps a Latin inscription praising him. Fioravanti's Dormition Cathedral became the coronation church of the tsars, with Ivan IV the first crowned there in 1547, and the emperors came back to it for their coronations even after the court moved to Saint Petersburg. The Ivan the Great Bell Tower, built beside it, was long the tallest building in Muscovite Russia.

Two giant curiosities stand in the grounds. The Tsar Cannon was cast in bronze in 1586 by Andrei Chokhov, a bombard of unmatched calibre that was never fired in war; Voltaire joked that the Kremlin's two marvels were a cannon never fired and a bell never rung. The Tsar Bell was the third of its line. The first, cast in 1600, needed twenty-four men to swing its clapper, and the second burned. Ivan and Mikhail Motorin cast the two-hundred-ton successor in the 1730s, and when fire reached the Kremlin in 1737 it was still in its casting pit. Cold water thrown to save it split the metal, an eleven-ton slab broke off, and the bell lay in the pit for the rest of the century.

Catherine II let Vasily Bazhenov pull down a stretch of the wall and several old churches for a colossal palace, then called the work off for its cost. Napoleon held the Kremlin from 2 September to 11 October 1812 and had it mined on his retreat. The blasts shattered towers and the Arsenal, but rain soaked the fuses and most of the churches survived.
zh:
整个18世纪到19世纪初，莫斯科克里姆林宫的城墙都刷成白色，那时的城塞看上去是白的，而不是砖红色。它建在博罗维茨山上，涅格林纳亚河曾在此汇入莫斯科河，城墙围出二十七公顷半的地方，里面有五座宫殿和四座大教堂。1444年，山上还是大公们的白石堡垒；不到四十年，伊凡三世把它重建了一遍。米兰人皮埃特罗·安东尼奥·索拉里设计了砖墙和塔楼，斯帕斯卡亚塔门上保留着称颂他的拉丁文铭刻。菲奥拉万蒂所建的圣母升天大堂是历代沙皇加冕之处，1547年伊凡四世第一个在此加冕；宫廷迁往圣彼得堡以后，历代皇帝仍要回到这里加冕。旁边的伊凡大帝钟楼，长期是全俄最高的建筑。

城圈之内还有两件庞然大物。沙皇炮1586年由安德烈·乔霍夫以青铜铸成，口径之大无出其右，却从未在战争中发射；伏尔泰打趣说，克里姆林宫有两样奇物，一门从没响过的炮和一口从没响过的钟。沙皇钟是同一系列的第三口：1600年铸的头一口要二十四人合力才拉得动钟舌，第二口毁于火灾；伊凡·莫托林和米哈伊尔·莫托林父子18世纪30年代铸出两百吨重的新钟，1737年克里姆林宫失火时它还在铸坑里。救火的冷水激裂了钟体，一块十一吨重的裂片脱落，此后整个世纪它都躺在坑中。

叶卡捷琳娜二世听任瓦西里·巴热诺夫为一座宏大的新宫拆去一段城墙和几座老教堂，工程终因耗资过巨作罢。1812年9月2日至10月11日，拿破仑占据克里姆林宫，撤退时派人布雷；爆炸毁掉塔楼和军火库，雨水却浸湿了引信，多数教堂保住了。

en:
The tale is told everywhere that Ivan IV had the builder of this cathedral blinded so that he could never raise anything to match it. The chronicles give the builder only as 'Barma and company', and the master named Postnik Yakovlev worked on the walls and towers of the Kazan Kremlin afterwards, so historians mostly treat the blinding as legend. The cathedral is the brick church on Red Square, built between the Kremlin wall and the old moat in 1555-1561 to mark Ivan's conquest of Kazan and Astrakhan. Its proper name is the Cathedral of the Intercession of the Most Holy Theotokos on the Moat, and it replaced a white-stone Trinity church that stood in the middle of the market place. Each victory of the Kazan war fell on a different saint's feast, and for each Ivan put up a wooden memorial church beside Trinity until seven of them stood there. The stone cathedral gathered the cluster into nine chapels on one platform, eight around a tall central church of the Intercession. A victory church outside the Kremlin walls, facing the merchant posad, was something new in Muscovy.

The popular name came in 1588, when a tenth chapel was raised over the grave of Vasily the Blessed, a Muscovite fool-for-Christ who went naked through the city and spoke his mind even to the tsar. He was canonised when the chapel was built, and Muscovites gave his name to the whole cathedral. On Palm Sunday the patriarch and the tsar held their procession here, and the church stood for the Temple of Jerusalem. In the 1680s the nine separate churches were bound into one building by enclosed galleries and a new tent-roofed belfry, and the domes received their first colours. The great fire of 1737 badly damaged the church. In 1812 Napoleon's men stabled horses in it and stripped what they could carry, but it escaped both the Moscow fire and an order to blow it up.
zh:
到处都在讲，伊凡四世弄瞎了圣瓦西里大教堂的建造者，免得他再造出能与之媲美的建筑。编年史只把建造者记作「巴尔马及其同伴」，而名叫波斯特尼克·雅科夫列夫的匠师此后又参与修筑喀山克里姆林宫的城墙和塔楼，所以史家多把刺目之说当作传闻。这座砖造大堂在红场上，1555至1561年建于克里姆林宫城墙与旧护城河之间，纪念伊凡攻灭喀山和阿斯特拉罕。它的正式名称是护城河边圣母帡幪大堂，原址是市集中央一座白石三一教堂。喀山战事的每次胜利都赶上不同圣徒的纪念日，伊凡便命人在三一教堂旁添一座木制还愿教堂，最后攒下七座；新建的石造大堂把这群小教堂收成九座圣堂，立在同一个台基上，八座环绕中央高耸的帡幪堂。把胜利教堂建在克里姆林宫外、面朝商人城关，在莫斯科是前所未有的事。

教堂的俗名得于1588年，这年圣愚瓦西里墓上添了第十座小堂。瓦西里是莫斯科的「为基督装疯」的圣愚，赤身行走在街头，对沙皇也直言不讳；小堂建成时他受封为圣徒，市民便把他的名字给了整座大堂。每年棕枝主日，牧首和沙皇的游行行列到此，这座教堂象征耶路撒冷圣殿。17世纪80年代，九座各自独立的教堂被围廊和新建的帐篷顶钟楼连成一体，穹顶也开始饰上色彩。1737年大火重创教堂。1812年拿破仑的士兵在堂中养马、掠走可搬动的器物，但它既躲过莫斯科大火，也没被按命令炸毁。

en:
Mausolus, the Persian-appointed satrap of Caria, moved his capital to Halicarnassus and died there in 353 BC. His sister and wife Artemisia II carried his tomb to completion. Later writers made much of her grief: Boccaccio says she drank Mausolus' ashes mixed in wine, and Renaissance painters liked to show her doing it. The tomb was a stepped stone podium about 45 metres high, ringed with an Ionic colonnade and capped with a pyramid roof, on which stood a four-horse chariot. Four Greek sculptors, Scopas, Leochares, Bryaxis and Timotheus, took one side each, and nearly four hundred statues stood in the precinct. Antipater of Sidon counted it among the Seven Wonders, and the Romans afterwards gave Mausolus' name to every grand tomb above ground.

It stood above the harbour for roughly sixteen centuries; Alexander's army spared it, and in the twelfth century the bishop Eustathius could still write that it 'was and is a wonder'. Earthquakes ended that. When the Knights Hospitaller arrived in 1402 to build the Castle of Saint Peter, they found ruins and treated the site as a quarry. In 1494, strengthening the castle against the Ottomans, they broke open the podium for dressed stone, burned much of the marble into lime, and set the finest relief slabs into the castle walls, where travellers saw them for another three hundred years. A knight named de La Tourette later described a stairway of twelve steps and a corridor lined with sculpture: his men admired the reliefs and then smashed them, and the retreat trumpet sounded before they could open the burial chamber. When they came back the next morning the door stood open and gold ornaments lay shattered on the floor; earlier robbers had tunneled in first. The last of the tomb was broken up in 1522, when the knights readied Bodrum for the Ottoman attack that followed the fall of Rhodes.
name_zh: 哈利卡那索斯的摩索拉斯陵墓
zh:
哈利卡那索斯的摩索拉斯陵墓是为卡里亚总督摩索拉斯修的。他由波斯任命，把都城迁到哈利卡那索斯，公元前353年在那里去世。他的姊妹兼妻子阿尔特米西亚二世主持陵墓完工。后世作家爱渲染她的悲痛：薄伽丘写道，她把摩索拉斯的骨灰调在酒里饮下，文艺复兴时期的画家也反复描绘这个场面。陵墓是层层收分的石砌台基，高约45米，立着爱奥尼柱廊，盖着金字塔形屋顶，顶上架着驷马战车。斯科帕斯、莱奥卡雷斯、布里亚西斯和提摩修斯四位希腊雕刻家各负责一面浮雕，陵区立有近四百尊圆雕。西顿的安提帕特把它列入七大奇迹，罗马人之后把一切宏伟的地上陵墓都照摩索拉斯的名字来称呼。

巨墓在海港上方矗立了约十六个世纪；亚历山大的军队没有动它，12世纪时，主教尤斯塔提乌斯仍能写下它「过去是奇迹，现在还是」。终结它的是地震。1402年医院骑士团到来修建圣彼得城堡时，看到的已是废墟，便把遗址当成采石场。1494年为抵御奥斯曼人而加固城堡，他们凿开台基取走规整条石，把大量大理石烧成石灰，又把最好的浮雕板嵌进城堡墙壁，此后三百年里旅行者都能在墙上看见。一位名叫德拉图雷特的骑士后来记述：他们发现一道十二级台阶和一条排满雕刻的甬道，先对浮雕赞叹一番，随后动手砸碎；收工号在墓室打开前吹响，次日清晨再来时，墓门已开，金器碎了一地，早有盗墓者从地道先进去过。1522年，骑士团为迎战罗得岛陷落后将至的奥斯曼攻势而加固博德鲁姆，陵墓最后的残余就在这时被拆光。

en:
In 1171 Saladin's Ayyubids overthrew the Isma'ili caliphate and made al-Azhar a Sunni mosque. The Fatimid names were stripped from the mihrab and the Shia books sold or burned; contemporaries wrote that a hill of books rose in the courtyard and soldiers soled their shoes with the fine bindings. The mosque had been the first built in the new Fatimid capital, raised by the general Jawhar al-Siqilli from Mokattam limestone and named for Fatima al-Zahra, 'the luminous one', daughter of the Prophet. In 989 the vizier Ya'qub ibn Killis turned it into a school of higher learning, with thirty-five scholars teaching Qur'an, law, grammar, logic and astronomy. The Mamluks gave it a second life: Ibn Khaldun lectured there, and the sultans Qaytbay and Qansuh al-Ghuri raised minarets above its gates. In 1444 students from across the Muslim world lodged in the riwaqs around the court and took their licence to teach from its sheikhs.

Under the Ottomans the riwaqs were divided by nationality and legal school, and a student studied about six years before his sheikh licensed him. The Mamluk amir Abd al-Rahman Katkhuda added the Gate of the Barbers, where students had their heads shaved, and the Soup Gate, where rice soup was handed out to poor scholars; in 1776 he was buried in his own mausoleum inside the mosque, the first burial there in nearly two centuries. In 1798 Napoleon's French set up a governing diwan of nine Azhar sheikhs, but three months later the Cairo revolt began from the mosque. Guns on the Citadel fired straight at it, troops entered in their boots, tied their horses to the mihrab and threw Qur'ans to the floor, and six of the ulama were put to death. After the Azhar student Suleiman al-Halabi assassinated General Kléber, the mosque was shut, and its doors stayed bolted until Ottoman and British forces arrived in 1801.
zh:
1171年，萨拉丁的艾优卜王朝推翻伊斯玛仪派哈里发，把爱资哈尔大学的前身改成逊尼派清真寺。米哈拉布上法蒂玛王朝的名字被铲掉，派内藏书或卖或焚；据当时人记述，院里堆起一座「书丘」，士兵拿精美的封皮垫鞋底。这座寺原是法蒂玛新都建起的第一座清真寺，由大将昭海尔取穆盖塔姆山的石灰岩建成，寺名取自先知之女法蒂玛的称号「宰赫拉」，意为「光辉的女子」。989年，维齐尔叶尔孤白·伊本·基利斯把它办成高等学府，聘三十五名学者讲授《古兰经》、教法、语法、逻辑和天文。让它复苏的是马穆鲁克人：伊本·赫勒敦在此讲学，苏丹盖特拜和甘苏勒·古里在各门之上添建宣礼塔。1444年，来自穆斯林各地的学生住在庭院四周的学舍里，从谢赫手中领取执教凭证。

奥斯曼时期，学舍按民族和教法学派划分，学生通常要学约六年，由谢赫认定学有所成才发凭证。马穆鲁克埃米尔阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·卡特胡达添建了「理发师门」，学生进寺前在这道门外剃头，又修了「汤门」，向贫苦学生施散米汤；1776年，他葬在寺内自己所修的陵寝里，是近两个世纪来头一个获此待遇的人。1798年，拿破仑的法国人成立由九名爱资哈尔谢赫组成的政务会，三个月后，开罗起义就从这座清真寺发起。城堡上的炮火直接向寺里轰击，士兵穿着军靴闯入，把马拴在米哈拉布上，将《古兰经》掷在地上，六名乌莱玛被处死。爱资哈尔学生苏莱曼·哈拉比刺杀克莱贝尔将军后，寺被封闭，寺门一直紧闭到1801年奥斯曼与英国军队开入开罗。

en:
Herodotus, who visited around 450 BC, was told that an inscription on the outside recorded the radishes, onions and garlic eaten by the work gangs, and that 100,000 men had laboured in three-month shifts for twenty years. The Pyramid of Cheops is the tomb of Khufu, the Fourth Dynasty pharaoh the Greeks called Cheops, probably designed by his vizier Hemiunu. Some 2.3 million blocks went into it, with granite for the inner chambers brought 800 kilometres down the Nile from Aswan and white Tura limestone sheathing its faces. At 146.6 metres it was the tallest structure raised by human hands for more than 3,700 years; with the casing stripped it measures 138.5.

Later ages forgot Khufu. Christians read the monuments as Joseph's granaries, and Arab writers told of Surid, the antediluvian king who dreamed of the Flood and packed the pyramids with Egypt's wisdom. In 832 the caliph al-Ma'mun drove a tunnel into the north face in search of that treasure and broke through to passages and an empty granite sarcophagus; the story went that he found an emerald jar of a thousand coins, just enough to cover his costs. In 1196 Saladin's son al-Aziz sent workmen to raze the pyramids and cart the stone to Damietta, and gave up within a month. Builders carried the earthquake-loosened casing into Cairo, and by the 1400s the bare core loomed over a plateau with a name for bats and hauntings.

In 1435 the Italian traveller Cyriacus of Ancona climbed the plateau with Herodotus in hand and told European readers these were royal tombs, not Joseph's storehouses. The Oxford astronomer John Greaves later measured the sides and chambers more carefully than any visitor before him, and his Pyramidographia of 1646 became the first scholarly book on the monument, though he put Khufu's reign a thousand years too early. In 1763 Nathaniel Davison, British consul at Algiers, crawled through the narrow passage at the top of the Grand Gallery into a low relieving chamber above the King's Chamber, later named for him.
zh:
公元前450年左右到访的希罗多德听当地人说，塔外刻有铭文，记着工匠吃掉的萝卜、洋葱和大蒜，又说十万人以三个月一班轮换，修了二十年。胡夫金字塔是第四王朝法老胡夫（希腊人叫他齐奥普斯）的陵墓，主持建造的很可能是他的维齐尔赫米乌努。整座塔用去约二百三十万块巨石，内部墓室用的花岗岩从八百公里外的阿斯旺顺尼罗河运来，四面坡铺着图拉出产的白色石灰岩。塔原高146.6米，保持人类最高建筑的纪录超过三千七百年；外层石被拆走后，高138.5米。

后世却把胡夫忘了。基督徒把这些塔当作「约瑟的粮仓」，阿拉伯作者则讲，洪水之前的国王苏利德梦见灭世，便把埃及的学问封进金字塔。832年，哈里发马蒙为寻这笔宝藏，从北面凿入隧道，打通甬道后只见到一具空花岗岩石棺；传说他找到一只翡翠罐，内装一千枚金币，恰好抵偿凿塔的花费。1196年，萨拉丁之子阿齐兹派工匠去拆金字塔，想把石料运去杜姆亚特，一个月便罢手。营建者把地震震松的外层石运进开罗，到15世纪，只剩石核的巨塔立在高原上，人称塔中有蝙蝠作祟、鬼魂出没。

1435年，意大利旅人奇里亚科·德·安科纳带着希罗多德的书登上吉萨高原，告诉欧洲读者这是王陵，不是约瑟的粮仓。后来牛津的天文学者约翰·格里夫斯丈量塔身边长和内部墓室，精度超过此前所有来客；他1646年出版的《金字塔志》是研究这座建筑的第一部学术著作，只是他把胡夫的在位年代算早了一千年。1763年，英国驻阿尔及尔领事纳撒尼尔·戴维森从大甬道顶端的窄道爬进国王墓室上方的一间低矮减压室，这间石室后来便以他的名字命名。

en:
The Citadel of Aleppo crowns a fifty-metre mound in the middle of the city, an oval 450 metres long and 325 wide that has been fortified since the third millennium BC. Local tradition says the prophet Ibrahim once milked his flocks on the hill, and the storm-god Hadad had a temple there when Aleppo was the capital of Yamhad. The mound was once faced throughout with dressed limestone and is girdled by a moat twenty-two metres deep, crossed by a single tall viaduct of arches. The two mosques on the crown, the Great Mosque and the Mosque of Abraham, began as Byzantine churches.

It was a royal prison in the wars with the Franks. Baldwin II of Jerusalem was held there for two years, Joscelin II of Edessa died in its cells, and Raynald of Chatillon was kept there before his release. Most of what crowns the mound is the work of Saladin's son al-Zahir Ghazi, who between 1193 and 1215 deepened the moat, threw the arched bridge across it and built the bent entrance, a vaulted ramp that turns six times under machicolations, its passages carved with figurative reliefs and threaded with secret stairs. His 'palace of glory' burned down on his wedding night and was rebuilt. Wells on the crown went down 125 metres, and tunnels ran out to the advance towers and, it was said, under the moat into the city.

Timur's army sacked the citadel in 1400, and the Mamluks rebuilt it, raising the Throne Hall above the gate; the last Mamluk sultan, al-Ashraf Qansuh al-Ghawri, replaced its flat ceiling with nine domes. When Aleppo opened its gates to the Ottomans in 1516 the citadel became an Ottoman garrison. For the next three centuries the sultans kept no court on the hill, and the Ayyubid palaces were left to soldiers, storerooms and slow decay.
zh:
阿勒颇城堡坐落在城中心一座五十米高的土丘上，丘基为椭圆形，长四百五十米、宽三百二十五米，早在公元前第三千年便已设防。当地相传先知易卜拉欣曾在这座山丘上放牧羊群、挤取羊乳；阿勒颇做亚姆哈德国都城时，风暴神哈达德的神庙也立在丘顶。山坡曾整体包着凿平的石灰岩，丘下环绕着深二十二米的壕沟，只有一座高耸的多拱引桥可以通过。丘顶的大清真寺和易卜拉欣清真寺，最初都是拜占庭人的教堂。

这里也是十字军战争中的王室牢房：耶路撒冷国王鲍德温二世被囚两年，埃德萨伯爵乔斯林二世死在堡中，沙蒂永的雷纳德获释前也关押于此。丘顶现存的建筑大半出自萨拉丁之子扎希尔·加齐之手：1193至1215年间，他加深壕沟、架起拱桥，又修出折角式大门，攻门者要在拱顶坡道上连转六道弯，头顶全是倾倒沸液的堞口，通道里刻着人物浮雕，还岔出暗藏的阶梯。他那座「荣耀宫」在新婚之夜失火焚毁，后来又重建。丘顶的水井深达一百二十五米，地道通向前方塔楼，据说还穿过壕沟通到城里。

1400年帖木儿的军队洗劫了城堡，马穆鲁克人随后重建，在城门上方盖起觐见大殿；末代马穆鲁克素丹阿什拉夫·坎苏·戈里把殿内平顶换成了九座穹顶。1516年阿勒颇向奥斯曼人开城，城堡成了奥斯曼驻军的营盘。此后三百年里素丹们再没有上山临朝，艾尤布时代的宫殿留给了士兵、库房和慢慢的朽坏。

en:
Above the door of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre a wooden ladder rests on the cornice beneath an upper window. It appears in a Franciscan engraving of 1728, and it stayed where it was because the six Christian rites that share the church had to agree before anything was moved; Ottoman firmans in the seventeenth century had already settled who held every chapel and lamp inside. The Holy City of Jerusalem is not a single building but a crowd of shrines packed into a few hundred metres of stony hill. Every Holy Saturday the Greek patriarch enters the tomb chapel and comes out carrying a flame that the crowd passes from candle to candle through the church. Muslim scholars of the tenth and eleventh centuries wrote of the rite and noted that the city's emir and qadi waited among the crowd for the light.

On the Haram al-Sharif the Dome of the Rock rises over the exposed Foundation Stone, and a few steps east stands the open-pillared Dome of the Chain, where medieval tradition set David's chain of judgement and the scales of the Last Day. In the platform's eastern wall is the Golden Gate. Jews expect the Messiah to enter by it and Christians say Jesus rode through it on Palm Sunday; in 1541 Suleiman's builders walled it up for good. Westward runs the Via Dolorosa, about 600 metres from the place of Pilate's judgement to the Sepulchre. Franciscan friars led pilgrims along it from about 1350, and its stations were fixed only in the eighteenth century.

In the winter of 1700 Judah HeHasid arrived with some 500 Ashkenazim from Poland and died within days. His followers raised a synagogue on borrowed money, and in 1721 their Arab creditors burned it down and the Ashkenazim were expelled. The empty plot was known ever after as the Hurva, the Ruin.
zh:
耶路撒冷圣墓教堂的门上方，一扇窗下的檐台上搁着一把木梯。1728年方济各会的版画里已经画着它；共用这座教堂的六派基督徒必须一致同意才能挪动任何东西，所以它一直搁在原处。17世纪奥斯曼的诏书早已裁定过堂内每一座小堂、每一盏灯归谁。耶路撒冷圣城没有哪一座建筑可指，只有几百米石山之内挤作一团的重重圣迹。每年圣周六，希腊牧首走进墓亭，手持圣火走出，人群一烛接一烛把火传遍整座教堂。10至11世纪的穆斯林学者写过这一仪式，还提到城中的埃米尔和卡迪也站在人群里等光出现。

尊贵禁地上，圆顶清真寺罩着裸露的奠基石；往东几步是以柱环绕的链圆顶，相传大卫王审断的链条立在这里，末日审判的天平也将设在此处。禁地东墙里封着金门：犹太人相信弥赛亚必从此门入城，基督徒则说耶稣棕枝主日骑驴经过此门；1541年，苏莱曼的工匠把它彻底砌死。往西是维亚多勒罗沙，即苦路，从彼拉多审判之处到圣墓教堂约600米。方济各会修士约自1350年起率朝圣者沿此路行进，现行的各处圣站则到18世纪才固定。

1700年冬，犹大·赫哈西德率约五百名阿什肯纳兹人从波兰抵达，几天后便去世。门徒借债建起一座会堂，1721年阿拉伯债主放火烧堂，阿什肯纳兹人也被逐走。那块空地此后称作胡瓦，意思是废墟。

en:
The Kaaba is the square stone house at the centre of the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, about fifteen metres high, its walls draped in black silk. Muslims believe Ibrahim and his son Ismail raised it at God's command, and that an angel brought the Black Stone fixed in its eastern corner. Every pilgrim who enters the mosque walks seven turns around it, anti-clockwise, beginning at the Black Stone, and kisses or touches it when the crowd allows.

Around 600, after fire and flood, the Quraysh rebuilt the house and quarrelled over who should set the Black Stone in place. Muhammad settled it by having the clan elders carry the stone on a cloak, then placing it with his own hands. When he took Mecca in 630 he had the 360 idols around the building broken, sparing a painting of Maryam and her son Isa. After a fire in the Umayyad siege, Caliph Abd al-Malik rebuilt the house in 693, and the cube has kept its shape ever since.

The Black Stone suffered its worst treatment in 930, when Abu Tahir al-Jannabi's Qarmatians sacked Mecca, threw pilgrims' bodies into the Zamzam and carried the stone off to al-Ahsa. The Abbasids ransomed it only in 952, and it came back broken into pieces.

From Ayyubid times the black silk covering, the kiswa, was made in Egypt, with a band of gold-embroidered Quranic verses, and travelled to Mecca with the Cairo caravan. The old cloth was cut up and sold to pilgrims, and from the fifteenth century the new one rode under a decorated camel-litter called the mahmal. Heavy rains collapsed the walls in 1626, and Murad IV had the house rebuilt that same year from Meccan granite.
zh:
天房是矗立在麦加禁寺中央的方形石殿，高约十五米，外墙常年罩着黑色丝幕。穆斯林相信，易卜拉欣和儿子易司马仪奉真主之命筑起这座殿堂，天使送来的黑石嵌在东角。每个走进禁寺的朝觐者都要逆时针绕行天房七圈，从黑石开始，人群允许时便上前亲吻或触摸它。

约600年，天房遭火灾和洪水之后由古莱什人重建，各部落为谁来安放黑石争执不下。穆罕默德让众族长把黑石托在斗篷上抬起，再亲手将它安置就位。630年他进入麦加，命人捣毁天房周围的三百六十尊偶像，唯独留下一幅麦尔彦和她儿子尔撒的画像。倭马亚人围攻麦加时天房遭焚，哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克于693年重建，立方体的形制此后再没有改动。

黑石遭受的最大劫难在930年：阿布·塔希尔·贾纳比率盖尔迈特派攻陷麦加，把朝觐者的尸体抛入渗渗泉，又将黑石劫往哈萨。阿拔斯王朝直到952年才将它赎回，送回时已碎成数块。

从阿尤布时代起，每年一袭的黑色丝质罩幕都在埃及制成，上面有金线绣成《古兰经》经文的腰带，随开罗驼队运到麦加。旧幕被割成小块卖给朝觐者，15世纪以后新幕改由装饰华丽的驼轿「迈哈米勒」随行。1626年暴雨冲毁殿墙，穆拉德四世同年用麦加花岗岩重建天房。

en:
The City of Sana'a is a wonder made of a whole walled town: 6,500 houses packed inside clay ramparts nine to fourteen metres high, entered through the Bab al-Yaman, a southern gate already more than a thousand years old. Each quarter was laid out around an endowed complex of mosque, bathhouse and kitchen garden, and the three fed one another. The houses sent their refuse down chutes to dry in the mountain air, and the dried matter fuelled the bathhouse fires, while the gardens were watered with the spent water of the ablution pools.

The houses are towers, five to eight storeys of rough stone and fired brick, edged with white gypsum in geometric friezes and pierced with windows of carved plaster and coloured glass. One extended family lived in a single tower and added a floor when a son married. Grain and animals stayed on the ground floor, and the top room, the mafraj, was the reception hall where men chewed qat of an afternoon. Below ran the Suq al-Milh, the Salt Market, trading under its timber roof in salt, spices, raisins, cotton, copper and silverware.

The coffee trade kept this city and made it denser. Ottoman governors laid out a garden suburb at Bi'r al-Azab outside the walls, the Turkish quarter first mentioned in 1627. In 1679 the imam expelled the city's Jews to the hot coast in the Mawza Exile; the survivors were let back in 1680 and given land outside the walls, where their Qa' quarter took shape. Europeans hardly ever reached the highlands, but in 1763 Carsten Niebuhr, the sole survivor of a Danish scientific expedition, was received in Sana'a by Imam al-Mahdi Abbas and carried an account of the tower city back to Europe in his published travels.
zh:
萨那城的奇观就是这座有城墙的城本身：六千五百栋房屋挤在九至十四米高的土墙之内，南门「也门门」已有上千年历史。每个街区都围绕一组宗教捐赠建筑而建，清真寺、澡堂和菜园互相供养：各家的污物顺槽而下，在山风中晾干后充作澡堂的燃料，菜园则用清真寺净身池的废水浇灌。

民宅就是塔楼：毛石与烧砖砌成的五至八层高楼，白色石膏勾出层层几何饰带，窗户雕花抹灰、嵌着彩色玻璃。一座塔楼住一个大家庭，儿子娶妻便往上添一层。底层囤粮、圈牲口，顶层的「迈夫拉杰」是客厅，男人们下午在这里嚼卡特。塔楼下是盐市，木棚下买卖食盐、香料、葡萄干、棉花、铜器和银器。

咖啡贸易兴隆的年代，萨那城的格局被保留下来，屋舍也越添越密。奥斯曼总督在墙外辟出花园郊区比尔阿扎布，这个「土耳其区」最早见于1627年的记载。1679年，伊玛目把城中的犹太人逐往炎热的沿海，史称「穆瓦扎流徙」；幸存者1680年获准回来，只得到城墙外的一块地，在那里建起盖阿街区。欧洲人极少踏进这片高原，1763年，丹麦科学考察队唯一活下来的成员卡斯滕·尼布尔获伊玛目迈赫迪·阿拔斯接见，把这座塔楼之城的见闻写进游记，带回了欧洲。

en:
Nizwa Fort is a stone drum twenty-four metres high and forty-three across, built around the deepest water in the oasis at the centre of Oman's old inland capital. A stronghold stood here from the ninth century. Imam Nasir bin Murshid had it rebuilt over the old ruins in 1625, and the second Ya'rubi imam, Sultan bin Saif, raised the present fort from about 1650, twelve years' work above a subterranean stream. The imam's armies drove the Portuguese out of Muscat and the coastal forts, and in peace the keep served as the seat of imams and governors, with courts, prisons, storerooms and a mosque within its walls.

Everything about it was made to defeat cannon. The foundations go thirty metres into the ground and the lower core is packed with rubble to soak up shot; the walls are rounded and sloping, and the doors are sheathed in thick metal. There are 480 gun-ports and twenty-four embrasures for heavy guns, and four cannon rest on the summit platform, one of them engraved with Sultan bin Saif's name.

The only way up is a single twisting stair behind a heavy wooden door studded with spikes. An attacker who forced it met shafts above every doorway for pouring boiling oil or water, and date syrup from the fort's cellars could serve instead. The dark passages hide six pitfalls closed by planks that can be pulled away. Seven wells, cisterns and underground granaries made a long blockade survivable, and the wall-walk at the top had room for 120 guards with muskets.
zh:
尼兹瓦城堡的主楼是一只石砌的巨鼓，高二十四米、直径四十三米，围着这座阿曼旧都腹地绿洲里最可靠的水源而建。9世纪起此处就有一座要塞。1625年，伊玛目纳绥尔·本·穆尔希德命人在旧堡废墟上重修；叶阿里卜朝第二任伊玛目苏丹·本·赛义夫又于1650年前后建成现存的堡垒，在地下溪流之上施工十二年。这位伊玛目的军队把葡萄牙人逐出马斯喀特和沿海堡垒；太平时节，圆塔是伊玛目和地方长官的驻地，墙内设有公堂、监狱、库房和清真寺。

它处处是为对付火炮设计的。地基深入地下三十米，塔芯下部填以碎石来吸收炮击；塔墙圆而斜，大门包着厚厚的铁皮。四百八十个枪眼和二十四个重炮射孔覆盖所有来路，塔顶平台上放着四门炮，其中一门铸有苏丹·本·赛义夫的名字。

登塔只有一条盘旋窄梯，隔着一扇钉满尖刺的厚重木门。破门而入者在每道门上方都会遭遇倾倒滚油和开水的孔洞，城堡窖里的枣浆也可以拿来代用。幽暗的通道里设有六处陷阱，铺着可以抽走的木板。七口水井、蓄水池和地下粮仓足以支撑长期围困，塔顶巡道可部署一百二十名火枪手。

en:
Agathangelos records the founding vision: a figure came down from heaven and struck the ground with a golden hammer to mark where the church was to rise. It was later understood as Christ himself, and the name Etchmiadzin means the place where the Only-Begotten descended, though that name is not found before the fifteenth century. The cathedral stands at Vagharshapat, in the vineyard country west of Yerevan, the mother church of the Armenian Apostolic Church. Tradition dates it to around 301, when Gregory the Illuminator built it over a pagan temple after King Tiridates III made Armenia the first kingdom to adopt Christianity as a state religion. The present core was raised in the fifth century after a Persian invasion: a square of four massive piers carrying a central dome.

In 1441 a council of several hundred clergy voted to bring the catholicosate back from Cilician Sis, and Catholicos Kirakos restored the church. War with the Safavids followed. In 1604 Shah Abbas I sacked Etchmiadzin while moving the border Armenians to Iran, and meant to carry the whole building to his new foundation of New Julfa near Isfahan. The cost stopped the demolition, but the altar stones, the stone where Christ was said to have descended, and the Right Arm of Gregory the Illuminator went to New Julfa and were set into the church of St Georg, built in 1611.

Later catholicoi repaired the dome and foundations, walled the monastery and added a tall belfry over the west entrance. Catholicos Simeon set up Armenia's first printing house nearby in 1770. In June 1804, during Tsitsianov's campaign against Erivan, Russian troops entered Etchmiadzin and sacked its churches before being driven back; a French envoy at the Persian court recorded the damage and set it against the shah's treatment of his Christian subjects.
zh:
史家阿加坦格洛斯记下了建堂异象：一位使者自天而降，以金锤敲击地面，标出建堂之处。后来教会认定这位使者就是基督；埃奇米阿津意为「独生子降临之地」，不过这个名字15世纪以前还看不到。主教座堂在埃里温以西葡萄之乡的瓦加尔沙帕特，是亚美尼亚使徒教会的母堂。相传它始建于301年前后：梯里达底三世把基督教立为国教，亚美尼亚成为第一个以基督教为国教的王国，启蒙者格列高利便在一座异教神庙之上建起这座教堂。现存核心部分是5世纪波斯入侵之后重建的，四根巨柱承重，托起中央穹顶。

1441年，数百名教士召开公会议，决定把大主教座从奇里乞亚的西斯迁回，基拉科斯大主教重修教堂。战祸随萨法维王朝而来：1604年，沙阿·阿拔斯一世在迁徙边境亚美尼亚人的同时洗劫埃奇米阿津，打算把整座教堂搬到他在伊斯法罕附近新建的新朱尔法。拆运耗资太大，计划作罢，但祭坛石、相传基督踏过的圣石和启蒙者格列高利的右臂仍被运走，1611年砌入新朱尔法的圣乔治教堂。

后来的几任大主教修补穹顶和地基，在修道院四周筑墙，又在西门上添了高大的钟楼。西缅大主教1770年在近旁办起亚美尼亚第一家印刷所。1804年6月，齐齐安诺夫进攻埃里温期间，俄军一度进入埃奇米阿津、劫掠各教堂，随后被击退；波斯宫廷中的法国使节记下了这场破坏，还拿它同沙阿善待基督徒臣民的做法对照。

en:
On the oil-bearing Absheron peninsula east of Baku, at Surakhani, hydrocarbon gas seeps through seven natural vents and burns without fuel. Arab geographers knew the place: al-Istakhri wrote in the tenth century of fire-worshippers living near Baku, and the Persian name Ateshgah means house of fire. The pentagonal complex around a courtyard was raised in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries by merchants from Multan in the Punjab who, with the Armenians, ran much of the Caspian caravan trade. A four-pillared altar sheltered the eternal flame, monks' cells lined the walls, and a trident rose over the roof. The inscriptions, mostly Hindu with a few Sikh and one Persian, consecrate the shrine to Jwala Ji, the fire goddess whose Himalayan temple at Jawalamukhi the merchants copied. Pilgrims called this the greater Jwala Ji and the Kangra shrine the lesser.

The men who kept the flame were a mixed company. Engelbert Kaempfer, passing in 1683, counted the seven fires and met two worshippers descended from Persians who had migrated to India; the Jesuit Villotte found Hindus, Sikhs and Zoroastrians there together. In 1745 a Zoroastrian from Isfahan cut a Persian New Year verse over a doorway, giving thanks for reaching Baku. In 1770 Samuel Gottlieb Gmelin watched ascetics performing yogi austerities, and in 1820 the French consul Gamba still found Hindus, Sikhs and Zoroastrians keeping the same flame: pilgrims and merchants of three faiths at the end of the Multan road.
zh:
巴库东郊阿布歇隆半岛产油地带的苏拉哈尼，地下油气从七处天然气孔渗出，无需柴薪，自行燃烧。阿拉伯地理学家早就知道此地：10世纪的伊斯塔赫里写过巴库附近住着拜火之人；阿特什加这个名字在波斯语里意为「火的居所」。五边形院落建于17至18世纪，由木尔坦的旁遮普商人营建，他们和亚美尼亚人一道把持着里海的商队贸易大半。院中央的四柱亭罩着长明火，僧房沿墙排开，屋顶立着三叉戟。庙中题记多为印度教，另有几处锡克教和一处波斯语，把此庙奉献给火焰女神久瓦拉吉，商人们仿照的是喜马拉雅山麓贾瓦拉穆基的同名神庙。朝圣者把这里称作大久瓦拉吉，坎格拉那座反倒是小的。

守着火的人成分混杂。1683年恩格尔贝特·肯普弗路过，数到七处火口，还遇到两名祖上从波斯迁到印度的礼拜者；耶稣会士维洛特见到印度教徒、锡克教徒和琐罗亚斯德教徒共处一庙。1745年，一名来自伊斯法罕的琐罗亚斯德教徒在门道上刻下波斯语新年诗，感念神助他抵达巴库。1770年萨穆埃尔·格梅林看到苦行僧行瑜伽苦修；1820年法国领事冈巴仍见到印度教徒、锡克教徒和琐罗亚斯德教徒同守这一团火：木尔坦商路的尽头，三种信仰的朝圣者与商人聚在一处。

en:
Narikala is a citadel of two walled courts strung along a steep ridge above the sulfur baths of Tbilisi, its walls stepping down almost to the Kura, where Metekhi fortress faces it across the water. Georgian sources call it Shuris-tsikhe, the Rival Fortress, and legend credits its building to Vakhtang I Gorgasali, the king who founded Tbilisi. A fort certainly stood here by the 360s, when the Iberian king Varaz-Bakur held the site. David the Builder rebuilt it after he took the city in 1122, and the Mongols who came in the 1230s renamed it Narin Qala, the Little Fortress. A small church of St Nicholas, built in the thirteenth century, stood in the lower court.

By 1444 the ridge walls had been rebuilt more than once, and the works a later traveller saw were newer still. The square Stambolis Tower and the Shahtakhti gun platform date to the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, when Kartli's Safavid and Ottoman overlords refortified the rock. Rostom, the shah's appointed king of Kartli, walled the approaches and put the citadel itself in Iranian hands. Whoever took Tbilisi took Narikala with it: Ottoman gunners entered in 1578 and held the fort for about forty years, and the Persians returned after them. Its last fight in these years came in September 1795, when Agha Mohammad Khan's Qajar army broke Heraclius II at Krtsanisi and the battle moved into the streets. The garrison held out on the ridge for hours before the citadel fell and was sacked together with the city.
zh:
纳里卡拉堡由两座围墙院落连成，沿第比利斯硫磺浴场上方的陡脊铺开，城墙顺山脊层层下降，几乎伸到库拉河边，与对岸的梅特希堡隔水相望。格鲁吉亚文献称它为舒里斯齐赫，意为「匹敌之堡」，相传它的修建者是营建第比利斯的瓦赫坦格一世·戈尔加萨利。4世纪60年代这里确实已有要塞，伊比利亚国王瓦拉兹-巴库尔据有其地。1122年大卫四世收复城市后再度重修，1230年代入城的蒙古人把它改叫纳林卡拉，意为「小堡」。下院里还有一座13世纪所建的圣尼古拉小堂。

1444年山脊上的城墙已经几经改建，后世旅人看到的工事还要更新：方形的伊斯坦布尔塔和沙赫塔赫提炮台都是16至17世纪所建，那时卡特利的萨法维和奥斯曼宗主轮番加固这座岩脊。萨法维册封的卡特利国王罗斯托姆在山脚下加筑围墙，并把要塞本身交给伊朗军队驻守。哪支军队拿下第比利斯，就一并拿下纳里卡拉：1578年奥斯曼炮手入城，占据近四十年，之后波斯人又回来。这一时期它的最后一仗在1795年9月，卡扎尔的阿迦·穆罕默德汗在克尔察尼西击溃伊拉克略二世，战斗延入街巷；守军在山脊上又撑了几个小时，要塞才随城市一同陷落、遭洗劫。

en:
The Marble Throne of the Golestan Palace stands on supports cut into the shapes of men, women, fairies and demons. Fath-Ali Shah commissioned it in 1805 for an open iwan by the garden: 65 pieces of yellow marble from a Yazd quarry, designed by the painter Mirza Baba Shirazi and carved by the royal stonecutter Mohammad Ebrahim Esfahani. It was modelled on the throne of Solomon, which the old stories said genies and fairies carried through the air at his command. The palace itself is the royal complex inside Tehran's arg, the citadel whose walls once ringed the old town. Shah Tahmasp I walled Tehran and marked out a royal enclosure there in the sixteenth century, Shah Abbas I laid out a high-walled garden at its north end, and Shah Suleiman I added a palace and audience hall. In the last year of Safavid rule Shah Soltan Hoseyn received the Ottoman envoy Ahmad Dari Effendi in that hall, not long before the Afghans overthrew the dynasty.

Karim Khan Zand later renovated the buildings and for a time held court here. In 1786 Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar, who had spent sixteen years as a hostage at Karim Khan's court in Shiraz, made Tehran his capital and took the arg as his seat. Crowned King of Kings in 1796, he wore a new Kiani Crown of red velvet set with about 1,800 pearls, 300 emeralds and 1,800 rubies, its shape taken from the crowns of the Sasanian and the mythical Kiyani shahs. His nephew Fath-Ali Shah rebuilt the complex on a royal scale and sheathed its halls in mirror mosaic, and held audience in rooms that filled with Iranian crafts and the gifts of European missions.
zh:
戈勒斯坦宫（古列斯坦宫）的大理石御座，座脚刻成男人、女人、仙女和恶魔的形状。1805年法塔赫·阿里沙为花园旁的露天敞厅敕造了它：六十五块采自亚兹德的黄大理石，由画师米尔扎·巴巴·设拉子设计、王室石匠穆罕默德·易卜拉欣·伊斯法罕尼雕成。它仿照古传所罗门的王座，传说精灵和仙女依他的命令驮着王座飞行。宫殿本身是德黑兰阿尔格城堡里的王室建筑群，城堡的城墙曾环住旧城。16世纪沙阿·塔赫玛斯普一世为德黑兰筑墙，在城中划出王室禁地；阿拔斯一世在禁地北端辟出高墙围起的园林；苏莱曼一世又添建宫殿和议政厅。萨法维末年，沙阿·苏丹·侯赛因在这座厅里接见奥斯曼使臣艾哈迈德·达里·埃芬迪，那是他在位的最后一年，不久阿富汗人便推翻了这个王朝。

后来卡里姆汗·赞德翻修宫室，一度在此听政。1786年，曾在设拉子卡里姆汗宫中做了十六年人质的阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔定都德黑兰，以阿尔格为王居。1796年他加冕为众王之王时，头戴新造的基扬王冠，红丝绒的冠身缀着约一千八百颗珍珠、三百颗祖母绿和一千八百颗红宝石，形制仿照萨珊王朝和神话中基扬诸沙的王冠。其侄法塔赫·阿里沙按王家规模重建宫苑，各殿四壁嵌满镜面马赛克，在这些殿宇里接见来使，波斯工艺和欧洲各国使团的礼品渐渐摆满各殿。

en:
Local legend says Shem, son of Noah, began the building of Khorezm at Khiva and dug the city's sacred Xeyvak canal with a miraculous spade, and that the clay of Khiva was carried off to build Medina in the Prophet's lifetime. Itchan Kala is the walled inner city, a rectangle of about 650 by 400 metres at the centre of the oasis capital. Its walls are sun-dried mud brick eight to ten metres high and five or six thick, with watch towers jutting out every thirty metres and crenellated walks along the top. Four gates admitted the caravans: the Ota Gate on the west, Bogcha on the north, Tosh on the south and the Polvon Gate on the east, each flanked by towers and roofed by a vaulted gallery over the passage.

Inside the gates stand the Friday Mosque, the Kunya-Ark citadel and the khan's own quarter. The Friday Mosque was founded in the tenth century and rebuilt in 1788 as a dim hall whose flat roof is carried on rows of carved wooden columns taken from older ruined buildings. The Kunya-Ark rises against the west wall, where in the later seventeenth century Anusha Khan added baths, the Ak Mosque and his own audience hall, and madrasas followed beside it. Wars between Bukhara and Persia battered the inner city in the first half of the eighteenth century, and its broken walls were restored only at the century's end.

The shrine the city loved best was the grave of Pahlavon Mahmud (1247-1326), a Khivan poet born to humble craftsmen who was also an unbeaten wrestler and a healer. He had asked to be buried in his own leather workshop, and Uzbeks, Turkmens and Karakalpaks all came to his tomb on pilgrimage. Early in the nineteenth century the khans raised a grand new mausoleum over it and completed their palace in the Kunya-Ark.
zh:
当地相传，诺亚之子闪从希瓦开始营建花剌子模，用神铲挖出城内神圣的海瓦克渠；又说希瓦的黏土在先知在世时被运去修建麦地那。希瓦内城是城墙围起的内城，约650米长、400米宽，在这座绿洲都城的正中。城墙以日晒土坯筑成，高8至10米、厚五六米，每隔三十米外突一座敌楼，墙顶有垛口走道。四座城门迎纳商队：西为阿塔门、北为巴赫恰门、南为托什门、东为波尔冯门（英雄门），各门门道两侧有墩台，门上是拱顶巡廊。

门内是聚礼清真寺、库尼亚-阿尔克城堡和汗王的宫区。聚礼清真寺始创于10世纪，1788年重建为一座光线幽暗的大厅，平顶由一排排雕花木柱承托，木柱都取自更古老的废建筑。库尼亚-阿尔克紧贴西墙，17世纪后期阿努沙汗在这里添建浴室、阿克清真寺和自己的觐见厅，经学院也相继在近旁落成。18世纪上半叶布哈拉与波斯的交战重创内城，残墙直到世纪末才得以修复。

城里人最爱的圣迹是帕赫拉万·马哈茂德（1247至1326）的墓。这位希瓦诗人出身卑微匠人，又是所向无敌的摔跤手，还能为人治病；他留下遗嘱葬在自己的皮匠作坊里，乌兹别克人、土库曼人和卡拉卡尔帕克人都到他的墓前朝圣。19世纪初，汗王们在墓上建起宏伟的新陵，并完工了库尼亚-阿尔克里的宫殿。

en:
The Registan is the great sandy square of Samarkand; its name means the place covered in sand. Crowds gathered on the sand to hear royal proclamations blown in on enormous copper horns, and to watch public executions. Between 1417 and 1420 Ulugh Beg built his madrasa on the west side, a high pishtaq facing the square with four minarets at its corners, four domed lecture halls and two tiers of student cells around the courtyard. He lectured there himself, and the poet Jami was among the students who sat through its courses in mathematics, geometry, logic, natural science and theology. Across the square Ulugh Beg later raised a khanaka, and a caravanserai stood on the north side. In 1444 it was one of the foremost schools of the Muslim east.

Those two buildings stood for about two hundred years. When they decayed, Yalangtush Bahadur, the Uzbek governor of Samarkand, had the Sherdar Madrasa raised on the khanaka's site from 1619, designed by the architect Abdul Jabbar with tilework by Muhammad Abbas. It all but mirrors the older madrasa opposite, but its portal carries the picture that gave it its name: tigers with the sun on their backs, a living-animal motif taken from old Seljuk coinage. Its over-large dome began to crack within a few decades.

From 1646 the Tilya-Kori, the Gilded Madrasa, went up on the foundations of Ulugh Beg's old caravanserai; its western hall was sheathed in gold leaf and served as the city's Friday mosque. Behind the Sherdar, where the roads to Tashkent, Bukhara and Shahrisabz meet, the Chorsu bazaar was rebuilt as a domed hat market in 1785.
zh:
雷吉斯坦广场是撒马尔罕的大沙广场，「雷吉斯坦」的意思就是「铺沙之地」。沙地上聚起人群，听巨型铜号吹出君王的诏令，也围观公开处决。1417至1420年，兀鲁伯在广场西侧建起他的经学院：高大门楼朝向广场，四角立着宣礼塔，四座穹顶讲堂，学生的僧房沿院落排成两层。他本人亲自在院中讲学，诗人贾米便曾在他门下听受数学、几何学、逻辑学、自然科学和神学的课程。广场对面，兀鲁伯后来又建了一座罕卡修行所，北侧则是商队客栈。1444年，这里是穆斯林东方最出色的学府之一。

对面那两座建筑立了约两百年。待它们倾颓，撒马尔罕的乌兹别克城主雅兰图什·巴哈杜尔于1619年起在罕卡旧址上建起希尔·多尔经学院，由建筑师阿卜杜勒·贾巴尔设计、穆罕默德·阿巴斯主持瓷砖装饰。它几乎是对面老经学院的镜像，门楼上的图案却给了它名字：虎背上驮着太阳的猛虎，这种生灵活物的纹样取自古塞尔柱钱币。它的穹顶过大，建成不过几十年便开始开裂。

1646年起，季里·牙·卡尔里经学院（意为「贴金经学院」）在兀鲁伯旧商队客栈的基址上建起，西侧大殿遍贴金箔，兼作全城的聚礼清真寺。希尔·多尔身后，在通往塔什干、布哈拉和沙赫里萨布兹的几条路会合之处，名叫乔尔苏的巴扎于1785年被重建成一座穹顶帽市。

en:
The khan of the Golden Horde kept his court on the lower Volga in a city with no wall. Al-Umari described salty ground between the river and the sand, with markets, baths and caravanserais but nothing circling the town; only a wall protected the goods of visiting merchants. Even at the height of the Horde the khan did not stay all year, but moved with the court and the herds. Sarai was spread among Akhtuba channels rather than gathered around one palace or citadel, and its name comes from a Turkic form of the Persian word for a court or mansion. Medieval writers may have known two successive towns of that name. Öz Beg founded a madrasa in one of them, an Orthodox bishopric and a Catholic see were established there, and coins were struck in the thirteenth century.

The brick ruins at Selitrennoye run for several kilometres along an Akhtuba branch. One estimate gives the built area about ten by two kilometres, with excavated estates, a mosque, a large necropolis and craft workshops. Scholars still divide over whether this was the first Sarai or the newer town founded in the 1330s. Timur's army destroyed the newer capital in 1395. In 1444 Sarai was still named as the Great Horde's capital, but the surviving court may have used the older site or a much reduced town. Afanasy Nikitin passed through on his way to India, and the Crimean khan Mengli I Giray burned what remained in 1502. When Samuel Gmelin travelled the lower Volga in 1769-1770, he heard Kalmyk accounts of a splendid city, and the brick mounds around him were attributed to the old capital of Great Tatary.
zh:
金帐汗国的可汗把汗廷设在伏尔加河下游的萨莱城，这座都城却没有城墙。阿尔-奥马里写到，这里地处河水与沙地之间的盐碱地，有市场、浴场和商队客栈，没有环绕全城的城墙，只有一道墙专门保护外来商人的货物。即使在汗国最强盛的时候，可汗也不全年驻在城里，而是随汗廷和畜群迁徙。萨莱散布在阿赫图巴河汊之间，没有集中在一座宫殿或堡垒周围；它的名字来自突厥语对波斯语「宫廷、府邸」一词的转写。中世纪作者笔下可能先后有两座同名城镇。月即别在其中一座设立过经学院，城中有过罗斯正教会主教区和天主教主教区，13世纪就已开始铸币。

谢利特连诺耶遗址的砖构残迹沿阿赫图巴一条支汊延伸数公里；有估算认为城区约长10公里、宽2公里，已发掘出宅院、清真寺、大型墓地和手工业作坊。学者仍在争论它是最早的萨莱，还是14世纪30年代建立的新萨莱。1395年，帖木儿的军队摧毁了较新的都城。1444年，萨莱仍被称为大帐汗国的首都，但残存的汗廷可能使用旧城，也可能驻在一座大幅缩小的城镇里。阿法纳西·尼基京前往印度时经过此地；1502年，克里米亚可汗明里一世·格莱焚毁了残余的城市。1769至1770年，萨穆埃尔·格梅林走过伏尔加河下游，听到卡尔梅克人讲起一座宏大的城市，而他周围的砖土丘已被人当作大鞑靼旧都的遗迹。

en:
Tortuga is a steep, turtle-backed island a few kilometres off the north-west of Hispaniola, its south coast opening into the sheltered roadstead of Cayona, with a rock platform above it. In 1640 the French engineer Jean Le Vasseur walled that platform as Fort de Rocher, also called the Dovecote, with its guns trained on every vessel entering the anchorage, and threw the port open to outlaws of every nation in exchange for a share of their takings. A first Spanish attempt to dislodge him lost a ship to the fort's fire and ended in an ambush on the beach. Cayona became the first great pirate rendezvous of the Caribbean. Le Vasseur did not last: in 1653 two of his lieutenants killed him. As the story goes, he had taken one man's mistress, and the two lured him out of the fort to inspect a warehouse, where a musket shot and then daggers finished him.

The men who gathered there were the boucaniers, named for the Arawak word for the wooden frames on which they smoked meat. They began as landless hunters of wild cattle and boar on Hispaniola and Tortuga, selling jerked beef and hides to passing corsairs; Spanish campaigns to kill off both the hunters and their cattle drove them from the land into boats. According to Exquemelin, a Tortuga man named Pierre Le Grand pioneered the attack on homeward-bound galleons in the Windward Passage. In 1663 the two buccaneer stations, Tortuga and Jamaica, held about fifteen ships and nearly a thousand men.

Alexandre Exquemelin reached Tortuga in 1666 as an indentured servant of the French West India Company, served three years, then joined the buccaneers as a barber-surgeon and sailed with Henry Morgan. His History of the Buccaneers of America came out in Amsterdam in 1678 and in English in 1684. Morgan, by then a knighted planter in Jamaica, sued the English publishers for libel, had the book withdrawn and collected 200 pounds in damages.
zh:
托尔图加岛地势陡峻，状如海龟，在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛西北角外数公里，南岸凹进避风的卡约纳锚地，锚地上方耸起一块岩台。1640年，法国工程师让·勒瓦瑟尔把岩台围筑成罗谢堡，也叫「鸽舍」，炮口对准每一艘进港的船，又宣布港口对各国亡命徒开放，只从每份战利品里抽成。西班牙人第一次来攻，一艘船被炮台火力击沉，登陆的人踩进伏击圈后退走。卡约纳就此成为加勒比头一个大海盗聚集地。勒瓦瑟尔自己没能坐稳：1653年，两名部下杀了他。据说他夺了其中一人的情妇，两人便把他骗出要塞去查看仓库，先开一枪，再用匕首结果了他。

聚在这里的人叫布坎尼尔，名字来自阿拉瓦克语里熏肉用的木架。他们原是伊斯帕尼奥拉和托尔图加没有土地的猎人，猎野牛和野猪，在木架上熏成肉干，卖给过路的海盗船；西班牙出兵连猎人带牛群一起清剿，把他们从岸上逼进海里。据埃克斯克默兰记载，岛上一个叫皮耶尔·勒格朗的人最先在向风海峡截击返航的大帆船。1663年，托尔图加和牙买加两个据点共有约十五条船、近一千人。

亚历山大·埃克斯克默兰1666年作为法国西印度公司的契约佣工来到托尔图加，服役三年后入伙布坎尼尔，当上外科理发师，跟随亨利·摩根出海。他的《美洲海盗史》1678年在阿姆斯特丹出版，1684年出了英译本。此时摩根已是牙买加的爵士和种植园主，他告英文出版商诽谤，让书收了回去，还拿到200英镑赔偿。

en:
The Fuerte del Morro, the Castillo San Felipe del Morro of the Spanish maps, sits on the bare rocky headland that commands the entrance to San Juan Bay, the easternmost fortified harbour of Spain's Caribbean. In 1539 King Charles I ordered the headland armed, on the advice of Gonzalo Fernandez de Oviedo, who judged the rock a better site for closing the anchorage than La Fortaleza inland. The first work was a round tower with four embrasures and a water battery of three guns at its foot. The military engineers Juan de Tejada and Bautista Antonelli later traced the bastioned outline the fortress keeps, and the finished citadel rises through six levels to 43 metres above the Atlantic, its walls 5.5 to 7.6 metres thick.

In 1593 the first permanent garrison arrived: Portuguese infantry sent from Lisbon by Philip II. Many married island women, and Portuguese surnames in Puerto Rico date from that posting. Two years later Francis Drake came with a fleet. A chain was drawn across the harbour mouth, and El Morro's gunners put a cannonball through the cabin of Drake's flagship; he turned away without taking the city.

The single loss on the fortress's record came in June 1598, when the Earl of Cumberland landed on the undefended eastern shore and took it from the landward side. Dysentery drove his garrison out within months. In 1625 a Dutch fleet sailed past the guns into the harbour and burned San Juan, but could not take the castle. After the British captured Havana in 1762, Charles III sent Field Marshal Alejandro O'Reilly and the engineer Tomas O'Daly to turn San Juan into a 'defence of the first order', and by the 1780s their revisions had given El Morro its final form.
zh:
海角要塞（圣费利佩海角城堡，常称埃尔莫罗）坐落在封锁圣胡安港湾入口的光秃岬角上，是西班牙加勒比属地最东端的设防港口。1539年，国王卡洛斯一世下令武装这块岬角。此前贡萨洛·费尔南德斯·德·奥维耶多考察后认定，比起深处内陆的拉福塔莱萨，这块巨岩更能锁住锚地。最初的工事是一座开四个炮眼的圆塔，坡脚另设三门炮的水边炮台。后来军事工程师胡安·德·特哈达和包蒂斯塔·安东内利画出要塞的棱堡轮廓，日后再没大变；建成的城堡共六层，高出大西洋海面43米，墙厚5.5至7.6米。

1593年，第一支常备守军抵达，是腓力二世从里斯本派来的葡萄牙步兵，不少人娶了岛上女子，波多黎各的葡萄牙姓氏就来自这次驻防。两年后，德雷克带着舰队前来。港口入口拉起一条铁链，埃尔莫罗的炮手一炮打穿了德雷克旗舰的船舱，他掉头离去，没能拿下这座城。

要塞防线上唯一一次失守在1598年6月：坎伯兰伯爵从没有设防的东岸登陆，从陆地一侧拿下了它，几个月后痢疾又逼得他的守军撤走。1625年，一支荷兰舰队驶过炮口进入港湾，烧了圣胡安，却没能攻下城堡。1762年英军攻陷哈瓦那后，卡洛斯三世派陆军元帅亚历杭德罗·奥赖利和工程师托马斯·奥戴利整顿防务，要把圣胡安建成「一等防御」，到18世纪80年代，他们的改建给了埃尔莫罗最后的形制。

en:
Seen from the flat road into Multan, a white dome rides a mound of red brick at the north-western edge of the fort, high enough to be seen for miles. The tomb was built for someone else. Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq, then governor at Dipalpur and not yet sultan of Delhi, raised it between 1320 and 1324 as his own mausoleum, the earliest monument in the Tughluq style and older than the Tughluq tombs of Delhi. His son Muhammad bin Tughluq gave the finished building to the descendants of Sheikh Rukn-ud-Din Abul Fateh (1251-1335), the Suhrawardiyya master of Multan and grandson of Bahauddin Zakariya, who is known as Shah Rukn-e-Alam, 'Pillar of the World'. The sheikh was first buried in his grandfather's shrine, and his remains were moved into the empty tomb afterwards.

The tomb is an octagon of three tiers, thirty-five metres high, with sloping turrets at the corners and a battlemented roof, so that it looks like a fortress turned into a mausoleum. Red brick is bound with shisham beams that have blackened with age, and bands of dark blue, azure and white glazed tile run across the walls. The dome is fifteen metres across, the second largest in South Asia after the Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur, and nothing props it from within. The sarcophagus lies a little off the centre, ringed by the graves of seventy-two of the saint's kin, a number chosen to recall the seventy-two companions of Imam Hussein killed at Karbala. Each year pilgrims gathered here for the urs, the feast of the saint's death and the greatest assembly in the City of Saints.
zh:
从木尔坦平坦的近郊望去，沙·鲁克内·阿拉姆陵的白色穹顶坐在木尔坦堡西北缘的红砖高台上，几里外就能望见。这座陵墓原本是为别人修的：吉亚斯—乌德—丁·图格鲁克还在当迪帕尔普尔总督、尚未登上德里王位时，于1320至1324年为自己营建了这座墓，它是图格鲁克风格最早的纪念建筑，比德里的图格鲁克诸陵还早。他的儿子穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克把完工的陵墓赠给了谢赫·鲁克努丁·阿布勒·法塔赫（1251—1335年）的后人。这位谢赫是木尔坦苏赫拉瓦迪耶教团的长老、巴哈乌丁·扎卡里亚的孙子，封号沙·鲁克内·阿拉姆，意为「世界之柱」。他最初葬在祖父的圣陵里，遗骨此后才迁入这座空陵。

陵体八角三层，高35米，角上立着内倾的角塔，顶部环列雉堞，像把堡垒搬进了陵墓。墙身红砖砌成，束以印度黄檀木梁，木梁历经数百年已经发黑，深蓝、天蓝与白色的琉璃砖成带地镶在红砖之间。穹顶直径15米，论大小在南亚仅次于比贾布尔的果尔·古姆巴斯，下方不施任何支撑。圣徒的石椁略偏中央安放，周围是他七十二名亲属的墓葬，排成这个数目，是为了纪念在卡尔巴拉殉难的伊玛目侯赛因的七十二名同伴。香客每年来此参加圣徒忌辰的法会「乌尔斯」，这是「圣徒之城」一年中最盛大的聚礼。

en:
Mehrangarh crowns a bluff of rock a hundred and twenty-two metres above the Jodhpur plain, its walls climbing the hill through seven gates. Rao Jodha began it on 12 May 1459, when the thousand-year-old fort at the old capital of Mandore no longer seemed safe. The hill was Bhakurcheeria, the mountain of birds, and its only dweller was the hermit Cheeria Nathji, 'lord of birds', who refused again and again to move. Jodha called in Karni Mata of Deshnoke, the warrior-sage of the Charans, and at her word the hermit left, cursing the citadel to everlasting scarcity of water. Jodha built him a house and a temple to soften the curse, and Karni Mata laid the foundation stone herself.

Tradition adds a darker rite. A man of the Meghwal caste called Raja Ram offered to be buried alive in the foundations for the fort's luck, and his family took Rathore land in return. The first works were rough siege walls; the palaces came later, most of them under Jaswant Singh between 1638 and 1678, and the ramparts on the crest now run up to thirty-six metres high and twenty-one metres thick.

The gates read like a record of Marwar's wars. Dedh Kangra Pol, the second gate, is pocked with the cannonball marks of Jaipur's armies. Jai Pol, the Victory Gate at the head of the climb, was raised by Maharaja Man Singh in 1806 after he defeated the combined armies of Jaipur and Bikaner. Inside stand the Pearl Palace, the Flower Palace and the mirror-lined Sheesh Mahal. The last gate of the ascent is the Loha Pol, and set into its wall are rows of small red handprints, left by the ranis and princesses of Marwar who passed through it to burn as satis on their husbands' pyres.
zh:
梅兰加尔城堡踞在焦特布尔平原上方122米的岩山上，城墙随山势拾级而上，一路要过七道门。拉奥·乔达1459年5月12日动工建堡，旧都曼多尔那座千年古堡，在他看来已经不够安全。岩山本叫巴库尔切里亚，即「鸟山」，山上唯一的住户是人称「鸟主」的隐士切里亚·纳特吉，他一再拒绝搬走。乔达请来德斯赫诺凯的查兰族武圣克勒妮·玛塔，隐士见她出面便即刻离去，临走诅咒这座城堡永远缺水。乔达在堡内为他建屋修庙以平息诅咒，奠基石由克勒妮·玛塔亲手安放。

传说还有更阴沉的一幕：梅格瓦尔人拉贾·拉姆自愿被活埋进地基为城堡求吉，他的家族则换得拉索尔人赐下的土地。最早的工程只是粗糙的围战墙，宫殿是后来才有的，现存大多建于1638至1678年贾斯万特·辛格之世；山脊上的城墙最高36米、厚21米。

一道道城门，读起来就是马尔瓦尔历次战争的账单。第二道门代德坎格拉门上布满弹坑，那是斋普尔军队的炮击留下的。登顶的主门贾伊门意为「胜利门」，是摩诃罗阇曼·辛格1806年击败斋普尔与比卡内尔联军后修建的。门内有珍珠宫、花宫和镶满镜片的镜宫。登城路上最后一道门是洛哈门，门墙里嵌着一排排小小的红色手掌印，那是马尔瓦尔的王后和公主们留下的，她们从这道门走出去，在丈夫的火葬堆上自焚殉夫。

en:
The Taj Mahal stands on the right bank of the Yamuna at Agra, a white-marble tomb built by Shah Jahan for his favourite wife, Mumtaz Mahal, who died in the imperial camp during a campaign in the Deccan, giving birth to their fourteenth child. Court historians wrote that the emperor shut himself away for a week; tradition makes one of her last requests a tomb the like of which the world had not seen.

Work began in 1632 on a riverside estate of Raja Jai Singh, who was paid with a palace in the middle of Agra. More than twenty thousand artisans worked under a board of architects headed by Ustad Ahmad Lahori: the Ottoman master Ismail Efendi took the dome and the Persian Amanat Khan cut the Quranic calligraphy. Makrana marble came up a fifteen-kilometre earthen ramp, hauled by oxen and elephants, and twenty-eight kinds of stone went into the inlay: lapis from Afghanistan, turquoise from Tibet, jade from China, carnelian from Arabia. The tomb was finished in 1648, the mosque and garden in 1653.

The four minarets, over forty metres tall, lean slightly outward so that an earthquake would throw them away from the tomb. The cenotaphs were first fenced with a gold railing, later replaced by a pierced marble screen set with gems, because Shah Jahan meant the queen alone to lie at the centre. In 1658 Aurangzeb deposed him, and he spent eight years a prisoner in Agra Fort with the dome in view across the river. He died in 1666 and was laid beside her, the only asymmetrical thing in the building. The gem merchant Tavernier, who visited in 1665, took home a story that a twin tomb of black marble had been planned across the river and stopped by the war of succession. In the eighteenth century the Jat rajas of Bharatpur stripped the chandeliers of silver and agate and the gold sheathing from the main finial.
zh:
泰姬陵在阿格拉的亚穆纳河右岸，是沙贾汗为最宠爱的妻子慕塔芝·玛哈修建的白色大理石陵墓。她随军征战德干，在军营中生下第十四个孩子时去世。宫廷史家记载皇帝悲痛难抑，一周不见朝臣；相传她的遗愿之一，是要一座举世未见的陵墓。

工程1632年动工，基址是杰伊·辛格王公临河的庄园，皇帝以阿格拉城中的一座大宫相换。主持工程的是乌斯塔德·艾哈迈德·拉合里为首的匠师班子，两万多名工匠应募：奥斯曼匠师伊斯梅尔·埃芬迪掌穹顶，波斯人阿马纳特汗镌刻古兰经铭文。马克拉纳的大理石由牛群和象队沿十五公里长的夯土坡道拖来，镶嵌用石共二十八种，有阿富汗的青金石、西藏的绿松石、中国的玉石、阿拉伯的红玉髓。陵寝1648年建成，清真寺和花园1653年完工。

四座四十多米高的宣礼塔都微微向外倾斜，地震时会倒向远离陵寝的一侧。两具衣冠冢最初围着一道金栏，后来换成镶满宝石的镂空大理石屏，因为沙贾汗本只打算让皇后一人安卧墓室中央。1658年他被奥朗则布废黜，在阿格拉堡中被囚八年，隔河就能望见穹顶。1666年他去世，葬在妻子身侧，成了整座建筑中唯一不对称的一笔。宝石商人塔韦尼耶1665年到访，回欧洲后讲起一个传闻：河对岸原计划再建一座黑色大理石陵，因夺位之战而停工。18世纪，珀勒德布尔的贾特王公劫走陵中的银质和玛瑙吊灯，还剥去主宝顶上的包金。

en:
The monuments of Hampi spread across more than forty square kilometres of granite boulders and palm grove on the south bank of the Tungabhadra: about 1,600 temples, halls, gates, tanks and stables raised by the emperors of Vijayanagara for their capital. The oldest stones belong to Virupaksha, the Shiva temple of Pampa that drew pilgrims before the city existed and never lost its rites. Its 50-metre painted gopuram opens onto a 750-metre stone bazaar; within stand a hundred-column hall and a community kitchen fed by a channel cut through living rock. The emperors built mostly in the Dravidian manner with Hoysala-style pillars, while a few buildings, the queen's bath and the elephant stables among them, borrowed the arches and domes of the Deccan's Muslim architects.

Krishna Deva Raya filled the city with new work. His Krishna temple of 1515 fronts a colonnaded chariot market and a stepped tank, and beside it sits a 6.7-metre Narasimha, the man-lion of Vishnu, in yoga. At the Vitthala complex the courtyard holds a stone chariot that carries Garuda, and a hall of 56 stone beams was cut to give different musical notes when struck. In the royal centre the Mahanavami Dibba, three square granite stages, is covered with reliefs of elephants, horses and camels in procession, female stick-dancers and citizens drenching each other at Holi; it once carried the wooden pavilion where the Raya watched the nine nights of Dasara and received tribute. Nearby stood the king's balance, on which he weighed himself against gold for distribution. Eleven domed chambers stabled the royal elephants.

After the battle of January 1565 the victors sacked the city, and the monuments show it: fire took the wooden pavilions and left a hundred stone stubs where the audience hall had stood; the Narasimha shrine was burned, its Lakshmi broken away and its floor blackened; work at Vitthala stopped mid-course. The court departed and the great bazaars emptied to boulder and scrub, while the lamps at Virupaksha, with its pilgrims, stayed lit through the centuries that followed.
zh:
亨比的古迹散布在栋格珀德拉河南岸四十多平方公里的花岗岩巨石与棕榈林间：约一千六百座神庙、厅堂、城门、水池和马厩，都是毗奢耶那伽罗皇帝为都城修建的。最古老的石头属于维鲁帕克沙神庙，这座供奉潘帕的湿婆庙在建城之前就吸引香客，祭仪从未中断。庙前50米高的彩绘瞿布罗门楼朝向一条750米长的石砌市集；门内有百柱厅，还有靠在天然岩石上凿出的水渠供水的公共厨房。皇帝们大多以达罗毗荼法式营造，柱式带着曷萨拉遗风；王后浴室、象厩等少数建筑，则借用了德干穆斯林建筑师的拱券与穹顶。

克里希纳·德瓦·拉亚在城中大兴土木。他1515年的克里希纳神庙前是柱廊夹道的战车市集和一座阶梯水池，庙旁是6.7米高、结跏趺坐的人狮毗湿奴（那罗辛哈）。维塔拉神庙群的院中有驮着迦楼罗的石战车，还有一座由56根石梁组成的大厅，敲击时能发出不同乐音。王城区的大平台（玛哈纳瓦米·迪巴）分三层方形花岗岩台座，壁上刻满列队的象、马、骆驼，持棍的女舞者，还有在洒红节上互相泼水的市民；台上曾有木构楼阁，罗阇在此观看九夜庆典、接受贡品。旁边是国王天平，罗阇在这里称出与自己等重的黄金分施。十一间带穹顶的房舍养着御象。

1565年1月的大战之后，胜利者洗劫了都城，古迹本身记着这场劫难：木构楼阁被焚，觐见厅只留下一百根石柱残桩；那罗辛哈神龛被烧，身旁的吉祥天女像被毁，地面熏得焦黑；维塔拉的工程半途而废。王廷离去，市集退化成乱石与灌丛，只有维鲁帕克沙神庙的灯火和香客，在之后的几百年里一直没有断绝。

en:
A medieval Marathi legend says a queen vowed to fast until she could see a temple spire, and the architect Kokasa cut down through the rock from the top and produced a shikhara within a week. The temple is Kailasa, Cave 16 at Ellora, raised for the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I and carved from a single rock from the top down. Its courtyard sinks 82 by 46 metres into the hillside, the temple rises 32.6 metres above its floor, life-size elephants carry the plinth on their backs, and a panel shows Ravana shaking Mount Kailasa. Manikeshwar, the earliest name attached to the temple, is said to be the queen's. A copper-plate inscription of 812 already calls it a work that astonished even the gods and its own builder.

Kailasa is one of thirty-four temples and monasteries cut side by side into a two-kilometre face of basalt in the Charanandri hills, about thirty kilometres from Daulatabad. Buddhists began excavating around AD 600, Hindus followed through the eighth and ninth centuries, and Jains added the last caves under the Yadavas.

When the Delhi sultans' armies took nearby Devagiri, they did not break the temples at Ellora; the troops came as sightseers, and the Sufi quarters later took the name Rauza. The Bijapur historian Rafi al-Din Shirazi ranked Kailasa with Persepolis as a wonder and a rarity. Mughal nobles went there on outings: Aurangzeb, who had temples thrown down elsewhere in the Deccan, liked to walk the courts and called Kailasa one of the wonders of the transcendent Artisan, charming to the eye and beyond what any written description could picture. Travellers left their names in the records: Thevenot in the mid-seventeenth century, Niccolao Manucci, who judged from the workmanship that the caves had been executed by the ancient Chinese, and the Company resident Charles Warre Malet in 1794. In the late eighteenth century Ahilyabai Holkar paid for the last painted decoration the temple received, at a time when much of the carved stone still carried its old paint.
zh:
一则中世纪马拉地传说讲，一位王后立誓不见塔尖便不进食，建筑师科卡萨就从岩顶向下开凿，七天之内造出了塔尖。这座庙就是埃洛拉的第16窟凯拉萨神庙，为罗湿陀罗拘陀国王克里希纳一世而凿，整座从整块岩石的顶部向下雕出：庭院在山坡上沉出八十二米长、四十六米宽的深坑，庙身在坑底之上高32.6米，等身大的石象驮着底座，还有罗波那撼动凯拉萨山的浮雕。神庙最早的名字「马尼格什瓦尔」据说就来自这位王后。812年的一则铜版铭文已把它称作连神祇和建造者本人都为之惊叹的工程。

凯拉萨只是埃洛拉石窟三十四座寺院之一，它们在恰拉南德里山一道两公里长的玄武岩崖壁上并排凿出，距道拉塔巴德约三十公里。约公元600年佛教徒首先开窟，8至9世纪印度教徒继之，耆那教徒在亚达瓦王朝时期补上最后几窟。

德里苏丹国的军队拿下附近的德瓦吉里后，没有毁坏埃洛拉的神庙，士兵反倒当作胜景来游，苏非行者的住处后来得名「劳扎」。比贾普尔史家拉菲丁·设拉子把凯拉萨与波斯波利斯并称，视为稀世奇观。莫卧儿贵族常来游宴：在德干别处拆过神庙的奥朗则布却喜欢在庭院间漫步，称凯拉萨是大匠（真主）的奇迹之一，悦目怡神，非笔墨所能形容。行旅者也在记载中留名：17世纪中期的泰夫诺、据雕工断定石窟出自「古代中国人」之手的尼科劳·马努齐，以及1794年东印度公司驻扎官查尔斯·沃伦·马利特。18世纪末，阿希莉娅拜·霍尔卡出资为神庙加绘了最后一层壁画，那时许多石雕上还带着旧日的色彩。

en:
The Sun Temple at Konark was cut as the chariot of the sun god Surya. Built around 1250 for Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty on the shore some thirty-five kilometres north-east of Puri, it carries twelve pairs of stone wheels along its base, each nearly 3.7 metres across, with seven horses straining in front. The wheels are sundials: their spokes mark the eight watches of the day and their shadows give the time to the minute. At dawn, seen from inland, the khondalite chariot appears to rise out of the sea carrying the sun. The great tower over the sanctuary once rose close to seventy metres; the assembly hall that survives reaches only half that.

Odia legend tells of the boy Dharmapada, son of the master mason Bishu Maharana, who set the crown stone in a single night to save twelve hundred craftsmen from execution, and threw himself into the sea so the deed could never be traced to them.

Rites went on for centuries, and Abul Fazl, writing at Akbar's court, described a living temple that left the visitor astonished. The tower fell to ruin between the late 1500s and the early 1600s; the army of Kalapahar, which overthrew the last Hindu king of Odisha in 1568, is held in Odia tradition to have sacked the shrine. Sailors in the Bay of Bengal took the dark mass for a sea mark and called it the Black Pagoda, against the White Pagoda of Jagannatha at Puri, and the name appears in European accounts by 1676. By the 1700s the place lay abandoned under overgrowth. Maratha rulers carried stone away for the Puri temple enclosure, and around 1779 a Maratha holy man removed the ten-metre chlorite Aruna pillar from the entrance and set it before the Lion Gate at Puri. In 1803 the Bengal government forbade carrying any more stone from the site.
zh:
戈纳勒格太阳神庙被雕成太阳神苏利耶的战车。它约建于1250年，为东恒伽王朝的那罗辛诃·提婆一世而建，坐落在普里东北约三十五公里的海岸边：底座排着十二对石轮，每只直径近3.7米，七匹骏马在前方作牵引状。这些轮子同时是日晷，轮辐标出一天的八个时辰，日影能把时间读到分；黎明从陆上望去，这座孔兹岩战车仿如载着朝阳从海中升起。神龛上方的主塔原高近七十米，残存的集会殿仅及其半。

奥里亚传说里有个少年达摩帕德，是工匠头比苏·莫赫拉纳的儿子，他一夜之间装好塔顶石，救下将被处死的一千二百名工匠，自己投海而死，让此事再也追查不到他们头上。

此后数百年祭仪不断，阿克巴宫廷里的阿布勒·法兹勒笔下，这是一座令观者惊叹的在用神庙。主塔在16世纪末至17世纪初塌毁；1568年推翻奥里萨末代印度教国王的卡拉帕哈德大军，在奥里亚传说中正是洗劫神庙的人。孟加拉湾的水手把这座黑色巨物当作航标，称它「黑塔」，与普里贾格纳特神庙的「白塔」相对，1676年的欧洲人记载里已有此名。到18世纪，庙地荒废，掩没在草木之中。马拉塔统治者运走石料修筑普里神庙的围墙，约1779年，一位马拉塔苦行僧人把庙前十米高的绿泥石阿噜那石柱迁走，立到普里神庙的狮门之前。1803年孟加拉政府下令不得再从遗址运走石料。

en:
Swayambhunath crowns a low, wooded hill west of Kathmandu, its white dome and gilded spire visible across the whole valley. The name means 'self-arisen'. According to the Swayambhu Purana the valley was once a lake where nagas lived, until a lotus sown by a Buddha of a past age opened above the water in a thousand petals and gave out an eternal, self-born light. Manjushri came to worship, cut a gorge through the hills with his sword to drain the lake, and a king of Gaud raised the first stupa where the light had burned.

Pilgrims climb a long stone stairway to a hemisphere of brick and earth, topped by a cube painted on all four faces with the Buddha's eyes gazing in every direction, the curl between them shaped as the Nepali numeral one. Above rise thirteen gilded rings, the thirteen stages on the way to nirvana. Sacred monkeys live on the hill and give the shrine its traveller's name of Monkey Temple; local legend makes them lice from the hair of Manjushri.

An inscription of 640 records works by the Licchavi kings, and legend keeps Nagarjuna here for twelve years and Padmasambhava and Shantarakshita on their road to Tibet. The Indian master Shariputra, the last abbot of Bodh Gaya, directed a great rebuilding with a Malla king's support and died in 1426. In 1504 the king of Kathmandu called in the Kagyu yogin Tsangnyon Heruka, the Madman of Tsang, who carried a renovation through in three months. In the seventeenth century Pratap Malla built the long eastern stairway that became the usual way up, and Tibetan lamas crossed the passes to Swayambhu throughout the Malla years.
zh:
斯瓦扬布纳特寺（斯瓦扬布，又称四眼天神庙）坐落在加德满都以西一座林木葱郁的小山上，白色穹顶和鎏金塔身在整个谷地都望得见。寺名意为「自体升起」。《斯瓦扬布往世书》说，谷地本是龙众居住的大湖，过去佛在湖中播下一粒莲种，莲花绽开千瓣，放出自生的永恒光芒。文殊菩萨前来朝拜，以神剑劈开山口、排干湖水，一位高达国王便在光芒燃起之处建起第一座佛塔。

香客沿长长的石阶登上山顶，迎面是砖土夯筑的覆钵穹顶，穹顶上方立着方台，四面各绘一双佛眼注视四方，两眼之间的卷曲是尼泊尔数字的「一」。方台之上是十三层鎏金相轮，对应通向涅槃的十三层境界。山上栖居着圣猴，行旅之人便叫它「猴庙」，当地相传这些猴子是文殊菩萨头发里的虱子所化。

一块640年的残碑记载了李查维诸王的修缮；相传龙树曾在山上驻锡十二年，莲花生与寂护入藏途中也到过这里。印度高僧室利沙是菩提伽耶的末代住持，在一位马拉国王资助下主持大规模重修，1426年圆寂。1504年，加德满都国王请来噶举派瑜伽士藏宁·赫如迦，人称「藏地疯圣」，他三个月内便完成了一次修缮。17世纪，普拉塔普·马拉修筑了长长的东侧石阶，此后成为登山的正路；马拉列国之世，西藏喇嘛翻山而来的香火始终不绝。

en:
Over the gate of the Bara Katra, the Great Caravanserai, a Persian inscription by Shaduddin Muhammad Siraji recorded that twenty-two shops had been attached to the foundation, their rents to pay for repairs and to lodge travellers free; whoever undid the endowment would answer for it on the Day of Judgment. The building lines the north bank of the Buriganga at Dhaka, south of the Chawk Bazaar. Mir Abul Qasim, diwan and chief revenue officer of Prince Shah Shuja, built it between 1644 and 1646 as the prince's official residence while he governed Bengal and Orissa for his father Shah Jahan. The plan followed the caravanserais of Central Asia: four wings enclosed a square courtyard ringed with shops and lodging cells. The river-facing south wing ran almost sixty-eight metres, its centre thrust forward in a three-storey gatehouse between two high octagonal towers, and the way in led through a guardroom and an octagonal domed hall into the court.

The prince for whom it was built held it barely a decade. When Shah Jahan fell ill in 1657 Shah Shuja crowned himself and marched on the capital, but Aurangzeb's army broke him in January 1659; pursued across Bengal, he passed through Dhaka for the last time in April 1660 and took ship for Arakan, where he was murdered. His katra outlasted him as a free hostelry and a customs post, its river steps busy with the Bengal trade and with ships coming up from the Indonesian archipelago. Shaista Khan, the governor who followed, raised the smaller Chhota Katra 185 metres to the east. James Atkinson, seeing the old caravanserai in the early nineteenth century, called it 'a stupendous pile of grand and beautiful architecture'.
zh:
巴拉卡特拉商队驿站（意为「大驿站」）的门上嵌着一块波斯语石匾，由沙德丁·穆罕默德·西拉吉撰文，写明这处义产附带二十二间店铺，租金用来修缮房屋并供旅人免费投宿；谁若撤销这份捐赠，末日审判时必将受罚。驿站在达卡布里甘加河北岸、乔克巴扎尔以南，1644年至1646年由沙舒贾亲王的迪万、首席税务官米尔·阿布·卡西姆主持修建，作为沙舒贾代父沙贾汗统治孟加拉和奥里萨时的官邸。它仿照中亚商队客栈形制：四座翼楼围成方形庭院，四周排满店铺和供人住宿的房间。临河的南翼长近六十八米，中央突出三层门楼，两侧是高耸的八角塔楼；进门先过卫兵室，再经一座八角形穹顶大厅才到庭院。

修建它的亲王没能享用多久。1657年沙贾汗病重，沙舒贾自立为帝、进军京师，却在1659年1月被奥朗则布的军队击败；他被一路追击穿过孟加拉，1660年4月最后一次经过达卡，随后登船逃往若开，在那里被杀。他的驿站留存下来，继续充当免费客栈和海关关卡，河边台阶上孟加拉商货往来不绝，印度尼西亚群岛的船只溯河而上。继任总督沙伊斯塔汗在东面一百八十五米处建起较小的「小卡特拉」（Chhota Katra）。詹姆斯·阿特金森在19世纪初见到这座旧客栈，称它是「一座宏伟壮丽的惊人巨构」。

en:
The pillars of the Kanbawzathadi were whole teak trunks, sent by the vassal towns of Bayinnaung's empire, and each was inscribed in Mon with the name of the town and lord that gave it. Bayinnaung, founder-king of the Toungoo empire, ordered the palace built in the middle of his new capital of Hanthawadi at Pegu. By 1556 the walled grounds covered seventy acres and held seventy-six halls and apartments. The largest was the Great Audience Hall, its roof laid with sheets of beaten gold and its interior covered in gold paint. There Bayinnaung received his ministers from the Lion Throne, carved with lions, the first of nine royal thrones, each with its own motif and ceremony. Behind it stood the private Bee Throne hall with the king's bedchamber, crowned by a seven-tiered pyatthat spire. European visitors who saw the palace in the 1580s wrote of gilded halls roofed in gold.

The golden palace stood for little more than forty years. In 1565, while Bayinnaung campaigned in Lan Na, resettled Shan hostages rose in Pegu and burned the whole complex. He rebuilt it on the same brick terraces, grander than before. His son Nanda Bayin reigned there as the empire broke around him, until 1599, when the viceroy of Toungoo and an Arakanese fleet took the city. The victors stripped the gold from the halls and fired the palace, and the nine thrones burned with it. Nothing was rebuilt. The seventy-acre enclosure stood abandoned, its teak halls gone and only the brick foundations of the audience halls left above the grass.
zh:
勃固王宫（甘菩遮塔迪宫）的殿柱是整根的柚木巨柱，由勃印曩帝国各藩属城镇进献，柱身刻着孟文铭文，记下献柱的城镇与首领之名。东吁王朝的开创者勃印曩下令在新都汉达瓦底、也就是勃固城的正中兴建这座王宫。到1556年，宫城占地七十英亩，内有厅堂七十六座。最大的是大觐见厅，殿顶铺着锤打成的金板，内壁通体金饰。勃印曩在这里高踞狮王座接见群臣，王座雕满狮子，是宫中九座王座之首，每座各有纹饰、各司典礼。厅后是蜂王座内殿，安置国王的寝宫，顶上立着七级层叠的塔尖。1580年代入宫的欧洲访客留下记载，说殿宇是金板覆顶的。

金宫存世不过四十余年。1565年勃印曩远征兰那时，迁居勃固的掸人人质起事，焚毁了整座宫城；他在原有砖台基上重建，规制比先前更宏大。其子南达勃因在此继位，帝国却在他手中分崩。1599年，东吁诸侯与若开舰队攻破勃固，胜者剥去殿上的金板、纵火焚宫，九座王座一同化为灰烬。此后再无重建：七十英亩宫城就此荒废，柚木殿宇荡然无存，只剩大觐见厅的砖筑基台露在荒草之上。

en:
Angkor Wat faces west, unlike other Khmer temples, and its reliefs run counter-clockwise, the order of Brahmin funeral rites. From the western causeway the rising sun at the equinox stands on the central tower. Suryavarman II began it about 1122 on the advice of the brahmin Divakarapandita as his state temple to Vishnu, and work stopped at his death about 1150 with reliefs still uncarved. Between five and ten million sandstone blocks, the heaviest a ton and a half, were quarried at Mount Kulen forty kilometres away and rafted by canal and across the lake to the site.

The temple fills a rectangle of 162 hectares north of the Tonle Sap, ringed by a moat 190 metres wide and more than five kilometres around. Inside, three galleries climb to a quincunx of towers, the central one sixty-five metres high: the five peaks of Mount Meru, with the wall and moat for the mountains and ocean around it. Nearly a thousand square metres of bas-relief line the outer gallery, among them the churning of the ocean of milk, Suryavarman's own marching army, and the heavens and hells. On the walls 1,796 individual devatas stand, each with its own jewellery and headdress.

When the royal cult turned to Buddhism, the Vishnu image in the central shrine was walled in and the new faces of the shrine were carved with standing Buddhas. That is why Angkor Wat kept its monks and pilgrims while most of the old capital emptied. Pilgrims left image after image of the Buddha in the cruciform cloister called the Hall of a Thousand Buddhas, and cut merit inscriptions into it in Khmer, Burmese and Japanese. Royal patrons added new reliefs in the sixteenth century, including the gallery panel of Vishnu overcoming the asuras, and workmen repairing crumbling sections took down several secondary towers in the mid-seventeenth century. The oldest surviving plan of the temple is a measured drawing made in 1715 by a Japanese, Fujiwara Tadayoshi.
zh:
和其他高棉寺庙不同，吴哥窟坐东朝西，浮雕按逆时针排列，正是婆罗门葬仪的次序；春秋分之日从西边引道望去，初升的太阳正挂在中塔之上。苏利耶跋摩二世约在1122年采纳一位婆罗门国师的建议动工，作为供奉毗湿奴的国庙，约1150年他去世时工程中辍，部分浮雕仍未完工。建庙用了五百万到一千万块砂岩石料，最重的一块达一吨半，采自四十公里外的荔枝山，经运河放排、过湖泊运到工地。

庙在洞里萨湖北岸，占地162公顷，四周围着190米宽、周长逾五公里的护城河。庙内三层回廊逐层升高，通向五塔组成的塔林，中塔高65米：五塔象征须弥山五峰，城墙与护城河就是环绕的群山与大海。外围回廊有近一千平方米浮雕，其中有搅乳海、苏利耶跋摩二世亲征的大军、天堂与地狱，墙上还立着1796尊女神像，首饰发式各不相同。

后来王室改奉佛教，中央神殿里的毗湿奴像被封入墙中，新墙面刻上立身佛像，吴哥窟也因此在旧都大半荒废之后仍留住了僧侣和香客。朝圣者把一尊尊佛像供进十字形的千佛廊，又在廊中刻下做功德的铭文，文字有高棉文、缅文和日文。16世纪，王室施主增刻新浮雕，回廊上毗湿奴战胜阿修罗的一幅就是此时补入；17世纪中叶，工匠修葺倾圮部分时，拆除了几座次要的塔。现存最早的吴哥窟实测图，是日本人藤原忠良1715年所绘。

en:
The royal mosque of Aceh had no dome. Its roof rose in tiers of thatch over timber prayer halls, the usual form of an Acehnese mosque, and it stood beside the sultan's kraton in Kutaraja. Acehnese tradition gives it two founding dates, 1292 under Sultan Alaidin Mahmudsyah and 1612 under Iskandar Muda, who raised it as the great mosque of his capital. In 1444 a mosque already served the small Muslim trading port at the northern tip of Sumatra.

The Baiturrahman was the Friday mosque of a court known as a centre of Islamic scholarship. The sultan and his chiefs gathered here for the great festivals and heard the law taught. After Iskandar Muda royal power faded: his son-in-law was followed by a line of queens who ruled until 1699, and the territorial chiefs went their own way. By the 1680s a Persian visitor could write that every corner of northern Sumatra sheltered a separate king or governor, and that none paid tribute to a higher authority. In 1727 a Bugis dynasty took the throne.

Through all of this the thatched mosque kept its place beside the kraton. It was the royal mosque of the queens, of the Bugis sultans and, in the pepper years around 1800, of the court of Sultan Jauhar al-Alam.
zh:
亚齐的皇家大寺没有穹顶。屋顶层层叠起茅草，下面是木构礼拜殿，是亚齐清真寺的惯常形制，它就坐落在哥打拉贾的苏丹王宫旁。传统上它有两个始建年代：一说是1292年阿拉丁·马哈茂德沙苏丹所建，一说是1612年伊斯坎达尔·穆达苏丹为都城营建的大寺。1444年，苏门答腊北端这座穆斯林小商港已有清真寺。

拜图拉赫曼是亚齐宫廷的聚礼寺，这个宫廷以伊斯兰学问闻名。苏丹和首领们在此参加重大节日的礼拜，听人讲授教法。伊斯坎达尔·穆达之后王权转弱：继位的女婿之后是历代女王，女王当政直到1699年，地方首领各自为政。1680年代，一位波斯旅人写道，苏门答腊北部处处各有国王或总督，没有谁向更高的权威纳贡。1727年，一个布吉人王朝取得王位。

世事几度更替，茅草顶的大寺始终留在王宫身侧，是历代女王、布吉系苏丹和1800年前后胡椒繁荣年代佐胡尔·阿拉姆苏丹的皇家清真寺。

en:
Pura Besakih climbs nearly 1,000 metres up the slopes of Mount Agung, the highest mountain on Bali, in six terraced levels. Indonesian accounts count twenty-six related temples, led by Pura Penataran Agung. A split gateway marks the entrance, and the tall Kori Agung gate opens into the second courtyard. The stone bases of the main shrines resemble megalithic stepped pyramids, which shows that the ground was holy for at least 2,000 years before the Javanese conquerors who settled in Bali in 1284 worshipped there as Hindus.

By the fifteenth century it was the state temple of Gelgel. That court had an origin story of its own. The Babad Dalem chronicle says that Majapahit planted a vassal dynasty on Bali, and that its second ruler, Dalem Samprangan, was vain and incompetent. His youngest brother Dalem Ketut set up a new royal seat at Gelgel and visited Majapahit, where Hayam Wuruk gave him powerful heirlooms. Majapahit afterwards fell into chaos and vanished.

Hindu-Javanese priests, nobles and rituals found refuge there in the sixteenth century. Near its coastal palace the court kept Pura Dasar as a lowland counterpart of the mountain temple, and Pura Jero Agung as its ancestral shrine. The Dutch first appeared in 1597 and entered friendly relations with the king, whose densely populated island sold cotton cloth to traders from Java's north coast in return for pepper. After the death of a king in 1651 the court fell into internal fighting, and in 1686 a scion of the old line set up a new paramount seat at nearby Klungkung.
zh:
布撒基寺沿巴厘最高峰阿贡火山的山坡向上，分六层台地，海拔近一千米。印尼语资料记有26座彼此相连的寺庙，以佩纳塔兰阿贡主庙为首。入口是一座中劈山门，高耸的科里阿宫门通向第二进院落。主要神龛的石基形似巨石阶梯金字塔，说明这片土地至少两千年前就被视为圣地，后来1284年定居巴厘的爪哇征服者在此举行印度教祭祀。

到15世纪，它已是格尔格尔王朝的国家神庙。这个王朝有自己的来历。《巴巴德·达仑》记载，满者伯夷在巴厘扶植了一个藩属王朝，第二代国王达仑·桑普朗岸自负又无能。他的幼弟达仑·克图另在格尔格尔立了新王庭，还去满者伯夷朝见，哈雅姆·乌鲁克赐给他有法力的传家宝。满者伯夷后来陷入混乱，就此消失。

16世纪，印度教爪哇的祭司、贵族和仪轨在这里找到了容身处。王廷在近海王宫旁另奉达萨寺，作为山上母庙的低地对应庙，耶罗阿贡寺则是王室祖庙。荷兰人1597年首次到达，与国王建立了友好关系；岛上人烟稠密，用棉布向爪哇北岸的商人换取胡椒。1651年一位国王去世后，王廷陷入内斗，1686年，旧王室的一位后裔在附近的克隆孔另立新的共主王庭。

en:
Tradition says the Jokhang stands on a lake. Songtsen Gampo threw his ring (others say his hat) and promised to build wherever it fell; it dropped into the water and a white stupa rose from the lake, which goats hauled earth to fill, so the town was first called Rasa, Goat Place, before it became Lhasa. The king founded the temple in about 640 to house Jowo Mikyo Dorje, the image of the Buddha at eight years old brought by his Nepali queen Bhrikuti. Its gate faces west towards Nepal. The image in the main shrine is the other Jowo, Shakyamuni at twelve, a gilded figure with a jewelled crown and a diamond on its forehead. Tibetan legend holds that the divine smith Vishvakarman made it in the Buddha's own lifetime; it arrived with the Tang princess Wencheng, was hidden in a back chapel when a Chinese invasion was feared, and was later moved into the central shrine, swapping places with the Nepali image. Pilgrims walk the Barkhor circuit around the walls, prostrate themselves at the threshold and press in to drape a ceremonial scarf over the statue or touch its knee.

In 1409 Tsongkhapa founded the Great Prayer Festival at the Jokhang, and every first month thousands of monks from Ganden, Drepung and Sera gathered in its courtyards. After the Fifth Dalai Lama took power in 1642 he enlarged the temple and had gilded copper plates fixed over its timber roofs, and the gold roofs became the mark of Lhasa. After the Gorkha war of 1792 the Qing court barred Nepalese from the shrine. Outside stood the old stone pillar carved in Tibetan and Chinese with the Tang-Tubo frontier treaty, and in 1794 another tablet was set up beside it advising hygiene against smallpox. Worshippers chipped pieces from it, believing the stone itself could cure.
zh:
相传大昭寺建在一片湖上。松赞干布掷出戒指（一说是帽子），说戒指落在何处就在何处建寺；戒指落入湖中，湖里浮出一座白塔，人们驱羊驮土把湖填平，所以这座城早先叫「惹萨」，意为羊土，后来才改称拉萨。赞普在640年前后建寺，为供奉尼泊尔尺尊公主带来的释迦牟尼八岁等身像「觉卧米居多杰」；寺门朝西，面向尼泊尔。主殿内供奉的却是另一尊觉卧像：十二岁等身的释迦牟尼，头戴宝冠，额前镶着钻石。藏地传说这尊像由天匠毗首羯磨在释迦牟尼生前铸成，随唐朝文成公主入藏；听说唐人要出兵时，它被藏进后面的暗殿，后来移入主殿，与尺尊公主带来的像互换了位置。香客沿八廓转经道绕寺而行，在门槛前全身伏地叩拜，再挤到像前献上哈达，或摸一摸佛膝。

1409年，宗喀巴在大昭寺创办默朗钦波祈愿大法会，此后每年正月，甘丹、哲蚌、色拉三寺的数千名喇嘛齐聚寺院，连日诵经。第五世达赖喇嘛1642年掌权后扩建大昭寺，把木石屋顶包上鎏金铜板，金顶成了拉萨的标志。1792年廓尔喀战争后，清朝禁止尼泊尔人入寺朝佛。寺外立着以藏汉两种文字镌刻唐蕃边界条约的古碑，1794年旁边又立一碑，刻着预防天花的卫生告诫；信众却把碑石凿下碎片带走，相信石头本身就能治病。

en:
Around 256 BC Li Bing, Qin governor of Shu, built the Dujiangyan with his son at the foot of Mount Yulei, where the Min River spills onto the Chengdu Plain. Local legend gives the son, Erlang, the part of the hero: at the River God Temple he ambushed the dragon that took a human sacrifice every year, and chained it under the Lidui bluff. Li Bing put no dam across the river, which had to stay open for supply boats. He built a levee to split it. Its pointed Fish Mouth divides the water into an inner and an outer stream, sending roughly six tenths into the irrigation canals in the dry season and four in flood. Below it the Flying Sand Weir throws floodwater and silt back into the outer stream, and the twenty-metre Bottle-Neck Channel carries the controlled flow through the mountain cut. The levee was piled from long bamboo baskets of river stones held by wooden tripods. With no gunpowder yet, the channel was cut by heating the rock and cooling it until it split, eight years' work.

The works only keep working by being rebuilt. Every winter crews dredge the shoals and replace the baskets, following the six words carved at the Two Kings Temple: dredge the shoals deep, keep the weirs low. In 228 Zhuge Liang posted twelve hundred soldiers to the weirs and set a full-time weir officer over them. In 1335 the Yuan official Jidangpu rebuilt the headworks in mortared stone clamped with iron and cast a sixteen-thousand-jin iron turtle for the Fish Mouth. In 1550 the water commissioner Shi Qianxiang poured molten iron into his stonework and cast an iron-ox fish mouth of seventy thousand jin. The wars of 1644 emptied the irrigated villages and left the weirs derelict for years, until early Qing officials restored the annual dredging. In 1803 a local man, He Xiande, and his wife raised a plank-and-bamboo suspension bridge across both streams, and villagers called it the Couple's Bridge.
zh:
约公元前256年，秦国蜀郡守李冰和他儿子在玉垒山下、岷江出山口处修起都江堰，治住岷江年年泛滥。当地传说里立功的是李冰之子二郎：他在河神庙设伏，擒住每年索要人祭的孽龙，把它锁在离堆下的深潭里。李冰没有横江筑坝，因为航道还要供兵船通行，而是修了一道分水堤。堤头形如鱼嘴，把岷江分成内外两江，枯水时约六成水入内江灌溉，洪水时只放四成。下游的飞沙堰把多余的洪水和泥沙翻回外江，宽二十米的宝瓶口把受控的江水穿过山体送向成都平原。筑堤用的是塞满卵石的长竹笼，以木桩三角架固定；凿山时没有火药，工匠堆柴烧红岩石、再用水激冷使之崩裂，前后用了八年。

这套工程全靠年年重修。每年冬天枯水期，民夫淘挖河底淤沙、更换竹笼，依的是二王庙石壁上刻的六字诀：深淘滩，低作堰。228年，诸葛亮派出一千二百名兵丁护堰，并设了专职堰官。1335年，元朝肃政廉访使吉当普以浆砌条石加铁锚重修堰首，又铸了一头一万六千斤重的铁龟作鱼嘴。1550年，水利佥事施千祥以浆砌条石灌注铁水固堤，用七万斤生铁铸铁牛鱼嘴。1644年的战火使灌区人口流散、堰务荒废多年，入清以后地方官恢复岁修。1803年，本地何氏夫妇倡议重修索桥，以木板为面、竹索为栏，横跨内外两江，民间称作夫妻桥。

en:
The Grand Canal is 1,776 kilometres long, the longest artificial waterway on earth, and the Hangzhou section is its southern end, where boats leave the canal for the Qiantang River. Emperor Yang of the Sui joined the old channels into one network and called up more than three million labourers. In 610 he ordered the southernmost cut from Jingkou to Yuhang, now Hangzhou, 'more than eight hundred li long and over ten zhang wide' in the words of the Zizhi Tongjian, wide enough for his dragon barges, with posting palaces raised along the banks for an eastern tour. He never made it; rebels killed him at Jiangdu. The Yuan later cut new sections across Shandong and shortened the route by some seven hundred kilometres, and the Ming rebuilt the whole line with 165,000 labourers. By the middle of the fifteenth century 11,775 government barges carried four million dan of tribute grain north every year, crewed by 121,500 soldiers and officers.

In 1444 the southern traffic converged on the wharves at Hushu, north of the city. At Beixin Bridge, where the canal meets two other rivers, the Beixin customs house taxed every passing junk; it was one of seven great customs houses on the canal. In 1496 the official Liu Jingyin built a stone platform reaching three zhang out over the water, with steps on both sides, so merchants could clear their cargo without scrambling up the broken bank. Boats reached the Qiantang through the Longshan lock east of the city. In 1631 the three-arched Gongchen Bridge went up at Hushu, 92 metres of stone, the largest arch bridge in the city and the marker of the canal's end; its name means to salute the emperor. The Qianlong Emperor made six southern tours between 1751 and 1784, and all six reached Hangzhou. His grandfather the Kangxi Emperor had toured the south six times before him.
zh:
大运河全长1776公里，是世界上最长的人工水道，大运河杭州段是它的南端，漕船从这里出运河、入钱塘江。隋炀帝把各段旧河连成一张水网，征发三百多万人。610年他又下令疏凿江南河，《资治通鉴》记这段工程「自京口至余杭，八百余里，广十余丈」，宽得能走龙舟，沿途还修起驿宫，以备东巡。他没能成行，在江都被叛军所杀。元代在山东新凿了几段河道，航程缩短约七百公里；明朝又征发十六万五千民夫全线整修。到15世纪中叶，一万一千多艘官营漕船每年北运四百万石漕粮，驾船的官兵有十二万多人。

1444年，南端往来的船只都汇集在城北的湖墅码头。运河、西塘河与余杭塘河三水汇合处的北新桥上设有北新关，是运河七大钞关之一，向每一艘过往的船只收税。1496年，主事刘景寅筑起一座伸入运河三丈的石砌高台，两侧有台阶，商人报关不必再攀爬倾颓的河岸。运河船只经城东的龙山闸出入钱塘江。1631年，三孔石拱桥拱宸桥在湖墅落成，桥长92米，是杭州城里最大的石拱桥，也是大运河到杭州的终点标志，桥名取迎敬帝王之意。乾隆帝1751至1784年六下江南，六次都到杭州；他的祖父康熙帝此前也曾六次南巡。

en:
Tradition says Meng Jiangnu walked a thousand li to bring winter clothes to her husband on the frontier, found that he had died working on the wall, and wept until a stretch of it fell down. The tale keeps the memory of the labour levies behind the first walls. From the seventh century BC the northern states raised stamped-earth ramparts against the steppe, and the Qin first emperor linked them under Meng Tian, who held the new line with 300,000 men.
