By 1444 the Ming were building their own system along the Nine Garrisons, from the Shanhai Pass on the eastern sea to the Jiayu Pass at the edge of the desert, a chain of earth dykes, forts and beacon mounds that passed alarms by smoke in daylight and fire after dark.

After the Tumu disaster of 1449 the court accepted that the Mongols held the Ordos and built along its southern rim. Yu Zijun argued for walls for years against ministers who preferred to attack, and in 1474 forty thousand men raised more than two thousand li of wall and 800 towers and posts in a few months, from Hengcheng on the Yellow River past the Ningxia salt town of Huamachi to Qingshuiying in Shaanxi. Ningxia's own east-bank wall, 387 li of rammed earth, went up the same year. In 1482 raiders trapped between the double lines were destroyed, which won the border people over to the wall.

After 1567 Qi Jiguang faced the rammed-earth sections near Beijing with brick and built more than a thousand hollow watchtowers between Shanhai and Changping, each stocked with weapons and powder. Europeans knew the wall only from report until the Jesuit Bento de Góis rode overland from India through the Jiayu Pass in 1605. It could not stop a succession war: on 27 May 1644 Wu Sangui opened the gates of Shanhai to the Manchu army. Under the Qing, who ruled the steppe as well as the farmlands, the wall lost its border purpose.
zh:
相传孟姜女千里为戍边的丈夫送寒衣，找到的却是尸骨，哭声哭倒了万里长城的一段城墙。这个故事留下了最早修墙的徭役记忆。公元前7世纪起，北方诸侯国沿边境夯筑土墙防备草原，秦始皇把旧城连成一线，派蒙恬率三十万人驻守新墙。1444年，明朝正沿九边修筑自己的体系，从东海之滨的山海关到大漠边缘的嘉峪关，边墙、城堡和烽燧连成一线，白天燃烟、夜里举火，逐墩传递军情。

1449年土木之变后，朝廷承认河套已在蒙古手中，改沿沙漠南缘筑墙。余子俊力主筑墙，和主张出击的大臣争论多年；1474年，四万人几个月内筑成两千多里边墙和八百处墩台据点，自黄河边的横城经宁夏花马池延伸到陕西清水营。宁夏本省三百八十七里的河东墙全为夯土，同年筑成。1482年一支蒙古入寇骑兵被夹在两道边墙之间歼灭，边民这才服了筑墙之策。

1567年以后，戚继光把北京附近的夯土墙外包青砖，又在山海关至昌平之间修起上千座空心敌台，每座都存得下兵器火药。欧洲人长期只凭传闻知道长城，直到1605年耶稣会士鄂本笃从印度陆路东来，由嘉峪关入境。长城挡不住继统之战：1644年5月27日，吴三桂向满洲大军打开山海关城门。清代同时统治草原与耕地，长城失去了边防的意义。

en:
The banquet hall of Gyeongbokgung stood on forty-eight granite pillars nearly ten metres tall, each carved with a dragon climbing through clouds; a Ryukyuan envoy, the Yongjae chonghwa records, counted them among the three finest sights in Joseon. The hall belonged to the first and principal palace of the dynasty, laid out after Yi Seong-gye moved his capital to Hanyang in 1394. King Taejo set the scholar-official Jeong Do-jeon to name the palace, and Jeong took gyeongbok, 'great blessing', from the Book of Songs, quoting a wish that the lord might enjoy it for ten thousand years. The throne hall Geunjeongjeon, finished the next year, saw five kings crowned, Sejong among them. Sejong made the palace his main residence from the 1420s, and the Hall of Worthies worked beside an astronomical platform and a workshop casting movable type; in 1444 this was the working centre of the dynasty, not a ceremonial shell.

That banquet hall, Gyeonghoeru, rose three storeys on an artificial island in a square pond, rebuilt on a grand scale in 1412, and envoys and officials feasted there. In 1506 a hill named Mansesan was heaped beside the pond, planted with rare flowers and set with miniature fairy palaces, while a barge called the Yellow Dragon carried the king across and silk lanterns floated on the water at night. Fire in 1553 burned out the bedchamber quarter but spared the throne hall and the banquet hall, and 3,700 labourers rebuilt the lost halls within the year. The timber palace burned again in 1592, when the Japanese army took the city; of the banquet hall only the forty-eight carved pillars were left, standing in the abandoned pond.
zh:
景福宫的宴厅庆会楼立在四十八根近十米高的花岗岩石柱上，每根柱身都雕着一条穿云而上的龙；《慵斋丛话》记载，一位琉球使者把这些龙柱列为朝鲜三大壮观之一。宴厅所属的景福宫是朝鲜王朝第一座正宫，1394年李成桂迁都汉阳后兴建。太祖命文臣郑道传为宫殿命名，郑道传从《诗经》取「景福」二字，取「君子万年，介尔景福」之意。正殿勤政殿次年落成，先后有五位国王在此即位，世宗便是其中之一。世宗自15世纪20年代起以景福宫为主要居所，集贤殿在宫中办公，近旁设有观星的简仪台和铸造活字的作坊；1444年的景福宫是王朝真正运转的中枢，不只是行礼的地方。

庆会楼是三层楼阁，立在方形人工湖中的岛上，1412年大举重建，官员和外国使节都在这里赴宴。1506年，湖畔堆起万岁山，移种名花，布置小型仙宫模型，国王乘黄龙舟往来，夜里水面漂放丝绸灯笼。1553年大火烧毁寝殿区，勤政殿和庆会楼却幸存，三千七百名工匠当年就把焚毁的殿阁复建起来。1592年日军入城，木构宫殿再焚，庆会楼只剩四十八根雕花石柱，立在荒废的湖池中。

en:
Uyghur legend gave this shrine its other name. Iparhan, a Kashgarian woman carried off to Beijing after the revolt of 1759, refused to share the emperor's bed and was said to have killed herself; her coffin was then carried back from Beijing to Kashgar and buried among her kin. Chinese tellings made her a woman born with a strange natural scent, the Fragrant Concubine, and the mausoleum came to be called the Xiangfei Tomb.

The Afaq Khoja Mausoleum stands five kilometres northeast of Kashgar, at the village of Ayziret, and is the holiest Muslim shrine of the Tarim oases. It was begun around 1640 by the Naqshbandi master Hidayat Allah, better known as Afaq Khoja, as the tomb of his father Muhammad Yusuf, an Andijani khoja who had brought the order into Altishahr early in the century. A tiled dome seventeen metres high rises over the tomb chamber, ringed by four corner minarets banded with arabesques, and the grave platforms inside are glazed blue and draped in coloured silks. Around it lie four prayer halls on wooden beams, a lecture hall, a cemetery and a pool where visitors washed before entering.

Afaq Khoja led the White Mountain faction of the Naqshbandi order, and he returned with Galdan's Dzungar army in 1680 to make himself master of the oasis cities. When he died in 1695 he was laid beside his father, and the mazar came to hold the graves of five generations and 72 members of the family. The brothers Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan were the last of the line to take the field, and the Qing crushed their revolt in 1759. Even so the Qianlong Emperor issued an edict in 1760 ordering the old khoja tombs at Kashgar guarded, kept free of woodcutting and pollution, and repaired at official expense.
zh:
维吾尔民间的传说给了这座麻札另一个名字。回疆女子伊帕尔罕在1759年的叛乱平定后被送往北京，不肯侍奉乾隆帝，相传自尽而死，灵柩又被从北京运回喀什噶尔，葬在族人中间。汉地后来把她传成天生异香的香妃，这座麻札也就被俗称为香妃墓。

阿帕克和卓麻札（阿巴和加麻札）在喀什噶尔东北五公里的艾孜热特村，是塔里木盆地诸绿洲最受尊崇的穆斯林圣迹。纳合昔班底教团的圣裔伊达雅图勒拉，即阿帕克和卓，约在1640年为其父玛木特·玉素布修建此墓；玉素布是来自安集延的和卓，17世纪初把教团传入回疆。十七米高的瓷砖穹顶罩着墓室，四角立着缠着阿拉伯式花纹色带的宣礼塔，室内的墓座覆着蓝釉、披着彩色丝绸。陵墓四周另有四座木梁礼拜殿、一座讲经堂、一片公墓，以及供人进门前净身的水池。

阿帕克和卓是纳合昔班底白山派的首领，1680年随噶尔丹的准噶尔军队返回回疆，成为诸城之主；1695年死后葬在父亲身旁，麻札中先后入葬家族五代七十二人。家族末裔波罗尼都、霍集占兄弟是最后起兵的和卓，1759年叛清被平，乾隆帝却在1760年颁旨，命人看守喀什噶尔旧和卓的坟墓，禁止樵采污秽，修葺之事也由官府经办。

en:
Salvador, founded by Tomé de Sousa in 1549 on the bluff above the Bay of All Saints, was a fortress with a town inside it, and its earliest grand buildings were the Jesuits'. Manuel da Nóbrega came in the first fleet and opened a college for boys on the Terreiro de Jesus, its first chapel built of mud and thatch; once the bishopric was created, a mud church of Our Lady of Help served as the first cathedral. Governor Mem de Sá replaced it with a masonry church that the Jesuit Fernão Cardim later found furnished with damask and velvet hangings, silver crosses and reliquaries. The present church is the fourth on that ground and was consecrated in 1672. Its walls and floors are pale lioz limestone shipped from Lisbon, and of its thirteen altars the high altar, carved by the lay brother João Correia, is one of the few Mannerist altars in Brazil.

The upper-town squares also held the pelourinho, the stone pillory: the post of royal justice and the place where enslaved people were lashed, and the district around it kept the pillory's name. After the Dutch occupation of the 1620s the religious orders rebuilt in the full manner of the Brazilian baroque. The Franciscans' new church was begun in 1686 and its twin towers were finished only in 1797; the interior is among the most gold-covered in the Americas. On the Itapagipe peninsula stood the image of Nosso Senhor do Bonfim, brought from Portugal by the captain Teodósio Rodrigues de Faria in 1745 and moved into the Bonfim church when its interior was finished. By the early nineteenth century pilgrims wore fitinhas, ribbons cut to the length of the image's right arm to its chest.
zh:
巴伊亚的萨尔瓦多城由托梅·德·索萨1549年建于万圣湾上方的高崖上，与其说是一座城，不如说是要塞里装下的一座城，而城里最早的宏大建筑出自耶稣会之手。曼努埃尔·达·诺布雷加随首批船队到来，在耶稣广场办起男童学院，最早的礼拜堂是泥墙草顶；主教区设立后，同样泥草结构的阿茹达圣母堂成了第一任主教座堂。总督曼·德·萨后来把它换成砖石教堂，耶稣会士费尔南·卡尔丁后来见到堂内的陈设：锦缎和天鹅绒挂饰，银十字架和圣骨匣。现存这座教堂已是同一地点上的第四座，1672年祝圣启用；墙面和地坪用从里斯本船运而来的浅色莱奥兹石灰岩砌成，十三座祭坛中，世俗修士若昂·科雷亚雕成的主祭坛是巴西少有的风格主义祭坛之一。

高城的广场上还立着佩洛里尼奥，即石质刑柱：它代表王法，也是黑奴受鞭刑的地方，周围这片街区后来就以刑柱为名。1620年代荷兰人占据之后，各修会按巴西巴洛克的全盛气派把教堂重修一新。方济各会的新教堂1686年动工，双塔直到1797年才完工，内部遍覆金箔，是美洲金饰最盛的教堂之一。伊塔帕日佩半岛上供奉着邦芬耶稣像，它由船长特奥多齐奥·罗德里格斯·德·法里亚1745年从葡萄牙携来，待邦芬教堂内部落成后移奉其中。到十九世纪初，朝圣者已在腕上系许愿丝带，长度取圣像右臂到胸口的距离。

en:
The Cerro Rico de Potosi is a bare red cone of almost 4,800 metres above the Villa Imperial, ore so abundant that the friar Diego de Ocana, who saw it at the end of the sixteenth century, called it the eighth wonder of the world. He measured the mountain's base with a cord, 11,033 varas around, and watched 8,000 Indians working its galleries by tallow candle. In the first years after 1545 the hill yielded native silver rich enough to need only smelting, done in guayras, the ancient clay wind furnaces small as flowerpots; thousands of them stood on pedestals across the slopes, burning charcoal and llama dung in the cold mountain wind. When the high-grade ore ran short, mercury amalgamation let the miners work poorer rock; the mercury came from Huancavelica, and in 1609 a better pan process was devised at Potosi itself. The workings followed the veins more than 1,100 metres below the summit, and the mountaintop was cut away for its ore, giving the cone the silhouette it carried through the colonial centuries.

The Crown took a fifth of every mark of silver, and the mountain drew every kind of man. From 1622 to 1625 the Basque mine-owners fought an open street war with the Vicunas, a faction of Andeans, Portuguese and non-Basque Spaniards, for control of the workings, until Madrid imposed a peace sealed by a marriage between the leaders' children. Catalina de Erauso, the runaway nun who served across the Andes as soldier and llama driver, was in Potosi in those same years. Miners called the hill the one that eats men. In 1719 a typhoid epidemic killed some 22,000 people and tens of thousands more left the city; after 1776, when the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata was created, the silver trains were turned from Arica towards Buenos Aires, fifty-five days away on horseback.
zh:
波托西富饶山是波托西皇家城上方一座近4800米高的红色秃峰，矿脉之富，使16世纪末亲眼见过它的修士迭戈·德·奥卡尼亚称之为「世界第八奇迹」。他用绳索量过山脚，一周长11033巴拉，并看到8000名印第安人就着牛油烛火在坑道里劳作。1545年后的头几年，山里的天然银高品位到只需熔炼；炼银由印第安冶炼匠用古老的瓦伊拉风炉完成，那是花盆般大小的黏土炉，数千座立在墩座上、布满山坡，借着高寒山风燃烧木炭和骆马粪。高品位矿渐少之后，水银混汞法让低品位矿石也能取银，水银由万卡韦利卡供应；1609年，波托西本地又发明了更合用的槽碾混汞法。矿洞沿矿脉深入山顶以下1100多米，连峰顶也被凿开采矿，锥形山的轮廓在殖民时代就此定型。

王室对银产征收五分之一的五一税，银山也引来了各色人等。1622至1625年，巴斯克矿主同「小羊驼」派在街巷里公开开战，后者由安第斯人、葡萄牙人和非巴斯克西班牙人混成，双方争夺矿权，直到马德里强行议和，以两派首领子女联姻收场。那些年里，逃出修道院、女扮男装在安第斯各地当兵赶骆马的卡塔利娜·德·埃劳索也在波托西。矿工把这座山叫作「吃人的山」。1719年，一场伤寒夺去约2.2万人的性命，又有数万人弃城而去；1776年拉普拉塔总督区设立后，运银车队不再走阿里卡，改道骑马需55天才能抵达的布宜诺斯艾利斯。

en:
No chronicle, grant or tax paper names Machu Picchu. Late-sixteenth-century Spanish officials only heard Indians speak of returning to a place called Huayna Picchu, which may have been its Inca name. High above the Urubamba, 80 kilometres north-west of Cuzco, it sits on a granite saddle between two peaks at 2,430 metres, the river curling around it on three sides at the foot of cliffs 450 metres deep. Pachacuti ordered the estate built after his conquest of the lower Urubamba valley, and radiocarbon dates put the first occupation around 1420 to 1440, earlier than the 1450 once assumed.

Roughly two hundred buildings went up on parallel terraces around a central square: palaces and storehouses, the Temple of the Three Windows with its white granite wall, and the Intihuatana stone, 'the place where the sun is tied', aligned with the peaks around it. The granite was quarried on the mountain itself and fitted without mortar, with trapezoidal doors and rounded corners that let the walls flex through earthquakes on a ridge crossed by two fault lines. About 750 people kept the estate running, most of them yanacona retainers brought from coastal, highland and Amazonian communities, with a few hundred left to keep it through the harsh winter.

The estate was a seasonal retreat of the Sapa Inca and his court, and it did not pass to his successor. It was used for about eighty years. Then the court stopped coming, as the war between Atahualpa and Huascar, the smallpox that ran ahead of the Europeans and the fall of Cuzco emptied the ridge, possibly before any Spaniard climbed it. The latest radiocarbon dates stop around 1530. While encomiendas and roads took shape across the conquered empire around it, the terraces went back to cloud forest, and no Spanish column left a clear record of ever reaching the saddle above the Urubamba.
zh:
没有一部编年史、授地文书或税册提到马丘比丘。16世纪末的西班牙官员只听印第安人说起，他们要回一处叫瓦伊纳比丘的地方，这可能就是它的印加旧名。马丘比丘在库斯科西北80公里、海拔2430米处，坐落在两座山峰之间的花岗岩鞍部，乌鲁班巴河从三面环绕，崖壁直落450米才到河面。帕查库特征服乌鲁班巴河下游谷地后，下令在此修建王家别业，碳十四测年把最早的住人时间定在1420至1440年前后，比过去认定的1450年更早。

约200座建筑沿平行台地、围着中央广场排开：宫殿、仓库、白花岗岩砌墙的三窗庙，还有与四周群峰对齐的因蒂瓦塔纳石，克丘亚语意为「拴住太阳之处」。花岗岩就地开采，干砌咬合、不用灰浆，门窗呈梯形、墙角磨圆，墙体可在地震中轻微错动，而这道山脊正从两条断层上穿过。维持别业运转的约有750人，多数是从沿海、高原和亚马孙社群征来的亚纳科纳侍从，严酷的冬季只留几百人看守。

这座别业是萨帕·印卡和宫廷的季节性行宫，不传给继位君主，被使用了约80年。后来宫廷不再到来：阿塔瓦尔帕与瓦斯卡尔的内战、先于欧洲人蔓延的天花，再加上库斯科陷落，使山脊人去台空，时间可能早于任何西班牙人登临。最晚的碳十四年代止于1530年前后。被征服帝国的各处都在兴建监护地、整修道路，这道山脊上的梯田却重新没入云雾林，也没有一支西班牙队伍留下过登上乌鲁班巴河上方这处鞍部的明确记载。

en:
The Chimu told that the Sun laid three eggs, gold for the lords, silver for their wives and copper for the rest, and Spanish accounts report that the royal walls were sheathed with panels of gold. At the centre of Chan Chan the Chimu raised ten rectangular ciudadelas, one walled royal compound for each king. Each had a single narrow gate on its north side and adobe walls that reached twelve metres, five metres thick at the foot and only one at the crown, the trapezoidal batter built for the earthquakes of this coast. Inside, every compound followed the same plan: a northern plaza ringed with low stone benches, U-shaped audiencias where officials received business, rows of storehouses for tribute and a domestic quarter with its own well. At the middle stood a low truncated pyramid, the burial platform that held the dead lord, most of them dug open and emptied in the first years after the conquest. In the best-preserved compound, Nik An, moulded friezes cover the walls: waves, nets, pelicans, and fish swimming north and south, read as the cold Humboldt current meeting the warm El Nino flow. The palaces also enclosed deep stone-lined ponds dug down to the water table for rites of the sea cult.

After the Inca conquest around 1470 the compounds lost their court and their kings, and the Spanish town of Trujillo soon rose beside them. Through the whole Viceroyalty treasure hunters came back to the adobe walls again and again, on the conviction that the hoard of the Chimu was still hidden behind them. The sun-baked mud, raised on a coast where whole years pass without rain, softened in the rare El Nino downpours, and the moulded fish and nets slowly lost their edges. The name of the deserted city first entered Spanish paper in the Trujillo town council's act of 1536, written as Cauchan.
zh:
奇穆人相传太阳生下三颗蛋：金蛋归君王，银蛋归君王的妻妾，铜蛋归其余的人；据西班牙人记载，王宫的墙壁还曾镶有金板。昌昌城塞的中心，奇穆人建起十座长方形城寨，每一位国王拥有一座带围墙的王宫。每座城寨只在北面开一道窄门，土坯墙高达12米，墙基厚5米，墙顶仅1米，梯形收分是为这条多震海岸的地震而修。城寨内部都按同样的格局分划：北面是四周环以矮石凳的广场，接着是官员受理事务的U形听政所、一排排贡物库房和带井的家居区；中央立着一座低矮的截顶金字塔，即安葬故王的陵台，大多数陵台在征服最初的年头就被挖空。保存最完好的尼基·安城寨墙面覆满模压浮雕：海浪、渔网、鹈鹕，还有分别朝南朝北游的鱼，被解读为寒冷的洪堡洋流与温暖的厄尔尼诺洋流相会。王宫区还围有挖到地下水位的石砌深塘，用于海洋崇拜的仪式。

约1470年印加征服后，城寨失去了宫廷和国王，西班牙人的特鲁希略很快在它们旁边建起。整个总督区时期，盗宝者一再回到土坯墙前，认定奇穆的宝藏还藏在墙后。烈日晒干的泥土本是为整年少雨的海岸而生，遇上厄尔尼诺年的罕见暴雨便松软剥落，模压出来的鱼和渔网渐渐磨平了边缘。这座废城的名字第一次落进西班牙文书，是1536年特鲁希略市政会的文件，写作「考昌」。

en:
The Qhapaq Nan, the royal road of the Incas, ran some 40,000 kilometres without a wheel or a horse. Two arteries set out from Cuzco for the four quarters of the Tawantinsuyu: the coastal road hugged the foothills from Tumbes southward, while the high road held the puna grasslands above 4,000 metres, through Quito, Tumebamba and Huanuco, then past Lake Titicaca to Mendoza, 5,658 kilometres from end to end. Much of it was older than the Incas, rebuilt from Wari and Tiwanaku roads; Pachacuti's engineers began the great expansion around 1438, and in 1444 the northern terminus at Quito still lay beyond the Inca frontier, until Tupac Yupanqui carried the high road there around 1463.

On steep slopes the road was cut into steps. Rivers were crossed on log and slab bridges, on pontoons of tied totora reeds, in oroya baskets slung across gaps wider than 50 metres, and on grass-rope suspension bridges. The Apurimac bridge spanned 45 metres, and its ichu cables were renewed by mita labour every two years, when the old bridge was cut into the river. Llama caravans carried freight, and chasqui runners waited at posts to relay messages, quipus and fresh goods day and night. Tambos lodged officials a day's march apart, and qullqa warehouses held the tribute, 497 at Huanuco Pampa alone. Cieza de Leon, who travelled the road in the 1540s, wrote that it was 'everywhere clean, swept, clear of debris, full of dwellings, warehouses for valuable goods, temples of the Sun, relay stations'.

The conquistadors rode it into the empire: Almagro's Chile expedition followed it south from Cuzco. Horses and mules wore the paved steps and strained the rope bridges, and as the native population collapsed the maintenance mita lapsed; in 1553 Cieza found stretches broken, though they still showed 'the great thing that it was'. Surviving sections carried mule trains of Potosi silver to the coast, while branches to old fortresses and administrative centres grew over.
zh:
印加路网（Qhapaq Nan，克丘亚语意为「王家大道」）全长约4万公里，路上没有轮子，也没有马。两条主干道从库斯科伸向塔万廷苏尤的四方：沿海大道贴着山麓从通贝斯向南延伸；高原大道行在海拔4000米以上的普纳草原上，经基多、图梅班巴、瓦努科，绕过的的喀喀湖通向门多萨，全长5658公里。道路大半比印加更古老，是在瓦里和蒂亚瓦纳科古道的基础上整修连接而成；约1438年，帕查库提的工匠开始大规模扩建。1444年，大道北端的基多还在印加边界之外，约1463年图帕克·尤潘基才把高原大道修到那里。

陡坡上的路面凿成石阶。过河有木桥、石板桥，有把托托拉芦苇捆扎成的浮桥，有用吊篮越过50多米深谷的奥罗亚，还有草绳悬索桥。阿普里马克河上的索桥跨度45米，承重的伊楚草绳每两年由米塔役工更换一次，旧桥当场斩断、落入河中。骆马队驮运货物，查斯基信使在驿站等候，昼夜接力传递奇普文书和时鲜货物；相隔一天路程的坦博驿馆接待官员；科尔卡仓库存放贡物，仅瓦努科潘帕就有497座。16世纪40年代行经这条路的谢萨·德·莱昂写道，它「处处整洁，清扫干净，满是住宅、存放贵重货物的仓库、太阳神殿和驿站」。

征服者也沿着这条路进入他们正拆解的帝国：阿尔马格罗远征智利，就是从库斯科顺大道南下。马蹄和骡蹄磨损石阶、拉扯索桥，随着原住民人口锐减，养护道路的米塔也废弛了；1553年谢萨见到大段路面已经崩坏，却仍能看出「它当年的宏伟」。保留下来的路段改由骡队驮运波托西白银下山、前往海岸，而通往要塞和旧行政中心的支线，大多重新长满了荒草。

en:
For its first half-century Cartagena had no walls, and raiders knew it. The French sacked the open town in 1544; John Hawkins bombarded it for eight days and Martin Cote ransacked it the next year. After Francis Drake burned the city in 1586, Philip II put the engineer Bautista Antonelli in charge of the Caribbean defences, and the walled Cartagena he planned took two centuries to finish. Bastions and curtain walls girdled the old city, and Governor Francisco de Murga later enclosed Getsemaní too, its one gate and causeway covered by the Media Luna, the Half Moon battery. Inside the bay, forts commanded each shipping passage, and between Manzanillo and Castillo Grande a floating chain could close the water.

The landward core of the system was the Castillo San Felipe de Barajas on San Lázaro hill, a triangle of eight batteries raised largely by enslaved Africans and completed in 1654. The seaward gate was the Bocachica narrows: in 1640 three Portuguese ships ran aground in the old Bocagrande passage and their wrecks raised a sandbar, after which San Luis and San José covered Bocachica from either shore. The sea works had their failures. Pointis overran San Luis in 1697 when it held only thirty men, breached the Half Moon Gate and sacked the city for a month. In 1741 Edward Vernon forced the same channel with a vastly larger force and broke his army below San Felipe. The admiral commanding the defence, Blas de Lezo, had lost an eye, the use of an arm and a leg in earlier battles, and refused to wear an eyepatch. Antonio de Arévalo then rebuilt the gate and laid a 3,400-yard underwater stone jetty, the Escollera, across Bocagrande, while San Felipe gained underground corridors that let its garrison move within the hill unseen.
zh:
建城后的头半个世纪，卡塔赫纳一道城墙也没有，袭掠者对此一清二楚。1544年法国人洗劫了不设防的城镇；约翰·霍金斯连续炮击八天，次年马丁·科特又来劫掠。1586年弗朗西斯·德雷克纵火焚城，腓力二世才把加勒比诸港的防务交给军事工程师巴蒂斯塔·安东内利，他设计的环城城防此后施工了两百年。老城用棱堡和幕墙一圈圈围起，总督弗朗西斯科·德·穆尔加后来又把赫塞马尼区圈进墙内，该区唯一的城门与堤道由半月炮台封锁。内湾里，要塞逐一把各条通航水道置于炮火之下，曼萨尼约与卡斯蒂约格兰德两处堡垒之间，还能拉起一道横过水面的漂浮铁链。

陆地一侧的核心，是圣拉萨罗山上的圣费利佩·德·巴拉哈斯城堡：三角形堡体上布有八座炮台，石料的开采和垒砌大多由被奴役的黑人承担，1654年建成。海上大门是博卡奇卡窄口：1640年，三艘葡萄牙船在旧的博卡格兰德航道搁浅，沉船淤出沙洲，此后圣路易斯堡和圣何塞堡在两岸夹住博卡奇卡。这些海上工事并非无懈可击。1697年，普安蒂男爵趁圣路易斯堡只有三十名守军，一举将其攻破，又轰开半月门，洗劫城市一个月。1741年，爱德华·弗农以悬殊的兵力同样闯入这条水道，陆军却在圣费利佩堡脚下撞得粉碎。指挥守城的海军上将布拉斯·德·莱索，早年的战斗中已丢了一只眼睛、一条腿，一只胳膊也不能动，却不肯戴眼罩遮掩。战后安东尼奥·德·阿雷瓦洛重修海口，在博卡格兰德铺出一条3400码长的水下石堤，称作埃斯科列拉；圣费利佩堡也增建了地下廊道，守军可以在山体内部隐蔽调动。

en:
Only about 80 kilometres of jungle and swamp separate the Caribbean from the Pacific at Panama, and for three centuries after 1492 every maritime power in Europe dreamed of cutting through them. Vasco Nunez de Balboa crossed the isthmus in 1513 and became the first European to see the South Sea. A paved royal road then carried the silver of Peru by mule from Panama to Nombre de Dios and Portobelo, while ships still had to round South America. In 1524 Charles I ordered a waterway studied, but the wars in Europe and the engineering of the time killed the plan. The Jesuit Jose de Acosta argued that one ocean lay lower than the other and that a cut would serve Spain's rivals as much as Spain, and the Council of the Indies let the idea die in debate.

The one real attempt was Scotland's. The Company of Scotland raised about 400,000 pounds in a few weeks from every level of society, roughly a fifth of all the money in the kingdom. In July 1698 five ships sailed from Leith with some 1,200 settlers and founded New Edinburgh on the Gulf of Darien, calling the colony New Caledonia. William Paterson, who had promoted the scheme, meant it as a free port on an overland passage between the two oceans, open to the trade of China and Japan. Fever and hunger emptied the settlement within a year, and a second expedition found only ruins. Spanish forces blockaded the harbour, the last Scots gave up, and four hundred of them lay buried behind them. The loss ruined the Lowland burghs and did much to push Scotland into the Act of Union with England in 1707.

After that the canal lived on only on paper. In 1811 Alexander von Humboldt weighed five possible cuts across Central America and judged Nicaragua, with its great freshwater lake, the most promising line. No spade had gone into the ground at Panama by 1821; French and then American engineers opened the waterway on 15 August 1914.
zh:
巴拿马运河要穿过的那条地峡，最窄处只有约80公里，连绵的丛林与沼泽把加勒比海和太平洋隔开；1492年以后的三百年里，欧洲每个海上强国都想把它切开。1513年，巴斯科·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚越过地峡，成为第一个望见南海的欧洲人。此后一条铺石的王家大道用骡队把秘鲁白银从巴拿马城驮往农布雷-德迪奥斯和波托韦洛，船只却仍要绕行南美洲南端。1524年卡洛斯一世下令研究水道，欧洲的战事和当时的工程技术断送了这个计划。耶稣会士何塞·德·阿科斯塔提出，两个大洋一高一低，而且运河对西班牙对手的好处不比对西班牙少；印度事务委员会议来议去，让这个想法不了了之。

真正动过手的只有苏格兰。苏格兰公司几周之内从社会各阶层筹到约40万英镑，相当于全国流通货币的五分之一。1698年7月，五艘船载着约一千二百名拓殖者从利斯启航，在达连湾建起新爱丁堡，把殖民地叫作新喀里多尼亚。策划者威廉·佩特森要把它建成两洋陆路通道上的自由港，同中国和日本通商。热病和饥饿在一年之内掏空了定居点，第二支远征队到达时只见废墟。西班牙军队封锁了港口，最后一批苏格兰人撤走，身后留下四百座坟墓。这笔损失拖垮了低地各城，也是苏格兰1707年同英格兰签订《联合条约》的重要推手。

此后运河只活在纸面上。1811年，亚历山大·冯·洪堡比较了中美洲的五条可能线路，断定有巨大淡水湖可用的尼加拉瓜最有希望。到1821年，巴拿马的泥土一锹未动；这条水道最终由法国、继而由美国的工程师开凿，于1914年8月15日通航。

en:
Tikal, which its inscriptions name Yax Mutal, lies in the rainforest of the Peten Basin, on parallel limestone ridges above swampy lowland, and it had no river. Ten plastered reservoirs caught the rain, and raised causeways ran between the plazas and temple groups. The mapped centre covers about 16 square kilometres and holds roughly 3,000 structures; the stelae of the Great Plaza and the North Acropolis carry Long Count dates and the biographies of some 33 rulers across six centuries.

Those stones record the city's wars. On 14 January 378 the ruler Chak Tok Ich'aak was killed on the very day a westerner called Siyah K'ak' entered Tikal, backed by arms and emblems from distant Teotihuacan, and within the year a new king, Yax Nuun Ayiin, sat on the throne. After Calakmul and Caracol defeated Tikal in 562, no dated stela went up for about 130 years, and old sculptures were smashed. Then Jasaw Chan K'awiil I broke the rival power in 695. He lies under Temple I, the Temple of the Great Jaguar, which rises in nine stepped tiers for the nine levels of the underworld and carries a roof comb with the seated king. His tomb held jaguar skins, jade, spondylus shells and a jade necklace of 114 large beads weighing 3.9 kilogrammes. Temple IV, built for his son, counts among the tallest buildings the Maya raised. By the tenth century the city was empty and the forest had grown over its plazas.

In 1444 the Great Plaza had lain under the canopy for five hundred years. Hernan Cortes marched within a few kilometres of the ruins in 1525 on his way to Honduras and never mentioned them. In 1696 the Franciscan Andres de Avendano, lost in the Peten forest, described a ruin that may have been Tikal. Local Maya knew the site all along, but through the whole colonial period no European party stood in the Great Plaza.
zh:
蒂卡尔，铭文里写作亚什·穆塔尔，坐落在佩滕盆地的雨林中，城建在数道平行的石灰岩高脊上，四周是沼泽低地，城里没有河。十座抹灰水库蓄积雨水，抬高的石砌堤道连接各广场和神庙群。已测绘的中心区约16平方公里，分布着约三千座建筑；大广场和北卫城的石碑刻着长纪历日期和大约33位统治者的生平，前后六个世纪。

这些石头记着这座城的战事。公元378年1月14日，国王查克·托克·伊查克被杀，恰在同一天，一个叫西亚赫·卡克的外来者带着远方特奥蒂瓦坎的武器和徽记入城，不到一年，新王亚什·农·阿因就坐上了王位。562年卡拉克穆尔联合卡拉科尔打败蒂卡尔，此后约一百三十年没有再立纪年石碑，旧雕塑也被砸毁。后来贾索·钱·卡维尔一世在695年击垮了世仇。他安葬在一号神庙，也就是大美洲豹神庙之下：神庙九层台阶对应冥界的九层，顶冠雕着端坐的国王。墓里有美洲豹皮、玉石、海菊蛤贝，还有一条114颗大珠串成的玉项链，重3.9公斤。为他的儿子建的四号神庙，是马雅人最高大的建筑之一。到10世纪，城已空掉，雨林长回了广场。

1444年，大广场被树冠遮盖已有五百年。1525年，埃尔南·科尔特斯进军洪都拉斯时在遗址数公里外经过，只字未提。1696年，方济各会士安德烈斯·德·阿文达尼奥在佩滕林中迷路，描述过一处遗址，可能就是蒂卡尔。当地马雅人一直知道这座城，但整个殖民时代，没有一队欧洲人走到过大广场。

en:
The name means 'at the mouth of the well of the Itza', and water made the city: northern Yucatan has no surface rivers, and four cenotes, the sink-wells of the limestone plain, gave Chichen water all year. The largest, the Sacred Cenote, is about 60 metres across, and post-conquest Maya and Spanish sources describe offerings and human victims cast into it to the rain god Chaac. The Temple of Kukulkan, called El Castillo by the first Spaniards, rises 30 metres in nine terraces with feathered-serpent heads at the foot of its balustrades; on equinox afternoons a shadow like a serpent runs down the north stair. Nearby is the Great Ball Court, 168 by 70 metres, the largest in ancient Mesoamerica, with a panel showing a beheaded player whose blood streams away as serpents.

The Itza, whose name the locals glossed as 'those who speak our language brokenly', made Chichen the leading city of northern Yucatan, trading through its port of Isla Cerritos for obsidian from central Mexico and gold from the south. Its power faded around 1100. The Books of Chilam Balam remember Hunac Ceel, thrown into the Sacred Cenote with no expectation of survival: he climbed out and prophesied his own rise, and later chronicles made him the conqueror of Chichen. In 1444 the city was no capital, but in years of drought the cenote still drew pilgrims.

Francisco de Montejo the Younger reached the ruins in late 1532 with the stated aim of founding his capital there, and renamed the place Ciudad Real. The Maya let him divide the land, then besieged him among the ruins; a sortie cost him 150 men, and he slipped away in the dark. In the drought of 1536 the Xiu lords of Mani set out on pilgrimage to the Sacred Cenote to pray for rain. They needed passage through Sotuta, and Nachi Cocom granted safe conduct, then had the pilgrims killed at the village of Otzmal. By 1588 Chichen Itza was a working cattle ranch.
zh:
奇琴伊察的名字意为「伊察人的井口」，这座城因水而兴：尤卡坦北部没有地表河，四口天然井（石灰岩平原上塌陷形成的溶井）为奇琴供着全年不断的淡水。最大的圣井直径约60米，征服后的马雅和西班牙资料都记载，人们把祭品甚至活人投进井中，献给雨神查克。库库尔坎金字塔被最早的西班牙人叫作「城堡」，高30米，九层台基，栏杆底端雕着羽蛇头；春分秋分的下午，北面台阶上的影子像一条蛇顺梯而下。旁边的大球场长168米、宽70米，是古代马雅世界最大的球场，墙上一幅浮雕刻着被斩首的球员，血化成蛇流开。

伊察人的名字，当地人解释为「说我们的话结结巴巴的人」，他们让奇琴成了北尤卡坦的首城，借北岸港口塞里托斯岛做贸易，换来中墨西哥的黑曜石和南方的黄金。它的势力约在1100年前后衰落。《奇兰·巴兰之书》记着乌纳克·塞尔的故事：他被投进圣井，本无生理，却爬了出来，预言自己将要掌权，后来的史书把他写成奇琴的征服者。1444年，这里已不是都城，但大旱之年圣井仍吸引朝圣者。

1532年底，小弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍抵达遗址，目的从一开始就是在此建都，把它改名「王家城」。马雅人起初任他分地，随后把他围困在废城之中；一次出击折了150人，他趁夜色逃走。1536年大旱，马尼的休氏首领出发去圣井朝圣求雨，要借道索图塔；纳奇·科科姆许诺安全通行，却在奥斯马尔村杀了朝圣者。到1588年，奇琴伊察已经是一座经营中的养牛牧场。

en:
At the centre of Tenochtitlan stood the Hueyi Teocalli, the Great Temple, which the Mexica understood to be the centre of the universe. Its platform measured about 100 by 80 metres and carried two shrines with separate staircases, one to the war god Huitzilopochtli and one to the rain god Tlaloc. The first temple went up after the city's founding in 1325 and was rebuilt six times. It stood inside a walled square about 500 metres to a side holding some 45 public buildings, among them the tzompantli rack of skulls; beyond the wall rose Moctezuma's palace, its hundred suites each with a bath.

Ahuitzotl rebuilt the temple for its dedication in the year 8 Reed, 1487. Post-conquest accounts claim that 80,400 captives died over four days at four sacrificial tables on the summit; the Codex Telleriano-Remensis puts the figure at about 4,000, and scholarly estimates run from 10,000 to 80,400. In June 1520 the Spaniards fought up the temple's 114 steps and were thrown back with about a hundred dead. In the last days of the 1521 siege Spanish soldiers reached the summit, set the two shrines on fire and raised their banners, while below them the Aztecs cut the hearts from 70 prisoners at Huitzilopochtli's altar. The victors dismantled the pyramid and carried its stone off to the houses of the new Spanish city.

One stone survived by going underground. The sun stone, a basalt disc 3.6 metres across and weighing nearly 25 tonnes, had stood part-way up the pyramid; after years on open display it was buried near the Plaza Mayor on the order of Archbishop Montufar, so that the memory of the old rites would die with it. On 17 December 1790 workmen lowering the square struck the disc less than half a metre down. Antonio de Leon y Gama argued it out of reburial and wrote the first study of its carving, and the viceroyalty set the stone into the outer wall of the cathedral, where the Aztec monolith faced the Spanish square.
zh:
特诺奇蒂特兰的中心矗立着韦伊特奥卡利，即大神庙，墨西卡人认为它是宇宙的中心。台基约100米长、80米宽，上面两座神殿各有独立的石阶，一座奉战神威齐洛波契特里，一座奉雨神特拉洛克。第一座神庙建于1325年建城之后，先后重建六次。神庙围在边长约500米的方墙之内，墙里约45座公共建筑，包括头骨架；墙外是蒙特苏马的宫殿，上百个套间各带浴室。

阿维措特尔为1487年芦苇八年的落成礼重建了大神庙。征服后的记载称，四天之内有80400名俘虏在塔顶四张祭桌上被杀；《特列里亚诺-雷曼西斯手抄本》记的数字约为四千人，后世学者估计在一万到80400之间。1520年6月，西班牙人打上神庙的114级台阶，被逼退下来，折了约一百人。1521年围城的最后几天，西班牙士兵登上塔顶，放火烧毁两座神殿，插上自己的旗帜；就在他们脚下，阿兹特克人在威齐洛波契特里的祭坛前挖出70名俘虏的心脏。胜利者拆了金字塔，把石料运去修西班牙新城的宅院。

有一块石头靠埋入地下躲过了这一切。太阳石是玄武岩圆盘，直径3.6米，重近25吨，原来立在金字塔半腰；露天安放多年后，按大主教蒙图法尔之命埋在马约尔广场附近，好让旧仪式的记忆随它一起埋掉。1790年12月17日，工人铲低广场时，在不到半米深的地方撞上这块圆盘。安东尼奥·德·莱昂-加马力争不再把它埋回，写下第一篇研究其雕刻的著作；总督区把它嵌进大教堂外墙，阿兹特克人的独石面对着西班牙人的广场。

en:
The silver of Zacatecas was won with mules and quicksilver. Ore from the mines was crushed to powder, spread over paved patios with salt, copper pyrites and quicksilver, and trodden for weeks by mules and labourers until the silver bound itself to the mercury in an amalgam. The quicksilver travelled under the Crown's monopoly all the way from Almadén in Spain and Huancavelica in Peru, and the refining haciendas stood below the shaft mouths. Indians brought up from the south and black slaves bought for the camps did most of the digging and the treading.

The mine city grew out of the rock itself. Miners drove tunnels into the Cerro de la Bufa and the neighbouring sierras wherever a silver vein showed, and packed their town into the narrow Arroyo de la Plata ravine below, with no regular grid and houses rising several storeys on the steep ground. The first workings, the San Bernabé, opened in 1548, and in 1586 work began on the El Edén mine inside the Bufa itself, which yielded gold and silver for its best two centuries.

The first bonanza ran to the middle of the seventeenth century, after which output flagged as the veins went deeper and the lower galleries flooded. Early in the eighteenth century Zacatecas produced about a fifth of all the silver in the world, and mine owners spent their shares on churches of quarried stone and town houses. To follow the silver down, the Vetagrande company drove a general drainage shaft 360 varas, roughly 300 metres, by 1797.
zh:
萨卡特卡斯矿城的白银是靠骡子和水银炼出来的。矿石碾成粉，拌上盐、铜黄铁矿和水银，铺在石砌的庭院里，由骡子和工人反复踩踏数周，直到银与汞结成汞膏；选矿庄园就建在坑口下方。这些水银受王室专卖，远从西班牙的阿尔马登和秘鲁的万卡韦利卡运来。挖矿、踩矿的，多是从南方征来的土著和为矿区买来的黑奴。

这座矿城几乎是从岩石里长出来的。矿工沿着每一条出露的银脉把坑道打进布法山和周围群峰，又把城镇挤进山下「银溪」峡谷的窄地；这里没有规整的街网，陡坡上的屋子盖到好几层高。最早的圣贝尔纳贝矿坑1548年开工，1586年，埃登矿直接在布法山腹中动工，此后两百年盛产期里金银并出。

第一次景气持续到17世纪中叶，随后矿脉加深、低处巷道被水淹没，产量下滑。18世纪初，萨卡特卡斯出产的白银约占全世界的五分之一，矿主们把分得的财富花在凿石教堂和城市宅邸上。为追逐更深处的银脉，贝塔格兰德公司到1797年凿成一条深达360巴拉（约300米）的总排水井。

en:
The last roof beam at Mesa Verde was felled in 1281, and within a few years the people who cut it had left for good. Mesa Verde is a green table of pinyon and juniper in the canyon country where Colorado, Utah, New Mexico and Arizona draw together, its ravines cut into sandstone that holds whole towns in its alcoves. The farmers later called the Ancient Puebloans lived on the mesa tops for six centuries on corn, beans and squash. In the final decades of the twelfth century, as droughts tightened and clans fought, they moved down into the cliffs. Cliff Palace, the greatest of their works, fills one large alcove with 150 rooms and 23 circular kivas and housed about 125 people; its shaped sandstone walls were painted, and the village faces south-west to catch the low winter sun. Across the mesa they raised about 600 such dwellings.

The great drought of 1276 to 1299 ended the work, and the people went south to the valleys of New Mexico and Arizona; the pueblo peoples of those lands are their descendants. In 1444 the stone villages had been empty for a century and a half. Ute bands hunted across the mesa and wintered on its rims, but held the cliff dwellings sacred and never moved into the rooms, so sand and brush slowly buried them.

The first Europeans to reach the region were two Franciscans, Atanasio Dominguez and Silvestre Velez de Escalante, who in 1776 crossed the Colorado Plateau in search of a road from Santa Fe to Monterey. They saw the high, forested tablelands and named the country Mesa Verde, the green table, but never came at an angle that would have shown the towns in the cliffs. Their map carried the name onward, and for the rest of Spanish rule the mesa stayed a high, empty grazing ground above the silent rooms.
zh:
梅萨维德悬崖村的最后一根房梁砍伐于1281年，几年之后，砍下它的人就离开了，再没回来。梅萨维德是科罗拉多、犹他、新墨西哥、亚利桑那四地相接处的一座绿色台地，台面长满矮松和刺柏，峡谷切进砂岩，崖龛里藏着整座整座的石头村镇。后来被称为古普韦布洛人的农人在台顶生活了六百年，靠玉米、豆子和南瓜为生；12世纪最后几十年，旱灾日深、部族相攻，他们陆续搬到崖壁之下。其中最大的一处是悬崖宫，嵌在一个巨大的岩龛里，有150间房舍和23座圆形基瓦，约住125人；砂岩块砌成的墙壁曾绘着彩画，村舍朝向西南，好接住冬天低垂的日光。整座台地上这样的崖居约有600处。

1276至1299年的大旱终结了营造，居民南迁到新墨西哥和亚利桑那的河谷，那些地方的普韦布洛人就是他们的后人。1444年，这些石头村镇已空了一个半世纪。乌特人的游群在台地上游猎、在崖缘过冬，却把崖居视为圣地，从不搬入那些房舍，任沙土和灌木慢慢将其掩埋。

最早抵达这一带的欧洲人是两名方济各会士，阿塔纳西奥·多明格斯和西尔韦斯特雷·贝莱斯·德·埃斯卡兰特。1776年，他们为寻找从圣菲到蒙特雷的陆路横穿科罗拉多高原，望见高处林木覆盖的台地，把这里取名梅萨维德，意为「绿色的桌子」，却始终没走到能看见崖中村镇的角度。台地的名字随他们的地图传了下去，在西班牙统治余下的年月里，这里仍是一片高处的空旷牧场，底下的房舍无人问津。

en:
Monks Mound rises a hundred feet from the Mississippi bottomlands, and every basket-load of its soil and clay was carried by hand. Around 1100 the Mississippian town at Cahokia covered about six square miles and held roughly a hundred and twenty mounds and fifteen to twenty thousand people; trade brought copper from the Great Lakes and shark teeth and conch shells from the Gulf. The great mound took fifty-five million cubic feet of earth and measures 955 by 775 feet at the base, a footprint about the size of the Great Pyramid's. It climbs in four terraces to a flat summit where a wooden temple stood. A palisade of upright logs with square bastions ran round the central precinct and was rebuilt several times as the town contracted. A century before 1444 the city had emptied, and when Europeans reached the American Bottom the great mound stood grassed and abandoned, its plazas gone back to prairie.

In 1809 a small community of Trappist monks, given land by the French landowner Nicolas Jarrot, settled on a lesser mound beside the great one; French families were already farming the slopes. While they were still there the lawyer and traveller Henry Marie Brackenridge rode out from St. Louis in 1811 and wrote the first careful description of the mound. The sight, he wrote, struck him with an astonishment not unlike what he felt contemplating the Egyptian pyramids, and heaping up such a mass must have taken years and the labour of thousands. His account was printed in 1814 in Views of Louisiana, after he had pressed it in letters to his friend Thomas Jefferson. The earthwork took the name it carries now from the monks who had made their home at its foot.
zh:
僧侣墩从密西西比河泛滥平原上拔起约30米，每一筐泥土和黏土都靠人手搬来。约1100年，卡霍基亚这座密西西比文化城镇方圆约六平方英里，有大小土丘约一百二十座、人口一万五千到两万；贸易把五大湖的铜、墨西哥湾的鲨鱼牙和海螺壳带到这里。大土墩用土五千五百万立方英尺，底边长291米、宽236米，底面积与胡夫金字塔相去不远，分四层台地收束到顶部的平顶，上面曾立着一座木构神庙。中央祭祀区围着一道竖木栅栏，上有方型棱堡；城镇收缩时，栅栏又几度重修、缩小。1444年的一个世纪之前，这座城已经荒空，欧洲人来到阿梅里肯洼地时，大土墩上长满野草，旧日的广场重新变成草原。

1809年，一小群特拉伯苦修会修士经法裔地主尼古拉·雅罗赠予土地，在大土墩旁一座较小的土丘上住下，当时已有法裔家庭在坡面上耕种。他们尚在时，律师兼旅行家亨利·马里·布雷肯里奇于1811年从圣路易斯骑马到此，写下关于这座土墩的第一份细致记述：他说，眼前景象令他惊愕，与凝望埃及金字塔时的感受相去不远；堆起这样一座土山，必耗费多年光阴和数千人的劳作。他先在给友人托马斯·杰斐逊的信中力陈此事，记述后来收入1814年出版的《路易斯安那见闻录》。这座土工也因这群曾在它脚边安家的修士，得名僧侣墩。

en:
The story that white paint was first applied to hide the fire stains is false: the sandstone walls were whitewashed when the house was new, because the porous stone streaked with weather, and the mix was lime, rice glue, casein and lead. Locals were calling it the White House by 1811. In 1444 the lower Potomac was still Algonquian country, with Piscataway villages and canoe landings along the bank. Three and a half centuries on, the Residence Act of July 1790 placed the capital of the new republic on that river, and the award for the president's house went to James Hoban, an Irish-born architect trained in Dublin, whose sober Neoclassical design drew on Dublin's Leinster House. Enslaved African Americans quarried the grey Aquia Creek sandstone in Stafford County, Scottish masons raised the walls, and shortages of labour and money cut the planned three floors to two. George Washington oversaw every stage and died before anyone moved in. John Adams arrived on 1 November 1800 and wrote to Abigail that none but honest and wise men should ever rule under its roof.

Thomas Jefferson added low colonnades with Benjamin Latrobe, screening stables and storerooms, but the house stood barely fourteen years. On 24 August 1814, after the militia broke at Bladensburg, British troops under Robert Ross and George Cockburn burned it in answer to American burnings in Upper Canada. White House employees and enslaved servants carried out the Lansdowne portrait of Washington before the soldiers reached the rooms. The interior was gutted and only the scorched outer walls remained; most of those were taken down and rebuilt, fragments of the south wall excepted. Hoban and Latrobe ran the works, and James Monroe moved back in October 1817.
zh:
那种说白漆最初是为掩盖火烧痕迹才刷上的说法并不属实：房子刚建成时，砂岩墙面就已经刷白，因为多孔的石头容易被雨水浸出污迹，涂料用石灰、米胶、酪蛋白和铅调成。民间至迟在1811年已经管它叫白宫。1444年，波托马克河下游还是阿尔冈昆人的地界，河岸上散布着皮斯卡塔韦人的村落和独木舟泊地。三个半世纪后，1790年7月的《首都选址法》把新生共和国的首都定在这条河边，总统府的设计由出生于爱尔兰、曾在都柏林受训的建筑师詹姆斯·霍本中选，他那栋素雅的新古典主义宅邸以都柏林的伦斯特府为蓝本。被奴役的黑人在弗吉尼亚斯塔福德县的阿奎亚溪采出灰色砂岩，苏格兰石匠砌起墙体，因为缺工缺钱，原计划的三层缩成两层。全程督造的乔治·华盛顿没能等到有人入住。1800年11月1日，约翰·亚当斯成为这里的主人，他在给妻子阿比盖尔的信里写道，愿此后在这屋顶下主政的人，个个诚实而明智。

杰斐逊入住后和建筑师本杰明·拉特罗布在两侧加了低矮柱廊，遮住马厩和库房，但这房子只立了十四年。1814年8月24日，民兵在布拉登斯堡溃散后，罗伯特·罗斯和乔治·科伯恩率英军入城，为报复美军在上加拿大的纵火，放火烧了总统府。白宫的雇员和黑奴抢在士兵进屋前，把吉尔伯特·斯图尔特所绘的华盛顿兰斯当肖像搬了出去。室内烧得精光，只剩熏黑的外墙；这些墙后来也大多拆毁重建，只有南墙的几段保留下来。霍本和拉特罗布主持了重建，1817年10月詹姆斯·门罗重新入住。

en:
On the treeless tundra west of Hudson Bay, where a traveller can walk for days without meeting a landmark, a row of stones could pass for a file of hunters. In the caribou drive, rows of inuksuit were strung across a valley like standing men, sometimes dressed with sod and feathers that stirred in the wind. The migrating herd took the stones for people and turned the way the hunters wanted, towards bowmen hidden on land or kayakers waiting at a river crossing.

The word joins inuk, 'person', and -suk, 'substitute': 'that which acts in the capacity of a human'. The simplest cairn is a single stone set upright, while others are careful piles several stones high, sometimes six or seven feet tall, raised by a whole camp at once. They marked the safe line across ice and open country, the fishing place on a lake, the camp and the meat cache. In 1444 this was already an old device and still a living one. A cluster of about a hundred cairns at Enukso Point on Baffin Island may have been begun two thousand years earlier, and the Ahiarmiut bands of the Barren Lands kept raising their own.
zh:
哈得孙湾以西是没有树木的苔原，行人可以走上几天都遇不到一个地标，一排石头却可以冒充一队猎人。驯鹿围猎时，一排排石堆横列在山谷里，像一列站着的人，有时还缀上草皮和羽毛，风一吹便晃动。迁徙的鹿群把石头当成人，朝猎人要的方向转去，撞上埋伏在陆上的弓箭手，或在渡口等着的皮艇猎手。

因努伊特石堆（inuksuk）一词由 inuk（「人」）和 -suk（「替代」）拼成，意思是「充当人的东西」。最简单的石堆只是一块竖立的石头，复杂的由数块石头精心垒起，有时高达六七英尺，常由整个营地一起动手。它们标出冰面和旷野上的安全路线、湖上的捕鱼处、营地和藏肉的窖穴。1444年时，这已是一种古老却仍在使用的办法。巴芬岛伊努克索角约一百座石堆组成的石阵，最早的可能建于两千年前；不毛之地上的阿希亚尔米尤特游群则继续堆着自己的石堆。

en:
Sakurai Genbei, the master carpenter of Ikeda Terumasa, is said to have judged the finished keep to lean a little to the southeast. He climbed to the top and threw himself off with a chisel clenched in his teeth.

The keep stands on Himeyama, a 45.6-metre hill on the Harima plain where the San'yo road runs west. Ikeda Terumasa rebuilt the keep that Toyotomi Hideyoshi had raised, from the ground up, between 1601 and 1609. The main keep is 46.4 metres tall and joined by covered corridors to three smaller keeps; from outside it shows five storeys, but it holds six floors over a basement. The ground floor, spread with more than 330 tatami mats, was called the thousand-mat room, and its racks could hold 280 matchlocks and 90 spears. Upstairs are cramped hiding places where defenders waited to cut down anyone who broke in.

The approach was built to kill. Gates, baileys and stone walls twist the road into a spiral, doubling back so that the 130 metres from the Hishi Gate to the keep become 325 metres of steep, narrow passage, once crossed by eighty-four gates. About a thousand loopholes pierce the walls for bows and matchlocks, and thirty-three wells were dug inside the inner moat against a long siege. No army ever came through the maze: the works were finished nine years after Sekigahara, and Himeji was never assaulted.

The castle keeps ghosts as well as walls. Okiku's Well belongs to the Banshu Sarayashiki tale: the maidservant Okiku was falsely accused of losing dishes from a precious set, killed and thrown down the shaft, and at night her voice counts the plates from the water. The keep is said to belong to Osakabehime, who wears twelve-layered robes, reads men's thoughts and never shows herself. In another tale Hideyoshi ran short of stone in 1581 until an old widow gave him her own millstone; neighbours followed her lead, and her Ubagaishi is set in a castle wall.
zh:
据说，池田辉政的大工樱井源兵卫认定落成的天守微微向东南倾斜，便爬上天守顶，衔着凿子跳了下去。

天守立在姬山上，山高45.6米，山下就是山阳道西去的播磨平原。丰臣秀吉修过的天守，由池田辉政在1601至1609年间完全重建。大天守高46.4米，以带顶走廊与三座小天守相连：外观五层，内部实为六层加一层地下室。底层铺三百三十多张榻榻米，号称千叠敷，武具架可放二百八十支铁炮、九十杆长枪。楼上有逼仄的武者隐，守军藏在里面，专等破入者进来时杀出。

攻城之路被设计成杀局。门、曲轮和石墙把道路拧成螺旋，几度折回，从菱门到天守直线只有130米，实际要走325米又陡又窄的路，沿途原有八十四座门。墙上开着约一千个狭间，供弓箭和铁炮射击，内壕之内挖了三十三口水井，以备长期围困。但从来没有军队闯过这座迷宫：工程完工时距关原之战才九年，姬路城终未遭到进攻。

姬路城不仅留下城墙，也留下鬼怪。阿菊井的故事出自《播州皿屋敷》：侍女阿菊被诬弄丢了一套贵重盘子，被杀后投入井中，夜里井中传出她数盘子的声音。天守则传说是长壁姬的居所，她身着十二单衣，能读人心思，从不现身。另一则故事说，1581年秀吉修城时石材不够，一位老妇献出自己的磨盘，邻里纷纷跟着献石，她那块「姥石」就嵌在一道城墙里。

en:
One emperor of Japan waited twenty-one years for his enthronement because nobody could pay for it. Go-Kashiwabara succeeded his father in 1500, and the ceremony took place only in 1521, when gifts from the Hongan-ji abbot Jitsunyo and the Muromachi bakufu covered the cost. Soon afterwards all court ceremonies were suspended for lack of funds. The rites were held in the Kyoto Imperial Palace, in the Kamigyo district of the city.

The old Heian dairi had stood two kilometres to the west, but it burned so often that from the late twelfth century emperors lived in mansions lent by noble houses. The present grounds were once the Tsuchimikado Higashinotoin, a Fujiwara estate where a Northern Court emperor settled in the fourteenth century and Ashikaga Yoshimitsu later enlarged. Here stood the Shishinden, where emperors were enthroned, the Seiryoden apartments, and just to the north the retired emperor's palace. In 1444 Emperor Go-Hanazono lived here. The Muromachi shogunate was weakening after the murder of Yoshinori, yet emperors were still made in the palace and era names proclaimed there. The Onin War of 1467 wrecked the capital and scattered the court nobles, which brought the imperial house to its lowest point.

Oda Nobunaga and Toyotomi Hideyoshi repaired the palace after taking Kyoto, and the Tokugawa shoguns rebuilt it eight times in the Edo years alone. They also narrowed what an emperor might do. In the Purple Robe Incident of 1627 the shogunate annulled Emperor Go-Mizunoo's grant of purple robes to virtuous monks, and he abdicated two years later. In 1788 the Tenmei fire, the worst in the city's history, burned the palace, Nijo Castle, the shoshidai offices and more than four-fifths of Kyoto. Shogun Tokugawa Ienari paid for the rebuilding, and its halls were modelled on the Heian dairi as reconstructed in the court scholar Uramatsu Kozen's study of the old palace.
zh:
曾有一位日本天皇等了二十一年才举行即位礼，原因是没人出得起这笔钱。后柏原天皇1500年继位，直到1521年，本愿寺法主实如和室町幕府的献金才凑足费用，办成了仪式。不久之后，宫中各项仪式又因财用不足全数停罢。这些典礼都在京都上京的京都皇居里举行。

平安时代的大内里原在其西两公里，因频频失火，12世纪后期起天皇多寄住公家借出的「里内里」。现在这片皇居的基址原为藤原氏的土御门东洞院殿，14世纪北朝天皇在此定居，后来足利义满又加以扩建。境内有举行即位礼的紫宸殿、天皇起居的清凉殿，北面紧邻退位天皇的仙洞御所。1444年，后花园天皇住在这里。室町幕府在足利义教遇刺后日益衰弱，但天皇仍在这座皇居即位，年号仍在这里颁定。1467年应仁之乱摧毁了大半都城，公家四散，皇室跌到谷底。

织田信长、丰臣秀吉入主京都后重修皇居，仅江户时代，德川幕府就把它重建了八次。幕府也在限制天皇的作为：1627年紫衣事件中，幕府宣布后水尾天皇准许高僧穿紫衣的敕令无效，天皇两年后退位。1788年，京都史上最大的火灾天明大火烧毁皇居、二条城、京都所司代和八成以上街市。重建由第十一代将军德川家齐出资，殿舍依照公卿学者浦上固禅《大内裏图考》复原的古大内里形制建造。

en:
In 1776 the small Kishiwada domain spent 84 percent of its whole budget in Edo. That was the price of alternate attendance, under which daimyo spent every other year in the shogun's capital and left their wives and heirs there as hostages when they went home. Toyotomi Hideyoshi had first made lords keep their families near him, and Tokugawa Ieyasu brought the custom to Edo; in 1635 Shogun Iemitsu made it compulsory for the tozama lords. Every domain therefore kept houses in Edo on land granted by the shogunate according to the lord's standing. A large domain kept three: the kami-yashiki, where the lord lodged and his wife and heir stayed; the naka-yashiki for the heir or a retired lord; and the shimo-yashiki, a suburban villa with gardens, rice warehouses and a parade ground. In 1684 the Tosa domain's houses held 3,195 people, 1,683 of them in the upper residence alone. City magistrates had no authority within a yashiki's gates.

The journey was half the burden. A daimyo entered Edo at the head of a retinue whose size was fixed by his domain's rice income; the Kaga house from Kanazawa brought between 2,500 and 4,000 men. Commoners along the road dismounted and knelt as the train passed, and on reaching Edo the lord changed into court dress and paraded his procession again before entering the castle. The march alone cost a domain 5 to 20 percent of its revenue, and the Edo houses together took 50 to 75 percent. One shogunal visit could beggar a great house: in the Genroku years the Kaga domain spent 360,000 ryo on a single reception.

The shimo-yashiki left gardens. At Koishikawa the Mito Tokugawa began the Korakuen in 1629, and Tokugawa Mitsukuni completed it and named it with advice from the Ming scholar Zhu Zhiyu. The Meireki fire of 1657 burned dozens of estates, and in the rebuilding the palaces moved outward onto wider streets cut as firebreaks.
zh:
1776年，小小的岸和田藩把全部支出的百分之八十四花在了江户。这是参勤交代的代价：大名每隔一年要在将军的都城居住，回国时妻儿作为人质留在江户。丰臣秀吉最早要求大名把家眷留在自己身边，德川家康把这套做法搬到江户，1635年三代将军家光明令外样大名必须参勤。各藩因此都在江户设有府邸，宅地由幕府按门第高下拨给。大藩通常有三处：上屋敷是藩主的住处，正室和嫡子也住在这里；中屋敷给嗣子或隐居的前藩主居住；下屋敷在郊外，带园林、藏米的仓廪和练兵场。1684年，土佐藩各处府邸共住三千一百九十五人，仅上屋敷就有一千六百八十三人。町奉行的权限到不了屋敷的大门之内。

旅途本身就是一半的负担。大名带着人数按本藩石高规定的随从进入江户，加贺前田家从金泽出发的行列有两千五百到四千人。沿途的平民要下马跪伏让行列通过，抵达江户后，藩主还要换上礼服，重新整列前往江户城。仅路上花费就占藩收入的百分之五到二十，连同江户府邸的开销则达百分之五十到七十五。将军一次临幸就能让大藩伤筋动骨：元禄年间，加贺藩为一次接待花了三十六万两。

下屋敷留下的是园林。水户德川家从1629年起在小石川营建后乐园，德川光国在明朝遗臣朱舜水指点下完工并命名。1657年明历大火烧毁数十处藩邸，重建时各府迁到更开阔、辟有防火空地的街道上。

en:
The ninth-century Tale of the Bamboo Cutter plays on the name of Fuji. Its heroine, Kaguya-hime, leaves an elixir of immortality; it is carried up the highest mountain in the land and burned, and from fushi, 'undying', the peak is named. The mountain is a lone cone 3,776 metres high, snow-capped for nearly half the year. The early court feared its fire. After an eruption in 781 it founded Sengen shrines to quiet the kami Konohanasakuya-hime, and pilgrims purified themselves at the head shrine in Fujinomiya before the climb. Only Shugendo ascetics reached the summit, and women were barred. After the great Jogan eruption of 864 the mountain went quiet, and in 1444 it had known no eruption for almost six centuries.

In the Sengoku age the ascetic Kakugyo practised austerities in a cave near Fujinomiya and began the faith later called Fuji-ko. A teacher of his line, Jikigyo Miroku, brought it to the townspeople of Edo and in 1733 fasted to death on the mountain. By the later eighteenth century Edo was said to hold eight hundred and eight confraternities with eighty thousand members, and the oshi guides of the Yoshida approach lodged their climbing parties. People too old or infirm to climb, and all women, climbed fujizuka instead: ten-foot copies of the mountain with its ten stations, built in Edo itself.

In 1707 a great earthquake struck the Tokai coast, and seven weeks later Fuji split open on its southeast slope. For about a fortnight scoria and ash fell on the lands to the east. Fields and villages were buried, the Odawara domain's records came to more than two thousand dead, and ash settled even on Edo, a hundred kilometres away. The new crater hill was named Hoei-zan. There was no lava flow, and Fuji stayed quiet for the rest of the Edo age.
zh:
9世纪的《竹取物语》拿富士山的名字做文章：辉夜姬留下不死之药，被人带上国中最高的山焚烧，「不死」之音便成了山名。富士山是一座海拔3776米的孤峰，山顶积雪近半年。古代朝廷畏惧它的火：781年喷发之后，朝廷兴建浅间神社安抚山神木花之佐久夜毗卖，登山者先在富士宫的总本宫净身。能登上山顶的只有修验道的修行者，女性则被禁止。864年贞观大喷发之后火山归于沉寂，到1444年，它已将近六百年没有喷发。

战国年间，修行者角行在富士宫附近的洞窟中苦修，开创后来所称的富士讲。其法脉中的食行身禄把信仰带给江户的町人，1733年在山中绝食入定。到18世纪后期，江户号称有八百零八个讲社、八万讲众，吉田口的御师接待登山的信众。年老体弱的人和所有女性不能登山，就爬富士冢：一丈来高、按十站仿造的迷你富士，江户城内就有。

1707年，东海沿海发生大地震，七周后，富士山东南斜面炸开。此后约两周，火山渣和火山灰倾落在东侧，田野和村庄被埋，小田原藩记录的死者超过两千人，连百公里外的江户也落了灰。新喷出的火山丘得名宝永山。这次喷发没有熔岩流出，此后整个江户时代富士山再未喷发。

en:
The Kazan Kremlin is the citadel on the high hill above the Kazanka, the old fortress of the Kazan khans. In the fifteenth century the khan's Ark was girdled by oak walls, perhaps partly of stone, up to nine metres thick, with four gated towers and deep ditches on the landward side, while the muddy Bulak channel covered it from the river. Inside stood the khan's palace and the congregational mosque with the mausoleums of the dead khans. Prince Andrey Kurbsky, who came here with Ivan IV's army, remembered stone palaces and 'exceedingly tall, stone-built mosques' holding the tombs of five khans, and later legend gave the cathedral mosque eight minarets. When the city was stormed in 1552 the imam Kul Sharif, a poet and diplomat who had negotiated the khanate's treaties with Moscow, led his students in defending the khan's palace and was killed in the fighting.

The leaning Söyembikä Tower is the hardest part of the Kremlin to date. The brickwork probably belongs to the turn of the eighteenth century, but legend says Ivan the Terrible's men raised it in a week and the captive queen Söyembikä threw herself from its top tier, which gave the tower her name. Ivan IV put the Pskov masters Postnik Yakovlev and Ivan Shiryay, the same builders credited with Saint Basil's in Moscow, in charge of the rebuilding. Two hundred Pskov stonemasons raised a new white-walled citadel from the mid-1550s, and the Annunciation Cathedral went up from pale local sandstone, the only sixteenth-century Russian church with six piers and five apses. Five stone buildings of khan date, mosque and mausoleums among them, served as powder stores for more than 150 years before they were pulled down as unsafe. The English envoy Giles Fletcher counted Kazan among the four strongest fortresses of Russia. In July 1774 Pugachev shelled the Kremlin for two days without taking it; after his capture he was held for a while in one of its casemates on his way to execution in Moscow.
zh:
喀山克里姆林宫是卡赞卡河高冈上的城塞，喀山汗国旧日的堡垒。15世纪时，汗的城堡围以厚达九米的橡木城墙，局部可能为石砌，开四座城门塔楼，朝向陆地的一侧深挖壕沟，泥泞的布拉克河汊又从河边遮住城脚。城内有汗的宫殿和聚礼清真寺，寺旁是历代汗的陵墓。随伊凡四世大军到此的安德烈·库尔布斯基后来回忆，山上有石造宫殿和「极高的石砌清真寺」，寺中安葬着五位故汗；后世传说那座主清真寺有八座宣礼塔。1552年城破之际，曾代表汗国与莫斯科谈判订约的伊玛目、诗人库尔·谢里夫率学生死守汗宫，战死在宫中。

倾斜的苏尤姆别卡塔是整座城塞里最难断代的部分。砖构多半属于17世纪末18世纪初，传说却讲伊凡雷帝的工匠七天将它建成，被俘的王后苏尤姆别卡从最高一层纵身跳下，塔也因此得名。伊凡四世命普斯科夫匠师波斯特尼克·雅科夫列夫和伊凡·希里亚伊主持重建，据说莫斯科圣瓦西里大教堂也出自这两人之手。两百名普斯科夫石匠从16世纪50年代中期筑起新的白墙城塞，圣母领报大堂用当地浅色砂岩砌成，六柱五后殿的形制在16世纪俄罗斯教堂中仅此一例。汗时代留下的五座石建筑，包括清真寺和陵墓，被充作火药库一百五十多年，终因倾危拆毁。英国使节贾尔斯·弗莱切把喀山列为俄国四座最坚固的要塞之一。1774年7月，普加乔夫炮轰克里姆林宫两天未能攻下；他被俘后，曾在这座城堡的囚室里关押过一阵，再被押往莫斯科处决。

en:
Unlike the universities of Europe, Sankore had no lecture halls, registers or diplomas. It was a web of private masters: a student attached himself to one sheikh for up to ten years, read in the master's house or in the open courtyard, paid in coin or goods and often earned his keep by copying manuscripts. Sankore is the mosque of the quarter of that name in northern Timbuktu, a word that means 'white masters' in Songhai, after the light-skinned Sanhaja Berber merchants who lived there. A mosque first went up under Mansa Musa in the 1320s, and the English account credits a wealthy Tuareg woman of the Aghlal tribe with paying for the building raised in the fourteenth or early fifteenth century. It is built entirely of clay and palm timber in the Sahelian manner, and its open courtyard served as the classroom. In 1578 the chief qadi of Timbuktu, al-Aqib ibn Mahmud ibn Umar, returned from the pilgrimage, pulled down the old sanctuary and rebuilt the courtyard to the exact measurements of the Kaaba in Mecca.

Books were the dearest merchandise in Timbuktu, caravaned across the desert from North Africa. When Leo Africanus visited in 1526 he found that manuscripts fetched more than any other merchandise, that the learned were maintained at the king's expense, and that the richest masters kept libraries of more than a thousand volumes. In the sixteenth century the city held 150 to 180 Qur'anic schools for four to nine thousand boys, and some two or three hundred students went on to grammar, Maliki law, astronomy and history, receiving a turban at each of the four grades. Ahmad Baba, the foremost of the Sankore masters, wrote more than forty books, including a biographical dictionary of Maliki scholars read across the Maghreb. The Moroccan conquest of 1591 ended the school. Its teachers were carried off to Marrakesh on charges of sedition with their libraries, Ahmad Baba alone losing 1,600 volumes; he returned years later, but the courtyard never taught on its old scale again.
zh:
和欧洲的大学不同，桑科雷没有讲堂、学籍和文凭，它是一张私人师徒织成的网：学生跟定一位谢赫，长则十年，在老师家中或露天庭院里读书，学费以钱或货物支付，还常靠抄书糊口。桑科雷大学是廷巴克图北部桑科雷区的清真寺；「桑科雷」在桑海语中意为「白主人」，得名于住在此区的浅肤色桑哈贾柏柏尔商人。曼萨·穆萨在位时的1320年代，这里首建清真寺；英文记载则把14世纪或15世纪初的营建归于阿格拉勒部落一位富有的图阿雷格妇人，是她出资修成。寺体通体为黏土和棕榈木，是萨赫勒做法，露天庭院就是讲学的课堂。1578年，廷巴克图首席卡迪阿基卜·伊本·马哈茂德·伊本·欧麦尔朝觐归来，拆毁旧礼拜殿，照麦加天房的精确尺寸重建庭院。

书是廷巴克图最贵重的商货，从北非随商队越沙漠而来。1526年利奥·阿非利加努斯到访时，见到手写本卖得比任何其他商货都贵，学者由国王出钱供养，最富的教师藏书千卷以上。16世纪，城中有150到180所古兰经学校，学童四千到九千人，另有两三百名学生深造，攻读文法、马立克教法、天文和历史，四级学业各授一种头巾。桑科雷众学者之首艾哈迈德·巴巴著书四十余种，其中一部马立克派学者传记辞典风行整个马格里布。1591年摩洛哥的征服断送了这所学府：教师们以煽乱罪名被押往马拉喀什，藏书随行，仅艾哈迈德·巴巴一人就失去一千六百卷；他多年后才归来，庭院里的讲学却再没有恢复到旧日的规模。

en:
Every year the whole of Djenné turns out to plaster its mosque. For days beforehand boys stir plaster curing in pits; on the day the men race to carry the first load to the walls, climb the bundles of rodier palm driven into the masonry as permanent scaffolding, and smear on the fresh coat while the masons' guild directs the work, elders watch from the seats of honour in the market square, and women and girls bring the water. Mud survives only while a whole city tends it. The Great Mosque of Djenné is the Friday mosque of this river market city in the Inland Niger Delta, filling one side of the square. A mosque has stood on this ground since the thirteenth century, and Askia Muhammad of Songhai rebuilt it at the end of the fifteenth. It is banco from its foundations to its roof: sun-baked earth bricks laid in mud mortar and coated in a smooth plaster.

Around this mosque worked one of the great Islamic schools of medieval Africa, with thousands of students passing through the madrasas of Djenné to read the Qur'an. Under the Askias its arcades were full of students copying texts while the market traded below the walls. The mosque outlasted the Moroccan conquest of 1591, but the caravans that paid for its upkeep dwindled as trade slipped toward the Atlantic and the Bambara wars closed the roads. The final blow came from the Fulani. When Seku Amadu's jihad took Djenné in 1818, the reformer judged the old mosque too sumptuous, let it fall into ruin, and closed the small mosques of the wards, moving communal prayer to a bare outer court. By 1821 the great towers that had gathered students to Djenné for five centuries stood untended above the market, and the yearly plaster was no longer renewed.
zh:
每年杰内全城出动，给自己的清真寺抹泥。开工前几天，孩子们在坑里搅拌熟化的灰泥；到了正日子，男人们比赛谁先把第一担灰泥送到墙边，再攀上墙里插着的一束束棕榈木棍（它们是现成的永久脚手架），抹上新泥，泥瓦匠公会指挥施工，长者在集市广场的尊位上观看，妇女和女孩负责送水。泥墙只有全城人一起照看才能撑住。杰内大清真寺是这座内尼日尔三角洲河畔商城的聚礼清真寺，占去广场的一侧。13世纪起，这块地上就有清真寺，15世纪末桑海的阿斯基亚·穆罕默德将其重建。整座寺从基到顶全是班科泥作：日晒泥砖以泥浆砌成，外抹光面灰泥。

中世纪非洲最重要的伊斯兰教学府之一就围着这座寺运转，成千上万的学生在杰内的经学院里诵读《古兰经》。阿斯基亚王朝时期，柱廊下满是抄书的学生，墙下就是照常交易的集市。清真寺熬过了1591年摩洛哥人的征服，但供养它的商队越来越少：贸易转向大西洋沿岸，班巴拉战争又截断了道路。最后一击来自富拉尼人。1818年塞库·阿马杜的圣战攻取杰内后，这位改革者嫌旧寺过于奢华，任其倾颓，还封闭了各坊的小寺，把聚礼挪到一处简朴的露天庭院。到1821年，五百年来把学生吸引到杰内的几座大塔无人照管地立在集市上方，一年一度的重抹也不再举行。

en:
The Walls of Benin were never walls of stone. Around Edo, the Oba's capital, workmen dug a deep ditch straight down into the brick-red laterite and piled the spoil into a rampart on the city side; from the bottom of the ditch to the crest of the bank measured as much as seventeen metres. Tradition puts the first digging under Oba Oguola. Oba Ewuare had the works deepened and rebuilt after he took the throne in 1440, and the inner ring around the palace city was complete around 1460. Beyond it, smaller ditches and banks ran out through the farmland, ringing outlying towns and villages: survey from the air and on the ground has traced roughly 16,000 kilometres of earthworks across 6,500 square kilometres, every metre cut by hand with iron hoes. One engineering reckoning holds that 5,000 men working ten-hour days could have raised the inner ring in 97 days. In 1444 the gates were shut and watched at night, traders paid toll to enter, and an attacker sliding down the loose steep bank lay exposed to the spears and poisoned arrows of the Oba's soldiers.

European visitors kept measuring the earthwork against the walls they knew. The Portuguese Duarte Pacheco Pereira, who entered Edo four times, wrote in 1508 that the city had no wall at all, only a moat so wide and deep that it needed no other defence. Around 1600 the Dutch captain Dierick Ruiters rode through a gate and saw a very high earthen bulwark and a broad dry ditch full of tall trees. Olfert Dapper, drawing on Dutch seamen's reports, described gates eight or nine feet high cut from one whole timber and turning on a single central pin. In 1787 the French officer Legroing noted the vestiges of an old earthen wall and added that he had not seen a single stone on the whole road up from the coast.
zh:
贝宁城墙从来不是石墙。在奥巴的都城埃多四周，工匠在砖红色的红土层里笔直向下挖出深壕，再把掘出的泥土堆在靠城一侧夯成堤垒；从壕底到垒顶最高达十七米。相传最早的壕沟始挖于奥巴·奥古拉时。奥巴·埃瓦雷1440年即位后将其加深重建，拱卫宫城的内圈约在1460年完工。内圈之外，较小的壕垒穿过农田向外延伸，环护着郊外的城镇和村落：航拍与实地勘测已追索到约一万六千公里的壕垒，散布在六千五百平方公里土地上，每一米都靠铁锄凭人力挖成。有工程估算认为，五千人每天干十小时，九十七天就能筑起内圈。1444年，城门入夜即闭，有人看守，商人入城须纳门税；来攻者一旦滑下松陡的壕坡，便暴露在奥巴士兵的长矛和毒箭之下。

欧洲来客总忍不住拿这座土工和他们熟悉的城墙比较。曾四进埃多的葡萄牙人杜阿尔特·帕切科·佩雷拉1508年写道，此城根本没有墙，只有一条又宽又深的壕沟，凭它便足以自守。约1600年，荷兰船长迪里克·勒伊特斯骑马过门，见到一道极高的土垒和一条又阔又深的旱壕，壕中长满高树。奥尔弗特·达珀据荷兰水手的见闻写道，城门八九英尺高，用整根木料凿成，只凭中央一根枢轴转动。1787年，法国军官勒格鲁万看到旧土墙的残迹，还补了一句：他从海岸一路上来，连一块石头都没见到。

en:
In 1648 the visitor Giovanni Francesco da Roma wrote that the manikongo's two-storey palace was the only building of its kind in all Kongo. It stood in the kulumbimbi, the royal enclosure of M'banza-Kongo, a walled town on the Mongo dia Kongo, a hill in Mpemba where inland trade routes crossed. The first Portuguese visitors compared its inner city to Évora, and it was possibly the largest town in sub-equatorial Africa. Kongo's own tradition remembered that the hill had been taken: two centuries after Lukeni's conquest, the descendants of the Mwene Kabunga, whose lands lay to the west around a shrine, still challenged it symbolically in an annual celebration.

After the royal conversion of 1491 the enclosure filled with stone buildings, among them private chapels and about twelve churches. The first church went up between May and July 1491 on the order of the newly baptised João I; Portuguese sources call it the first Christian church built south of the Sahara. A count of the 1620s recorded 4,500 baptisms a year in the city and its valleys, a figure that fits 30,000 to 45,000 people living on the mountain. Portuguese traders and Jesuits had lived in the city since the 1550s, and once conspired together to unseat the manikongo Diogo I.

The Jagas burned the church when they took the city in 1570. Álvaro II rebuilt it and in 1596 made it the cathedral of the new diocese of Angola and Congo. The name São Salvador do Congo, first used in Álvaro I's letters, stayed with the mountain from then on. In 1678 the pretender Pedro III's men destroyed the city, leaving the cathedral beside the kings' cemetery a roofless ruin.
zh:
1648年来访的乔瓦尼·弗朗切斯科·达·罗马写道，马尼刚果的两层王宫是全刚果唯一的两层建筑。王宫立在库伦比姆比，也就是姆班扎刚果城的王寨里。这座有城墙的山城建在姆彭巴境内的蒙戈·迪亚·刚果山上，内陆商路在山边交会。最早到来的葡萄牙人觉得光是内城就比得上葡萄牙的埃武拉，这里可能是赤道以南非洲最大的城市。刚果人自己也记得这座山是夺来的：卢肯尼征服此地两个世纪之后，西边卡本加酋长的后裔，仍在每年的庆典上象征性地向王权发起挑战，那里有一处圣所。

1491年王室皈依之后，王寨里立起一片石造建筑，包括私人祈祷堂和约十二座教堂。最早的教堂奉刚受洗的若昂一世之命，建于1491年5月至7月间，葡萄牙资料称它是撒哈拉以南建起的第一座基督教堂。1620年代的教会统计记载，城中及周围谷地每年施洗四千五百人，按这个数字推算，山顶住了三万到四万五千人。葡萄牙商人和耶稣会士自1550年代起住在城中，还曾合谋推翻马尼刚果迪奥戈一世。

1570年雅加人破城，将教堂烧毁。阿尔瓦罗二世重建后，于1596年把它立为新设的安哥拉与刚果教区主座教堂。「刚果圣萨尔瓦多」一名最早出现在阿尔瓦罗一世的书信里，此后一直跟着这座山城。1678年僭位者佩德罗三世的军队摧毁了这座城市，王陵旁边的主座教堂只剩没有屋顶的残垣。

en:
Kalanga oral tradition compresses the whole Torwa dynasty into one man, Chibundule, whose strength lay in a horn-like braid worn on his forehead. Changamire Dombo, it is told, could only beat him by sending his own sister as a wife, who cut the braid while he slept. Chibundule is the praise name of Madabhale, the first ruler of Butua, and means the sounding of the war horn.

Khami grew up in the granite country west of the Zimbabwe Plateau, on the Khami River, as Great Zimbabwe emptied. Around 1450 the gold of the western mines began moving north by the Zambezi route instead of through the old capital, and a Leopard's Kopje chiefdom made Khami its seat: the Kingdom of Butua, ruled by the Torwa dynasty under its mambo, or king. Arab and Portuguese dealers called the country the Mother of Gold; the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid wrote of a king of Butua in 1502, and in 1493 the Torwa court sent the Mwenemutapa 4,000 cattle and gold.

Seven built-up areas housed the royal family along the ridge, commoners the open valley. Each was a circular artificial platform, terraced two to seven metres high and faced with dry-stone walls laid without mortar. The great retaining wall of the Precipice Platform runs sixty-eight metres and stands six metres high, worked over its entire length in a checkerboard of light and dark stone, and the walls of the Hill Complex are decorated in chequer, herringbone and cord courses.

Torwa power ended in a family quarrel. In the 1640s the mambo's brother, married into a house of Swahili-speaking Muslim traders called the Mwenye, drove the king into exile; a Portuguese prazo-holder restored him in 1644 and left a garrison, which withdrew after its commander was killed. Dombo's Rozvi army took Khami around 1683 and never settled it, building Danamombe as their capital instead.
zh:
卡兰加口传把整个托尔瓦王朝压缩成奇本杜莱一个人，他的力量全在额前状如犄角的发辫上。相传昌加米尔·多姆博奈何他不得，最后把自己的姐妹嫁过去，趁他睡时剪去发辫，才把他打败。奇本杜莱是布图阿开国君主马达巴莱的赞美名，意为战号吹响。

卡米城在津巴布韦高原以西的花岗岩地带、卡米河畔，大津巴布韦冷落之时兴起。约1450年，西方金矿的黄金改走赞比西河北线，不再经过旧都，一个豹地文化的酋长国以卡米为都：这就是托尔瓦王朝的曼博（国王）统治的布图阿王国。阿拉伯和葡萄牙商人把这个国家称作「黄金之母」；航海家艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德在1502年记下了「布图阿之王」，1493年托尔瓦朝廷就送给穆韦内穆塔帕四千头牛和大量黄金。

山脊上七片建筑区住着王族，平民住在开阔的谷地里。每片都是圆形人工台地，垒成二至七米高的阶梯，外面用不施灰浆的干砌石墙包边。峭壁台地的大挡土墙长六十八米、高六米，整面墙用深浅两色石块砌成棋盘格；山丘建筑群的墙上饰有棋盘纹、鱼骨纹和绳纹。

托尔瓦的统治结束于一场家族争端。1640年代，曼博之弟娶进说斯瓦希里语的穆斯林商人家族姆文耶，靠岳家把国王赶出国土；一名葡萄牙普拉佐领主1644年派兵送他复位，留下驻军，指挥官被杀后驻军便撤走了。约1683年，多姆博的罗兹维军队攻下卡米，却没有在此定居，而是另建达纳莫姆贝为都。

en:
Kilwa's merchants lined their reception rooms with wall niches for porcelain, Chinese celadon and Arabian glazed ware kept there for display as much as use. The town covered the coral island of Kilwa Kisiwani, a short sail from the Rufiji shore. Traders had lived there since the ninth century in wattle-and-daub houses; the first coral-stone houses went up around 1200, when Sofala's gold began to pass through the sultan's customs, and in its best centuries the town held more than 10,000 people.

The Friday mosque anchored the town. Its northern prayer hall held sixteen bays and was one of the first mosques on the coast built without a courtyard; an inscription dates its minaret to 1269. Early in the fourteenth century Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman added the southern hall with its great dome. Ibn Battuta saw the mosque in 1331 and called it wooden, though excavation has since shown its stone walls long predated his visit. Pots of coins stamped with the name of Ali bin al-Hasan were found inside the masonry, laid in when the walls went up.

On a cliff outside the town stood Husuni Kubwa, the sultan's palace and warehouse, eight thousand square metres of coral stone: an emporium court for handling trade goods, more than a hundred rooms, an octagonal bathing pool, and a broad stair dropping from the cliff to a mosque on the beach. The finest imported celadons were dug up there, among them a Yuan flask from about 1300. Yet the palace was occupied only briefly and abandoned before it was finished, and neither the Kilwa Chronicle nor the Portuguese ever described it. The Gereza, Portuguese in origin, was rebuilt later in the Omani manner. Almeida's men burned the stonetown in July 1505 so thoroughly that its street plan could never be fully recovered.
zh:
基尔瓦城的商人在会客厅的墙上开出壁龛，摆放中国青瓷和阿拉伯釉陶，一半实用，一半炫耀。城建在基尔瓦基西瓦尼这座珊瑚岛上，离鲁菲吉河口海岸只有一船航程。9世纪起岛上便有商人居住，房屋都是枝条灰泥墙；约1200年，索法拉的黄金开始经苏丹的关卡出海，岛上出现头一批珊瑚石房屋，到最富庶的几个世纪，全城已有一万多人。

星期五清真寺是全城的中心。北段礼拜厅有十六个开间，是东非海岸最早不带庭院的清真寺之一，一条铭文把它的宣礼塔年份记为1269年。14世纪初，苏丹哈桑·伊本·苏莱曼增建了带大穹顶的南段大殿。1331年伊本·白图泰到访，说整座寺是木构的，但发掘证明石墙远早于他到访的年代。墙体内还发现成罐的钱币，铸着阿里·本·哈桑的名字，是砌墙时封进去的。

城外悬崖上立着胡苏尼库布瓦宫，苏丹的宫殿兼货栈，八千平方米的珊瑚石建筑：处理商货的贸易大院、百余间房屋、八角浴池，一道宽大石阶从崖顶直下海滩上的清真寺。殿内出土过最精美的进口青瓷，其中有一件约1300年的元代瓷瓶。这座宫殿却只被短暂居住，尚未完工便遭废弃，《基尔瓦编年史》和葡萄牙人的记载都没有提过它。格雷扎堡最初由葡萄牙人所建，后来按阿曼风格重修。1505年7月，阿尔梅达的部下放火烧毁石城，破坏之彻底，使街巷布局再也无法完全复原。

en:
Harar Jugol is the walled old town of the Muslim city on Ethiopia's eastern plateau, from which caravans went down to Zeila and the sea. In 1559 Nur ibn Mujahid, who had married the widow of Ahmad Gragn, came back from Fatagar carrying the head of the Emperor Galawdewos. While he was away, an Ethiopian raid had broken into Harar and killed the last Walashma sultan, Barakat ibn Umar Din; then Oromo riders destroyed his army at Hazalo and wasted the country around the city. He answered by girdling Harar with a rampart of local stone and clay broken by five gates: Assum Bari in the north, Argobba Bari in the east, Suqutat Bari in the southeast, Badro Bari in the south and Asmadin Bari in the west. The five quarters named after them have kept that shape ever since. Refugees crowded inside, and at the worst of the hunger a sa'a, four handfuls, of sorghum sold for twelve gold ashrafi and a cow for more than three hundred. Nur died of plague in 1568, and the wall fixed Harar's bounds for the next two and a half centuries.

Within the gates Harar is the City of Saints: the five quarters pack in 82 mosques, three of them tenth-century foundations, and 102 saints' shrines, the most venerated over the tomb of Abadir Umar ar-Rida, whom tradition brings to the plateau with 405 companions. The Jami mosque stands beside the Ferez Magala market square. Around it are the gey gar, Harari houses of dressed stone in walled compounds, their main rooms fitted with raised earthen benches and wall niches for holding Qur'ans. The dynasty of Ali ibn Da'ud, founded in 1647, ruled this crowded, devout town for two centuries. Emir Abdullah married five of his sons to Oromo women to bind the tribes to peace, sharifs migrated from Mecca to settle, and by 1789 the emirs were striking their own coin.
zh:
哈勒尔要塞古城是埃塞俄比亚东部高原上这座穆斯林城市的带城墙老城，商队从这里下山前往泽拉和海边。1559年，娶了艾哈迈德·格兰遗孀的努尔·伊本·穆贾希德从法塔加尔带回皇帝加拉德沃斯的头颅。他出征在外时，埃塞俄比亚人袭破哈勒尔，杀了瓦拉什马末代苏丹巴拉卡特·伊本·欧麦尔丁；随后奥罗莫骑兵在哈扎洛歼灭他的大军，蹂躏城周乡野。他于是环哈勒尔筑起一道当地石料混黏土的城墙，开五座城门：北为阿苏姆门、东为阿尔戈巴门、东南为苏库塔特门、南为巴德罗门、西为阿斯马丁门；五座城门各领一坊，格局此后不变。难民涌入城内，粮荒最重时，一萨阿（四把之量）高粱卖到十二个阿什拉菲金币，一头牛超过三百。努尔1568年死于瘟疫，此后两个半世纪里，这道墙就是哈勒尔的城界。

城门之内，哈勒尔是「圣徒之城」：五坊之中挤着82座清真寺，其中3座始建于10世纪；另有102座圣徒墓，最受尊崇的是阿巴迪尔·奥马尔·里达之墓，相传他率405位同伴来到高原。聚礼清真寺在费雷兹马加拉集市广场旁。四周是盖伊加尔式的哈勒尔民居，院墙以琢石围成，正房设夯土高台坐席，墙上壁龛存放《古兰经》。1647年阿里·伊本·达乌德建立的王朝统治这座拥挤而虔诚的城达两百年：埃米尔阿卜杜拉让五个儿子都娶奥罗莫女子，以此与各部修好；圣裔从麦加迁居于此，到1789年，埃米尔们已在铸造自己的钱币。

en:
Ships trading between the North Sea and the Baltic had to sail round Jutland and through the Sound, paying dues at Kronborg and risking the westerly gales of the Skagerrak. Lübeck found a partial answer on 22 July 1398, when thirty barges carrying the first load of Lüneburg salt reached the town along the new Stecknitz Canal. It was 11.5 kilometres of cut linking the Elbe and Trave rivers, with seventeen wooden locks, and it was only 85 centimetres deep. Salt moved along it for five hundred years, but seagoing ships still had to take the northern passage.

In 1571 Duke Adolf I of Holstein-Gottorp proposed a cut clear across the peninsula, joining a bend of the Eider to the Kiel Fjord, to compete with the Stecknitz Canal for merchant traffic. Christian IV of Denmark took up the plan in the next century, but the quarrels between the duchies and their crown left it on paper. Only after the Treaty of Tsarskoye Selo in 1773 put all the ground along the route in the hands of Christian VII could a canal commission under Heinrich Carl von Schimmelmann begin work. From 1777 to 1784 diggers followed the little Levensau from Holtenau towards the Eider, and six locks lifted ships over a divide seven metres high and down again. The cut was 34 kilometres long, and with the canalised Eider and its lakes the route to Tönning on the North Sea ran 173 kilometres. At 29 metres wide and 3 deep it took vessels of only 300 tonnes, yet until the railway age it was the shortcut every Baltic skipper bound for the Atlantic knew.

The Eider Canal could not pass the iron warships of the later nineteenth century. The present 98-kilometre Kiel Canal, opened in 1895, was cut on a straighter line to the Elbe mouth, taking over part of the old course.
zh:
往来北海与波罗的海的商船，从前必须绕过日德兰半岛、取道厄勒海峡，在克隆堡缴纳海峡税，还要冒斯卡格拉克海峡上西风的风险。吕贝克在1398年7月22日找到半截办法：三十艘驳船载着吕讷堡的第一批盐，沿新开的施泰克尼茨运河驶进了城。这条运河的人工河段长11.5公里，沟通易北河与特拉沃河，有十七座木闸，水深只有85厘米。盐在上面运了五百年，海船却仍旧得绕行北方水路。

1571年，荷尔斯泰因-戈托普公爵阿道夫一世提出开一条横穿半岛的水道，把艾德河的一道河弯与基尔峡湾接通，与施泰克尼茨运河争夺商船。下一个世纪，丹麦国王克里斯蒂安四世重提此议，但各公国与王室长期争斗，工程只停在纸上。直到1773年《皇村条约》把沿线土地全部交到克里斯蒂安七世手中，由海因里希·卡尔·冯·席梅尔曼主持的运河委员会才得以动工。1777至1784年，挖掘者沿莱文绍小河从霍尔腾瑙向艾德河推进，六座船闸把船只抬过七米高的分水岭再放下来。人工段长34公里，加上渠化的艾德河及沿途湖泊，到北海边滕宁的全程有173公里。河宽29米、水深3米，只能通过三百吨的船，但在铁路时代之前，这是每个要驶往大西洋的波罗的海船长都认得的近路。

艾德运河过不了19世纪后期的铁甲军舰。1895年通航的新基尔运河长98公里，取更直的路线一直挖到易北河口，沿用了旧河道的一部分。

en:
The floors of the chief halls of the Forbidden City were paved with golden bricks fired in the Suzhou kilns, polished until they rang like metal. Yongle's builders began the palace in 1406 and finished it in 1420, copying the plan of the old palace at Nanjing on a larger scale. More than a million men worked on it for fourteen years: whole logs of golden-thread nanmu were felled in the jungles of the southwest and floated north, and marble blocks came from quarries west of Beijing. The carpenter Kuai Xiang and the mason Lu Xiang led the workshops.

What rose was a rectangular city 961 metres by 753, ringed by ten-metre walls and a moat fifty-nine metres wide. The corner towers were so intricately jointed that Beijingers counted them as nine beams, eighteen pillars and seventy-two ridges. Through the Meridian Gate lay the outer court of three great halls, used for coronations and new-year audiences; beyond it stood the inner court, where the emperor and his consorts lived. The name joined the Purple Subtle Enclosure of the celestial pole to the word for forbidden, and unauthorised entry carried immediate death; tradition numbers the rooms at 9,999.

The halls burned within months of opening: lightning in 1421 destroyed the three main halls. Fires in 1557 and 1597 took them again, and the second rebuilding lasted three decades. When Li Zicheng withdrew from Beijing in 1644 he fired the palace, and only the Wuying Hall, a few lesser halls, the corner towers and one gate escaped. The boy Shunzhi was enthroned there that October, and Dorgon worked from the surviving Wuying Hall. The Qing renamed the great halls for harmony rather than supremacy, hung Manchu-Chinese nameplates and added shamanist shrines. The halls were rebuilt by 1695, and the Qing held their great state ceremonies in them through the eighteenth century.
zh:
紫禁城主要大殿的地面铺着苏州官窑烧成的「金砖」，打磨得叩之如金属有声。永乐帝的工匠1406年动工，1420年落成，以南京故宫为蓝本，规制更大。一百多万人修了十四年：西南丛林里伐下整根的金丝楠木，顺水运往北方，北京以西的采石场开出大块大理石。木工蒯祥、石工陆祥领衔做工。

建成的是一座九百六十一米长、七百五十三米宽的矩形之城，十米高墙环绕，墙外是五十九米宽的护城河。四角角楼构件繁复，北京人数出「九梁十八柱七十二条脊」。进午门是外朝三大殿，登基、元旦朝会等国家大典在此举行；再往里是内廷，皇帝与后妃居住。城名取紫微垣的「紫」与禁地的「禁」，擅入者立即处死；相传城内共有房屋九千九百九十九间。

大殿启用不过几个月便遭火灾：1421年雷击新宫，三大殿尽毁。1557年和1597年两场大火又把它们烧掉，后一次重建拖了三十年。1644年李自成撤出北京时纵火焚宫，只有武英殿、几座小殿、四角角楼和皇极门幸免。同年十月幼帝顺治在此登基，多尔衮在幸存的武英殿处理政务。清朝把大殿改名，突出「和」而非极，挂上满汉双语匾额，又添了萨满教神堂。殿宇到1695年修齐，整个18世纪，清朝的国家大典礼仍在三大殿举行。

en:
Nanjing was never on the Grand Canal's trunk route, and the grain it ate reached it by side canals cut for the purpose. In 1393 Zhu Yuanzhang ordered the Rouge Canal dug through the rocky hills southwest of the city, seven and a half kilometres from Shijiu Lake down to the Qinhuai, to link the Taihu water system to Nanjing's grain traffic. Where the cut ran into a stone ridge the workmen did not hew all the rock away. They left two spans of living stone standing across the water, the Heaven-Made Bridges. The northern bridge collapsed in 1571.

The first such canal was far older. In 245 Sun Quan, lord of Wu, had the Pogang Canal cut from Jurong to Danyang with twelve weirs along it, so that grain boats from Wu and Kuaiji could reach his capital at Jianye without crossing the Yangtze down at Jingkou. These are the earliest canal weirs recorded in China: ramps up which trackers, later often oxen, hauled the boats on ropes, with every vessel paying a toll. His engineers also cut a city canal, the Yundu, running supplies straight to the granary behind the Taichu Palace. In 1444 the tribute grain and the silk of Nanjing's looms still travelled these cuts into the Yangtze and downstream to Jingkou, to join the Grand Canal for Beijing.
zh:
大运河南京段不在运河干道上，它吃的漕粮靠专门开凿的支河运来。1393年，朱元璋下令凿通城西南的石质丘陵，开出胭脂河，从石臼湖北通秦淮河，全长7.5公里，把太湖水系和南京的漕运连了起来。河道撞上一道石脊时，工匠没有把岩石全部挖断，留下两座整块原生石凿成的天生桥横跨水上。北桥在1571年崩塌。

这类河渠的先例要早得多。245年，吴主孙权下令开凿破岗渎，从句容到云阳（今丹阳），沿途设了十二道埭，吴郡、会稽的粮船可以不经京口横渡长江，直达都城建业。这是中国文献里最早的堰埭记录：船只靠纤绳沿斜坡拖过坝，后来多用水牛，过关的船都要纳税。孙权的工匠还开凿了城内的运渎，把物资直接运到太初宫后的仓城。1444年前后，南京的漕粮和城里织出的丝绸，仍经这些河渠进入长江，顺流至京口转入大运河，运往北京。

en:
The pagoda of the Great Bao'en Temple was nine storeys of white glazed brick, 78.2 metres high, and it could be picked out from the Yangtze dozens of li away. It stood behind the temple halls outside Nanjing's Jubao Gate, on a site holy since the third century, when the monk Kang Senghui is said to have brought Buddhist relics here and Sun Quan raised the first Buddhist temple south of the Yangtze for them. After a monk burned the old Tianxi Temple to the ground, the Yongle Emperor ordered it rebuilt in 1412 to palace standards, to repay the grace of his father the Hongwu Emperor and Empress Ma. The work took nineteen years, over a hundred thousand labourers and two and a half million taels. Piles were driven into the ground, charred in place, rammed down with iron-wheeled stones and sealed with cinnabar against damp and insects.

The pagoda was finished in 1428 under Zheng He, the eunuch admiral, who commanded the Nanjing garrison between voyages. Its arch-frames were built of five-coloured glazed tiles moulded with lions, white elephants and flying sheep, and its finial was set with gold and gems. A hundred and fifty-two wind chimes hung at the eaves, and 140 lamps burned every night on 64 jin of oil. Kiln tradition held that every glazed piece was fired in triplicate and two spare sets buried near the city against future repairs. Late in the Jiajing reign fire swept the temple and left only the pagoda, a meditation hall and the kitchen standing.

The tower's fame sailed with the merchants. Johan Nieuhof passed it on the Dutch East India Company embassy of 1655-1657, and the plates in his embassy book taught Europe a 'porcelain tower' of Nanjing, which later readers set among the wonders of the medieval world. In 1801 lightning struck off the top four storeys, and repairs put them back within a few years.
zh:
大报恩寺琉璃塔九层，高78.2米，塔身贴白瓷色琉璃砖，数十里外的长江上也能望见。塔立在南京聚宝门外，殿宇之后，这块地方自3世纪起便是佛地：相传僧人康僧会携舍利来到建康，孙权为他建起建初寺，这是江南最早的佛寺。天禧寺被僧人放火烧得片木无存，1412年，永乐帝下令按皇宫的标准重建，为的是报答父亲朱元璋和母亲孝慈高皇后马氏的恩德。工程历时19年，征调工役十多万人，耗银250万两。地基先钉入木桩，纵火焚成木炭，用铁轮滚石夯实，再铺一层朱砂防潮杀虫。

塔在1428年竣工，由两次下西洋之间留守南京的太监航海家郑和督造。塔的拱门门框用五色琉璃砖砌成，塑着狮子、白象和飞羊，塔刹镶嵌金银珠宝。檐角挂着152个风铃，140盏长明灯夜夜不熄，一夜耗油64斤。窑工中相传，每块琉璃构件都一式烧三份，一份建塔，另两份埋在南京城外备换。嘉靖末年寺中再遭大火，只有塔、禅殿和香积厨存了下来。

塔的名声跟着商船走了出去。约翰·纽霍夫随荷兰东印度公司1655至1657年的使团经过南京，他行纪里的版画让欧洲人知道了这座「南京瓷塔」，后来的读者把它列为中古世界奇观之一。1801年，雷火击毁塔顶四层，几年之内又照原样修复。

en:
At Suzhou the canal's trunk line meets a second web of waterways, cut when the kings of Wu made the city their capital. Streets and canals run in pairs, each lane matched by a water lane, and the stone city map of 1229, the Pingjiang Tu, carries this double grid; it is the oldest surviving city plan in China. South of the walls the canal crosses the mouth of Dantai Lake over the Precious Belt Bridge, 318 metres of stone in 53 arches. The prefect Wang Zhongshu is said to have given his own belt to pay for it, and the bridge took its name from the gift. It carried the towpath, so no solid parapet screened the deck, and the trackers hauled from the bridge itself. Just to the north, Maple Bridge and Hanshan Temple faced the canal. The poet Zhang Ji wrote of the temple's midnight bell reaching a moored boat, and that made this the best-known mooring on the whole canal.

In 825 the poet Bai Juyi, newly appointed prefect, cut the Shantang Canal from the Changmen Gate out to Tiger Hill, seven li long, and laid an embankment along its north bank. In 1444 grain junks bound for Beijing and barges loaded with the city's silk passed through this maze in single file. In the Jiajing reign the monks of Hanshan cast a great bronze bell and put up a bell tower. On his third southern tour, in 1762, the Qianlong Emperor walked the Shantang embankment and wrote the words 'Finding the view at Shantang'. He liked the place well enough that, back in the capital, he had a Suzhou Street built along the back lake of the Summer Palace in its image.
zh:
大运河苏州段上，运河主干道接上另一张水网，那是吴王以苏州为都时开凿的河道。这里街与河并行，每条巷子都有一条水巷相配，这套街河并重的格局刻在1229年的《平江图》石碑上，它是中国现存最早的城市平面图。城南，运河跨过澹台湖口，压着宝带桥：桥长318米、共53孔。相传刺史王仲舒捐出自己的宝带助成工费，桥因此得名。它是纤道桥，桥面不设挡板，纤夫就在桥上拉纤。再往北，枫桥和寒山寺正对着古运河，张继写下寒山寺夜半钟声传到客船，枫桥便成了整条运河上最出名的夜泊处。
